> शुनं । पर्जन्यः । मधुना । पयःऽभिः । शुनासीरा । शुनं । अस्मासु । धत्तं ॥ ८ ॥

> *śunaṃ | naḥ | phālāḥ | vi | kṛṣaṃtu | bhūmiṃ | śunaṃ | kīnāśāḥ | abhi | yaṃtu | vāhaiḥ |*  
> *śunaṃ | parjanyaḥ | madhunā | payaḥ 'bhiḥ | śunāsīrā | śunaṃ | asmāsu | dhattaṃ ‖ 8 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्या अष्टम्या विनियोगः शुनासीराविमामित्यत्रोक्तः ॥
> नो भूमिं फाला भूमिविदारककाष्ठाः शुनं वि कृषंतु । शुनं यथा भवति
> तथा। कीनाशा बलीवर्दरक्षका वाहैर्बलीवर्दैरभि यंतु । अभिगच्छंतु । शुनं यथा
> भवति तथा । पर्जन्यो मधुना मधुरैः पयोभिरुदकैः सिंचतु । हे शुनासीरा
> इंद्रवायू वाय्वादित्यौ वा शुनं सुखमस्मासु धत्तं । धारयतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The use (viniyoga) of this eighth verse has been stated at *śunāsīrāvimāṃ* (in the verse beginning so). May the ploughshares, the wooden implements that split the earth, plough our land happily, that is, so that it be happy. May the ox-keepers (कीनाशा (*kīnāśā*)) go to their work with the oxen (वाहैः (*vāhaiḥ*)), again happily. May Parjanya sprinkle with sweet waters. O Śunāsīra, Indra and Vāyu, or Vāyu and Āditya, bestow happiness (शुनं (*śunaṃ*)) on us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- भूमिं (*bhūmiṃ*)—field
- फालाः (*phālāḥ*)—ploughs and other implements for ploughing
- शुनं (*śunaṃ*)—happily
- वि कृषंतु (*vi kṛṣaṃtu*)—let them plough
- कीनाशाः (*kīnāśāḥ*)—farmers
- वाहैः (*vāhaiḥ*)—with bulls
- शुनं (*śunaṃ*)—happily
- अभि यंतु (*abhi yaṃtu*)—let them go to their tasks
- पर्जन्यः (*parjanyaḥ*)—Parjanya
- शुनं (*śunaṃ*)—so as to bring happiness
- मधुना (*madhunā*)—sweet
- पयोभिः (*payobhiḥ*)—with waters (let him rain)
- शुनासीरा (*śunāsīrā*)—O Śunāsīra deities
- अस्मासु (*asmāsu*)—in us
- शुनं (*śunaṃ*)—happiness
- धत्तं (*dhattaṃ*)—provide

### Printed p. 643

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let the plough and the other implements of tilling plough happily. Let the farmers go happily to their tasks with their bulls. Let Parjanya rain with sweet waters so as to bring happiness. O Śunāsīra deities, bring us happiness.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May the ploughshares break up our land happily ; may the ploughman go happily with the oxen ; may Parjanya (water the earth) with sweet showers happily : grant Shuna and Shira, prosperity to us.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The use (viniyoga) of this Ṛk has been stated in the Special Topics of the fourth Ṛk of this sūkta.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning समुद्रादूर्मिः (*samudrādūrmiḥ*) has eleven Ṛks (the Kannada says thirteen Ṛks) **NOTE**. It is the thirteenth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. The last verse is in Jagatī, the rest in Triṣṭubh. The deity is any one of Agni, Sūrya, the waters, the cows (their product) and ghee. The seer is Vāmadeva. The Anukramaṇikā says: समुद्रादूर्मिरेकादशाग्नियं जगत्त्यंतं सौर्यं वापं वा गव्यं वा घृतस्तुतिर्वेति (*samudrādūrmirekādaśāgniyaṃ jagattyaṃtaṃ sauryaṃ vāpaṃ vā gavyaṃ vā ghṛtastutirveti*): the eleven verses are addressed to Agni, ending in a Jagatī, or to Sūrya, or to the waters, or to the cows' product, or are a praise of ghee. This sūkta is the ājya-śastra in the Viṣuvat (day), and the sūtra says: समुद्रादूर्मिरित्याज्यं त्यं सुमेषं (*samudrādūrmirityājyaṃ tyaṃ sumeṣaṃ*) (Ā. 8-6). In the Vyūḍha Daśarātra, on the seventh day, this very sūkta is the ājya (-śastra); it is written: अथ छंदोमाः समुद्रादूर्मिरित्याज्यं (*atha chaṃdomāḥ samudrādūrmirityājyaṃ*) (Ā. 8-9). The Kannada anuvāda repeats this and adds that the use is described in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra. The particulars: Maṇḍala 4, Anuvāka 5, Sūkta 58, Aṣṭaka 3, Adhyāya 8, Vargas 10 and 11; Ṛks in the sūkta 11; seer Vāmadeva; deity Agni, or Sūrya, or the waters, or the cows, or ghee; metre: verses 1–10 Triṣṭubh, verse 11 Jagatī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒मु॒द्रादू॒र्मिर्मधु॑मा॒ उदा॑र॒दुपां॒शुना॒ सम॑मृत॒त्वमा॑नट् ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> संमोदंतेऽस्मिन्यजमाना इति ना समुद्रोग्निः पार्थिवः अथवा समुद्भवंत्यापोऽस्मादिति व्युत्पत्ता वैद्युतोऽग्निः । तस्मादूर्मिरूर्मिवदुपर्युपर्युद्भूतो मधुमान्माधुर्योपेतफलसमूह उदारत् ' उद्दच्छति ' अथवा वैद्युतादूर्मुत्पादको रस उदारत् । उद्यूतः । अथवा समुद्रात्समुद्धवणसाधनादादित्यादूर्मि रस उदकलक्षण उदारत् । आदित्याज्जायते वृष्टिरिति श्रुतेः । यद्वा ।
> समुद्रादुक्तव्युत्पत्तेरंतरिक्षादूर्मिरुदकमुदारत् । अथवा समुद्रादुक्तलक्षणाद्गवामूधसः सकाशादूर्मिरुज्वलः क्षीररसः । एतद्कृतपक्षेऽपि समानं । यद्यपि
> धृतं क्षीराज्ञायते तथापि तस्योधस उत्पत्तेरेवमुपचर्यते । शिष्टं वाक्यमग्न्यादिपंचसु पक्षेष्टपि समानं । अंशुना दीप्त्यांशेन नामृतत्वं मोक्षमुपसमानट् । उपेति पूरणः । प्राप्नोति नरः । धृतस्य दीप्तस्य क्षीरद्रव्यरूपस्य वा
> गुह्यं नाम गोपनीयं नमनसाधनं यदस्ति तद्ब्रवीमि । तद्देवानां जिह्वास्वादकजिह्वास्थानीयं भवति । तदेवामृतस्य नाभिर्बंधकं भवति । तदुभयं धृतस्य
> नामेत्यर्थः । एवं सर्वमंत्रेषु तत्तत्पक्षानुसारेण योज्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

ना समुद्रोग्निः पार्थिवः (*nā samudrogniḥ pārthivaḥ*): sacrificers rejoice together in him; thus the "samudra" is the terrestrial Agni. Or, by the derivation that waters arise from it, it is the lightning fire. From it the wave (ऊर्मिः (*ūrmiḥ*)), like a wave, one after another, a sweet (मधुमान् (*madhumān*)) mass of fruits, rose up (उदारत् (*udārat*)). Or, from the lightning-fire the juice that produces the waves rose up. Or, from the "samudra" that is the means of drawing up the sea, namely the sun, the wave, a juice of the nature of water, rose up; for the śruti says: *ādityājjāyate vṛṣṭiḥ* (rain is born from the sun). Or else, by the derivation just given, from "samudra", the firmament, the wave, the water, rose up. Or, from "samudra" in the sense given, the udder of cows, the bright wave, the milk-juice. In the view that it is ghee, it is the same: although ghee is born from milk, it is so described because it arises from the udder. The remaining sentence is the same in all five views (Agni and the rest). By the ray (अंशुना (*aṃśunā*)), the radiant part, man attains (आनट् (*ānaṭ*)) immortality, liberation (उप (*upa*) is a filler). The secret (to be kept) name of the radiant ghee, or of ghee that is a milk substance, which is the means of bowing: I declare it. It becomes the tongue of the gods, the tongue that tastes; it is likewise the navel, the binding, of immortality. Both are the name of ghee. So in all the mantras it is to be construed according to the respective view.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- समुद्रात् (*samudrāt*)—from the aerial fire
- ऊर्मिः (*ūrmiḥ*)—like waves, one after another
- मधुमान् (*madhumān*)—masses of fruits endowed with sweetness
- उदारत् (*udārat*)—arise
- अंशुना (*aṃśunā*)—by the ray of the sun
- अमृतत्वं (*amṛtatvaṃ*)—freedom from death
- समानट् (*samānaṭ*)—(man) obtains
- धृतस्य (*dhṛtasya*)—for the radiant principle of ghee
- गुह्यं (*guhyaṃ*)—secret
- यत् नाम (*yat nāma*)—the name which
- अस्ति (*asti*)—there is (that)
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—of the gods
- जिह्वा (*jihvā*)—also in the form of the tongue
- अमृतस्य (*amṛtasya*)—of ambrosia
- नाभिः (*nābhiḥ*)—is also in the form of the navel

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

From the aerial fire, masses of fruits (waters) endowed with sweetness arise like waves, one after another. By the ray of the sun man obtains freedom from death. The secret name that the radiant principle of ghee has is both the tongue of the gods and the navel of ambrosia.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The sweet water swells up from the firmament: by the (solar) ray (man) obtains immortality : that which is the secret name of clarified butter is the tongue of the gods, the nevel of ambrosia.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

(1) समुद्रात् ऊर्मिः मधुमान् उदारत् (*samudrāt ūrmiḥ madhumān udārat*)—संमोदंतेऽस्मिन्यजमाना इति ना समुद्रोग्निः पार्थिवः (*saṃmodaṃte 'sminyajamānā iti nā samudrogniḥ pārthivaḥ*). In the matter of this sacrificial fire, the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice rejoice; hence "samudra" means the terrestrial fire.
(2) अथवा समुद्रवंत्यापोऽस्मादिति व्युत्पत्ता वैद्युतोऽग्नि (*athavā samudravaṃtyāpo 'smāditi vyutpattā vaidyuto 'gni*). "Samudra" means the firmament (Ni. 2-10). Since from this fire (lightning) in the firmament the waters pour down as rain, "samudra" also means the lightning-fire. From such a lightning-fire (like waves, one upon another) masses of fruits endowed with sweetness, or waters, arise. In the case of the terrestrial fire the meaning is that desired fruits come to the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice like waves, that is, one after another; in the case of the lightning-fire the sense is that the sweet rain-waters pour down wave upon wave, that is, in streams.
(3) अथवा समुद्रात् समुद्रवणसाधनात् आदित्यादूर्मा रस उदकलक्षण उदारत् । आदित्याज्जायते वृष्टिरिति श्रुतेः । (*athavā samudrāt samudravaṇasādhanāt ādityādūrmā rasa udakalakṣaṇa udārat | ādityājjāyate vṛṣṭiriti śruteḥ |*). Or also the sun, whose nature is to attract or drink up the juice, is called "samudra". Here juice may be water or any substance that is in liquid form. Because the sun draws up water from reservoirs by his rays, he is called "samudra". From such a sun rain in the form of water came to be.

### Printed p. 646
(4) यद्वा समुद्रादुक्तव्युत्पत्तेः अंतरिक्षादूर्मिरुदकमुदारत् (*yadvā samudrāduktavyutpatteḥ aṃtarikṣādūrmirudakamudārat*). Since the word "samudra" has the name "firmament", the meaning can also be given that water poured down (as rain).
(5) अथवा समुद्रादुक्तलक्षणात् गवामूधसः सकाशात् ऊर्मिरुज्वलः क्षीररसः । (*athavā samudrāduktalakṣaṇāt gavāmūdhasaḥ sakāśāt ūrmirujvalaḥ kṣīrarasaḥ |*). By the explanation of the word "samudra", "from samudra" can also mean from the udder of the cow. It can also be understood that the bright, that is, excellent milk-juice issues from the cow's udder. And since ghee is produced from milk, it can be said that ghee too is produced from the cow's udder. The main point is that the deities praised in this sūkta may be any one of these five: Agni, Sūrya, the waters, the cows (their product) and ghee. That is, the contents of this sūkta may be applied and interpreted in favour of any of these five deities. Therefore the five kinds of meaning have been set out above. Since the following sentences or Ṛks have a common meaning that suits all of them, it is enough to explain only the main meaning.
On the first sentence of this Ṛk Yāska has given an explanation:
समुद्रादूर्मिर्मधुमा उदारत् । इत्यादित्यमुक्तं मन्यंते । समुद्राद्धेषोऽद्ध्य उदेति च ब्राह्मणं ॥ (*samudrādūrmirmadhumā udārat | ityādityamuktaṃ manyaṃte | samudrāddheṣo 'ddhya udeti ca brāhmaṇaṃ ‖*)
(Ni. 7-18)
Some hold that the word "samudra" in this Ṛk beginning समुद्रादूर्मिः (*samudrādūrmiḥ*) means the sun. To support this they cite the Brāhmaṇa sentence that the sun rises (goes up) from the eastern sea. Besides, if it is to be interpreted as a synonym of Agni, there is a Brāhmaṇa sentence on that point also:
अथापि ब्राह्मणं भवति । अग्निः सर्वा देवता इति । तस्योत्तरा भूयसे निर्वचनाय । इंद्रं मित्रं वरुणमग्निमाहुरथो दिव्यः स सुपर्णो गरुत्मान् । एकं सद्विप्रा बहुधा वदंत्यग्निं यमं मातरिश्वानमाहुः ॥ (*athāpi brāhmaṇaṃ bhavati | agniḥ sarvā devatā iti | tasyottarā bhūyase nirvacanāya | iṃdraṃ mitraṃ varuṇamagnimāhuratho divyaḥ sa suparṇo garutmān | ekaṃ sadviprā bahudhā vadaṃtyagniṃ yamaṃ mātariśvānamāhuḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-864-46) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 647
इममेवाग्निं महांतमात्मानमेकमात्मानं बहुधा मेधाविनो वदंतींद्रं मित्रं वरुणमग्निं दिव्यं च गुरुत्मंतं दिव्यो दिविजो गुरुत्मान् गरणवान् गुर्वात्मा महात्मेति वा । यस्तु सूक्तं भजते यस्मै हविर्निरुप्यतेयमेव सोऽग्निः । निपातमेवैते उत्तरे ज्योतिषी एतेन नामधेयेन भजेते (*imamevāgniṃ mahāṃtamātmānamekamātmānaṃ bahudhā medhāvino vadaṃtīṃdraṃ mitraṃ varuṇamagniṃ divyaṃ ca gurutmaṃtaṃ divyo divijo gurutmān garaṇavān gurvātmā mahātmeti vā | yastu sūktaṃ bhajate yasmai havirnirupyateyameva so 'gniḥ | nipātamevaite uttare jyotiṣī etena nāmadheyena bhajete*)
(Ni. 7-18)
The meaning of the above śruti sentence is that Agni is present in the form of all the deities. In the Ṛk beginning इंद्रं मित्रं (*iṃdraṃ mitraṃ*) the meaning is that wise men call Agni by the names of the deities Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Suparṇa, Garutmat, Yama and Mātariśvan. But one should not think here that Agni himself is these deities, that these deities themselves are Agni, that there is no difference between any of them, or that identity between Agni and these deities is stated. अग्निः सर्वाः देवताः (*agniḥ sarvāḥ devatāḥ*) means that the qualities found in all the deities are also found in Agni. Therefore this sentence is used in the sense that Agni is of the nature of all the deities. Agni has a distinction that the other deities do not have. The sūkta in which Agni is praised is addressed to Agni. That is, Agni is not only praised with words of praise; the oblation is also offered into Agni. Therefore the one who accomplishes the offering is Agni. This distinguishing quality is not in the other deities. Besides, it is customary to say that Agni exists in heaven in the form of the sun, in the firmament in the form of the lightning-fire, and on earth in the form of the terrestrial fire. The sun in heaven and the lightning-fire in the firmament are called Agni in name only. The explanation of the meaning is that the terrestrial fire is the true Agni, that is, it is to be understood as the principal (real) nature of Agni.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वयं यजमाना धृतस्य नाम प्र ब्रवाम । स्तुमः । अस्मिन्यज्ञे नमोभिर्नमस्कारैर्हविर्भिर्वा धारयाम च । ब्रह्मा परिवृढो देवः शस्यमानं स्तूयमानमिदमुप शृणुवत् । शृणुयात् । चतुःशृंगः । चत्वारि शृंगाणि देवचतुष्टयरूपाणि
> यस्य सः । आदित्याग्निपक्ष एवं । इतरेष्वपि यास्कोक्तव्युत्पत्त्या शृंगशब्दो
> व्याख्येयः । गौरोऽरुणवर्णस्तादृशो देव एतत्कर्म जगद्वावमीत् । उद्दिरति ।
> निर्वहतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We, the sacrificers, declare (praise) the name of ghee. At this sacrifice we also offer (hold out) it with homages (नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)), or with oblations. Brahmā, the overseer (परिवृढो (*parivṛḍho*)) god, let him listen to this that is being recited, being praised. चतुःशृंगः (*catuḥśṛṃgaḥ*): he who has four horns in the form of four gods; this in the view of the sun and Agni. In the other views too the word "horn" is to be explained by the derivation stated by Yāska. गौरः (*gauraḥ*): the red-hued, such a god, अवमीत् (*avamīt*), brings forth, that is, carries through, this rite or this world.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we, the sacrificers
- धृतस्य (*dhṛtasya*)—of ghee
- नाम (*nāma*)—the name
- प्रब्रवाम (*prabravāma*)—we praise
- अस्मिन् यज्ञे (*asmin yajñe*)—at this sacrifice
- नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)—with homages
- धारयाम (*dhārayāma*)—we offer it
- चतुःशृंगः (*catuḥśṛṃgaḥ*)—possessing four horns (knowing the four Vedas)
- ब्रह्मा (*brahmā*)—the god Brahmā
- शस्यमानं (*śasyamānaṃ*)—this hymn that is being recited
- उप शृणवत् (*upa śṛṇavat*)—let him listen attentively
- गौरः (*gauraḥ*)—the god of red hue
- एतत् (*etat*)—this rite
- अवमीत् (*avamīt*)—carries through

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We, the performers of the sacrifice, praise the sacred name of ghee, and we offer it at this sacrifice with homages. Let Brahmā, who has four horns (who knows the four Vedas), listen attentively to this praise that is being recited. The god of red hue carries through this rite.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We celebrate the name of Ghrita at this sacrifice, we offer it with adoration : may the four-horned Brahma listen to its being glorified : the fair-complexined deity perfects this rite.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

चतुःशृंगः ब्रह्मा (*catuḥśṛṃgaḥ brahmā*)—here "four horns" means the four Vedas. "Brahmā" means the ṛtvij (priest). The meaning is the priest called Brahmā, who knows the four Vedas well. In the sacrifice the mantra

### Printed p. 649

and the like in the sacrifice may proceed without omission and in full; and if lapses occur through negligence, to remedy them by expiations and the like and to see that the sacrifice is completed according to rule — this is the duty of the officiating priest called Brahmā.

> *tridhā | baddhaḥ | vṛṣabhaḥ | roravīti | mahaḥ | devaḥ | martyān | ā | viveśa ‖ 3 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यद्यपि सूक्तस्याग्नि सूर्यादिपंचदेवताकत्वात्पंचधायं मंत्रो व्याख्येयस्तथापि निरुक्ताद्युक्तनीत्या यज्ञात्मकाग्नेः सूर्यस्य च प्रकाशकत्वेन तत्परतया
> व्याख्यायते । अस्य यज्ञात्मकस्याग्नेश्वारि शृंगा चत्वारो वेदाः शृंगस्थानीयाः ।
> यद्यप्यापस्तंबेन यज्ञं व्याख्यान्यामः स त्रिभिर्वेदैर्विधीयते । परिभा. १-३ ।
> इत्युक्तं तथाप्याथर्वणस्येतरानपेक्षयैवै काग्नि साध्यानां कृत्स्नकर्मणामभिधायकत्वात्तदपेक्षया चत्वारि शृंगेत्युक्तं। त्रयो अस्य पादाः सवनानि त्रीण्यस्य पादाः।
> प्रवृत्तिसाधनत्वात्पादा इत्युच्यंते । द्वे शीर्षे बह्मौ दनं प्रवर्गश्च । इष्टिसोमप्राधान्येनेदमुक्तं । सप्त हस्तासः सप्त छंदांसि । हस्ता अनुष्ठानस्य मुख्यसाधनं ।
> छंदांस्यपि देवताप्रीणनस्य मुख्यसाधनमिति हस्तव्यवहारः । त्रिधा बद्धो मंत्रकल्पब्राह्मणैस्त्रि प्रकारं बद्धः । बंधनमस्य तन्निष्टाद्यत्वं । वृषभः फलानां वर्षिता
> रोरवीति । भृशं शब्दायते । ऋग्यजुःसामोक्षैः शस्त्रयागस्तुतिरूपैर्होत्राद्युत्पादितैर्ध्वनिभिरसौ रौति । एवं महो देवो मर्त्याना विवेश । मर्त्यार्यजमानैर्निष्पाद्यत्वात्पवेश उपचर्यते ॥ अत्र यास्कश्चत्वारि शृंगेति वेदा वा एत उक्ताः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Although the sūkta has five deities, Agni, Sūrya and the others, so that this mantra ought to be explained in five ways, Sāyaṇa explains it here, following the Nirukta and the rest, as referring to the sacrificial Agni and to Sūrya, because they are what gives light. The four horns of this sacrificial Agni are the four Vedas, which stand in the place of horns. It has indeed been said, in the words quoted from Āpastamba (यद्यप्यापस्तंबेन यज्ञं व्याख्यान्यामः स त्रिभिर्वेदैर्विधीयते (*yadyapyāpastaṃbena yajñaṃ vyākhyānyāmaḥ sa tribhirvedairvidhīyate*), Paribhā. 1-3), that the sacrifice is enjoined by three Vedas; yet the Atharvan Veda, without regard to the others, sets forth all the rites that are accomplished by Agni alone, and in relation to it the "four horns" are spoken of. "Three are his feet": the three savanas are his feet; they are called feet because they are the means of progress. "Two heads": the Brahmaudana and the Pravargya; this is said with regard to the prominence of the iṣṭi and of soma. "Seven hands": the seven metres. The hand is the chief instrument of performance, and the metres are likewise the chief means of pleasing the deities; hence the figure of hands. "Bound threefold": he is bound in three ways by mantra, kalpa and brāhmaṇa; his being bound is his dependence on them **NOTE**. "Bull": the showerer of fruits. "Roars": sounds loudly; he roars with the sounds produced by the hotṛ priests and others, in the Ṛg, Yajus and Sāman, in the form of śastra, yāga and stuti. Thus the great god has "entered mortals"; since he is accomplished by mortal sacrificers, the entering is spoken of figuratively. Here Yāska has said, "By 'four horns' the Vedas are meant" (the sentence continues on the next page).

> नि. १३-७। इत्यादिना निरवोचत् । तदत्रानुसंधेयं ॥ अथ सूर्यपक्षे व्याख्यायते!
> अस्यादित्यस्य चत्वारि शृंगाणि चतुस्रो दिशः । एताः श्रयणार्थत्वाच्छृंगाणीत्युपचर्यंते। त्रयो अस्य पादाः । त्रयो वेदाः पादस्थानीया भवंति गमनसाधनत्वात् ।
> तथा ह्यग्भिः पूर्वाह्ने दिवि देव ईयत इत्युपक्रम्य वेदैरशून्यस्त्रिभिरेति सूर्यः ।
> तै. ब्रा. ३-१२-९-१ । इति हि वेदत्रयेण गतिराम्नाता । द्वे शीर्षे । अहश्च रात्रिश्चेति
> द्वे शिरसी । सप्त हस्तासो अस्य । सप्त रश्मयः षड्विलक्षणा ऋतव एकः साधारण इति वा
> सप्त हस्ता भवंति । त्रिधा बद्धस्त्रिषु स्थानेषु क्षित्यादिष्टग्न्याद्यात्मकत्वेन संबद्धः । ग्रीष्म
> वर्षाहेमंताख्यॆ स्त्रिभिस्त्रेधा बद्दो ना । वृषभो वर्षिता रोरवीति । शब्दं करोति
> वृष्ट्वादिद्वारा। स महो महान् देवो मर्त्याना विवेश तन्नियंतृतया। सूर्य
> आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च । ऋग्वे. १-११५-१ । इति हि श्रुतं॥ एवं त्वबादिपक्षेऽपि योज्यं ।
> शाब्दिकास्तु शब्दब्रह्मपरतया चत्वारि शृंगेति चत्वारि पदजातानि नामाख्याते
> चोपसर्गनिपाताश्चेत्यादिना व्याचक्षते । अपरे त्वपरथा । तत्सर्वमत्र द्रष्टव्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Yāska explained the verse in this way, beginning with चत्वारि शृंगेति (*catvāri śṛṃgeti*) (Ni. 13-7); this is to be consulted here. Now it is explained for the Sun. Of this Āditya the four horns are the four quarters; they are called horns because they are resorts. "Three are his feet": the three Vedas are in the place of feet, being the means of going. For after beginning with the words ऋग्भिः पूर्वाह्ने दिवि देव ईयते (*ṛgbhiḥ pūrvāhne divi deva īyate*) ("with Ṛks in the forenoon the god goes in the sky"), the text says वेदैरशून्यस्त्रिभिरेति सूर्यः (*vedairaśūnyastribhireti sūryaḥ*) (Tai. Brā. 3-12-9-1): the going is thus handed down as accomplished by the three Vedas. "Two heads": day and night are the two heads. "Seven hands": the seven rays; or the six seasons of differing characters and one common season make seven hands. "Bound threefold": bound in three places, earth and the rest, as being of the nature of Agni and the others; or bound threefold by the three called summer, rains and winter. "Bull": the showerer; "roars": makes sound by way of rain and the like. That great god "has entered mortals" as their controller; so it is heard: सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च (*sūrya ātmā jagatastasthuṣaśca*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-115-1). The same is to be applied in the case of the waters and the other deities. The grammarians, however, taking it as referring to Śabda-brahman, explain "four horns" as the four classes of words, beginning with noun and verb, and upasarga and nipāta; others explain otherwise. All that is to be seen here.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्य (*asya*)—to this Agni, who is the sacrifice itself
- चत्वारि शृंगाः (*catvāri śṛṃgāḥ*)—there are four horns (in the form of the Vedas)
- त्रयः पादाः (*trayaḥ pādāḥ*)—there are three feet (in the form of the three savanas)
- द्वे शीर्षे (*dve śīrṣe*)—there are two heads (in the form of the Brahmaudana and the Pravargya)
- अस्य (*asya*)—to this god
- सप्त हस्तासः (*sapta hastāsaḥ*)—there are seven hands (in the form of the seven metres)
- त्रिधा बद्धः (*tridhā baddhaḥ*)—bound in three ways (by mantra, brāhmaṇa and kalpa)
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—this god, the showerer of desires
- रोरवीति (*roravīti*)—makes much sound
- महो देवः (*maho devaḥ*)—this great-souled god
- मर्त्यान् (*martyān*)—all men
- अविवेश (*aviveśa*)—has pervaded

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Agni, who is the sacrifice itself, has four horns in the form of the Vedas, three feet in the form of the three savanas, two heads in the form of the Brahmaudana and the Pravargya, and seven hands in the form of the seven metres. Bound in three ways, by mantra, brāhmaṇa and kalpa, and a showerer of desires, this god makes much sound. This great-souled god has pervaded all men.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Four are his horns ; three are his feet ; his heads are two, his hands are seven : the triple-bound showerer (of benefits) roars aloud : the mighty deity has entered amongst men.

### Printed p. 651

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In explaining this Ṛk the commentator has followed the interpretation given by Yāska. As stated before, the Ṛks of this sūkta ought to be explained with reference to the five deities, Agni, Sūrya and the rest; but, following the view of the Nirukta authors, the meaning will be given in only two ways, with reference to Agni as the sacrifice and to Sūrya. The meaning with reference to the other deities the reader may supply for himself. So saying, the commentator has explained first with reference to Agni as the sacrifice and afterwards with reference to Sūrya. The meaning for the sacrificial Agni has been given by us in the Pratipadārtha part of this Ṛk, and since the Nirukta text is of the same kind, we shall first explain the meaning of Yāska's interpretation of this Ṛk and afterwards the meaning for Sūrya.
चत्वारि शृंगेति वेदा वा एत उक्ताः । त्रयो अस्य पादा इति सवनानि त्रीणि । द्वे शीर्षे प्रायणीयोदयनीये । सप्त हस्तासः सप्त छंदांसि । त्रिधा बद्धस्रेधा बद्धो मंत्रब्राह्मणकल्पैः । वृषभो रोरवीति रोरवणमस्य सवनक्रमेण ऋग्भिर्यजुर्भिः सामभिर्यदेनमृग्भिः शंसंति यजुर्भिर्यजंति सामभिः स्तुवंति महो देव इत्येष हि महान् देवो यद्यज्ञो मर्त्यान् आविवेशेत्येष हि मनुष्यानाविशति यजनाय ॥ (*catvāri śṛṃgeti vedā vā eta uktāḥ | trayo asya pādā iti savanāni trīṇi | dve śīrṣe prāyaṇīyodayanīye | sapta hastāsaḥ sapta chaṃdāṃsi | tridhā baddhasredhā baddho maṃtrabrāhmaṇakalpaiḥ | vṛṣabho roravīti roravaṇamasya savanakrameṇa ṛgbhiryajurbhiḥ sāmabhiryadenamṛgbhiḥ śaṃsaṃti yajurbhiryajaṃti sāmabhiḥ stuvaṃti maho deva ityeṣa hi mahān devo yadyajño martyān āviveśetyeṣa hi manuṣyānāviśati yajanāya ‖*) (Ni. 13-7)
We explain this interpretation together with the commentator's meaning.
चत्वारि शृंगाः (*catvāri śṛṃgāḥ*)—This Agni, the sacrifice, has four horns. Horns here means the Vedas. The four horns are the four Vedas, the Ṛgveda, Yajurveda, Sāmaveda and Atharvaveda.
त्रयो अस्य पादाः (*trayo asya pādāḥ*)—The parts of the sacrifice, that is, the three savana rites performed in the sacrifice in the morning, at midday and in the evening: the morning savana, the midday savana and the third savana. Savana means this: in order to offer soma to the deities and in order that the priests may drink soma, soma creepers are brought to the sacrifice, crushed with stones, the juice pressed out, strained, filled into vessels and consecrated with mantras and the like. Then it is offered in the fire to the several deities, and afterwards drunk. This is called the savana (pressing-out of the juice) rite. This rite takes place on the day of the pressing (sutyā), at the three times, morning, midday and evening. Because these rites are the chief means of the sacrifice, they are here described as the three feet of the sacrifice (or of the sacrificial fire).

### Printed p. 652

द्वे शिर्षे (*dve śirṣe*)—The two rites called Brahmaudana and Pravargya. Yāska explains them as the two rites called Prāyaṇīya and Udayanīya; that is, in the sacrifice the rite called Prāyaṇīyoṣṭi is performed at the beginning and the Udayanīyeṣṭi at the end. These two rites are here called the two heads of the sacrifice.
सप्त हस्तासो अस्य (*sapta hastāso asya*)—The seven kinds of metres, Gāyatrī, Anuṣṭup, Triṣṭup, Bṛhatī, Uṣṇik, Jagatī and Paṅkti, are the seven hands. There is a rule that in the Prātaranuvāka and in reciting the śastra mantras in the sacrifice, the mantras recited to the several deities must be those made up of Ṛks of these seven metres. Here those seven metres are described as the seven hands of the sacrificial fire.
त्रिधा बद्धः (*tridhā baddhaḥ*)—Since the sacrificial rite proceeds subject to the rules laid down in three kinds of texts, called mantra, brāhmaṇa and kalpa, it is said here that this sacrifice is bound by threefold rules. Mantra means the Vedic mantras recited, as occasion requires, by the hotṛ and other priests in each rite of the sacrifice. The meaning indicated in a mantra makes the rite concerned clear; therefore there is a rule that in every rite the mantra that indicates that meaning must be recited (this is explained in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa as rūpasamṛddhi). Brāhmaṇa means: injunctions and explanations such as that such a rite is to be done in this way at such a time, that there is such a reason for doing it in this way, that there is such an ancient story in this matter, and that therefore the rite must be done just so. Kalpa means the sūtras such as the Śrauta-sūtra. Great sages such as Āśvalāyana and Āpastamba have explained well in the Śrauta and other sūtras what mantras are to be said at what time in the sacrifice, how the rites are to be done, and so on. Sacrifices and the like must be conducted accordingly. It is therefore explained here that the sacrificial rite is subject to the sūtras and the like of the three kinds of rule-books, mantra, brāhmaṇa and kalpa.
वृषभो रोरवीति (*vṛṣabho roravīti*)—The word vṛṣabha means फलानां वर्षिता (*phalānāṃ varṣitā*), one who showers desired fruits. The sacrifice supplies the sacrificer abundantly with desired fruits. Such a sacrifice is accompanied by sound, that is, by the sound of mantras; the meaning is that the priests in the sacrifice recite the Vedic mantras with loud voice. At all three savana times the hotṛ and the other priests recite the three Vedas. The priests of the hotṛ group praise the deities with the mantras of the Ṛgveda. The priests of the adhvaryu group carry out the various operations of the sacrifice with the mantras of the Yajurveda. The priests of the udgātṛ group sing, in order to please the deities, with audible Sāma mantras. In this way, by the recitation of the mantras of the three Vedas

### Printed p. 653

the sacrifice has a sweet sound. Therefore the sacrifice is described by the words वृषभो रोरवीति (*vṛṣabho roravīti*).
महो देवः मर्त्यान् आविवेश (*maho devaḥ martyān āviveśa*)—The sacrifice, the great deity, entered, that is, pervaded, the priests, the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice. That is, since human sacrificers perform sacrifices and the like together with the priests, it is described in another manner that the sacrifice has entered men. This is the explanation of the meaning with reference to the sacrificial Agni. Now we give the explanation with reference to Sūrya (Āditya).
Explanation of the meaning with reference to Sūrya
चत्वारि शृंगाणि (*catvāri śṛṃgāṇi*)—चतस्रो दिशः । (*catasro diśaḥ |*) The four quarters are the four horns. There is a Vedic text that these four quarters are the four Vedas:
यचां प्राची महती दिगुच्यते । दक्षिणामाहुर्यजुषामपारां । अथर्वणामंगिरसां प्रतीची । साम्यामुदीची महती दिगुच्यते ॥ (*yacāṃ prācī mahatī digucyate | dakṣiṇāmāhuryajuṣāmapārāṃ | atharvaṇāmaṃgirasāṃ pratīcī | sāmyāmudīcī mahatī digucyate ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 3-12-9-1) **NOTE**
That is, the Ṛgveda has the name of the east quarter, the Yajurveda the south, the Atharvaveda the west, and the Sāmaveda the north.
त्रयो अस्य पादाः (*trayo asya pādāḥ*)—त्रयो वेदाः पादस्थानीया भवंति गमनसाधनत्वात् । (*trayo vedāḥ pādasthānīyā bhavaṃti gamanasādhanatvāt |*) तथा हि—ऋग्भिः पूर्वाह्ने दिवि देवा ईयते इत्युपक्रम्य वेदैरशून्यस्त्रिभिरीति सूर्यः (*tathā hi—ṛgbhiḥ pūrvāhne divi devā īyate ityupakramya vedairaśūnyastribhirīti sūryaḥ*) (Tai. Brā. 3-12-9-1) इति हि वेदत्रयेण गतिराम्नाता । (*iti hi vedatrayeṇa gatirāmnātā |*) For Sūrya the three Vedas, Ṛk, Yajus and Sāman, are like three feet. That is, the meaning is that Sūrya's course proceeds by means of the three Vedas. On this subject:
ऋग्भिः पूर्वाह्ने दिवि देव ईयते । यजुर्वेदे तिष्ठति मध्यॆ अह्नः । सामवेदेनास्तमये महीयते । वेद्यरशून्यस्त्रिभिरेति सूर्यः ॥ (*ṛgbhiḥ pūrvāhne divi deva īyate | yajurvede tiṣṭhati madhyè ahnaḥ | sāmavedenāstamaye mahīyate | vedyaraśūnyastribhireti sūryaḥ ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 3-12-9-1) **NOTE**
Such is the Vedic text. That is, by the power of the Ṛgveda mantras the Sun rises in the forenoon or early morning (in the east) and shines; by the power of the Yajurveda mantras he is at midday in the middle of the sky (overhead); by the power of the Sāmaveda mantras he sets in the evening in the western quarter. The meaning is that in this way the Sun has the power to move by the force of the mantras of the three Vedas. It is for this reason that these three Vedas, which are the means of his movement, are said to stand in the place of feet for Āditya.

### Printed p. 654

द्वे शीर्षे (*dve śīrṣe*)—अहश्च रात्रिश्चेति द्वे शिरसी । (*ahaśca rātriśceti dve śirasī |*) The two times, day and night, are the two heads of Sūrya.
सप्त हस्तासो अस्य (*sapta hastāso asya*)—सप्तरश्मयः षड्विलक्षणा ऋतवः एकः साधारण इति वा सप्त हस्ता भवंति । (*saptaraśmayaḥ ṣaḍvilakṣaṇā ṛtavaḥ ekaḥ sādhāraṇa iti vā sapta hastā bhavaṃti |*) The seven kinds of rays are the seven hands of Sūrya. Or the six seasons, distinguished by various qualities such as heat and cold, together with one season common to all, may make the seven hands. Or it may be said, if one wishes, that the seven horses of Sūrya are the seven hands.
त्रिधा बद्धस्त्रिषु स्थानेषु क्षित्यादिषु आग्न्याद्यात्मकत्वेन संबंधः । ग्रीष्मवर्षा हेमंताख्यैस्त्रिभिस्त्रेधा बद्धो वा ॥ (*tridhā baddhastriṣu sthāneṣu kṣityādiṣu āgnyādyātmakatvena saṃbaṃdhaḥ | grīṣmavarṣā hemaṃtākhyaistribhistredhā baddho vā ‖*) Since he is in the three places, earth, atmosphere and heaven, Sūrya has a threefold connection. Or, since he is the cause of the three chief seasonal conditions, the summer season, the rainy season and the winter season, Sūrya has a threefold connection.
वृषभो वर्षिता रोरवीति शब्दं करोति वृष्ट्यादिद्वारा (*vṛṣabho varṣitā roravīti śabdaṃ karoti vṛṣṭyādidvārā*)—Because Sūrya draws up by his rays the moisture and the like of reservoirs of water and causes it to pour down as rain in the form of clouds, he is called vṛṣabha, that is, one who showers rain. And because there are sounds such as thunder and lightning at the time of rain, he is also said to be making sound (the cause of the sounds).
महो देवो मर्त्यान् आ विवेश (*maho devo martyān ā viveśa*)—स महान् देवो मर्त्यानां नियंतृतया तान् प्रविशति । सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च (*sa mahān devo martyānāṃ niyaṃtṛtayā tān praviśati | sūrya ātmā jagatastasthuṣaśca*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-115. 1) इति हि श्रुतं। (*iti hi śrutaṃ|*) Such a Sūrya of great glory enters the body of all beings as the inner self, in order to impel them. All beings live by Sūrya. That Sūrya is the impeller of the whole class of beings, moving and unmoving, and dwells in them as the inner self, is confirmed by the Vedic text सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च (*sūrya ātmā jagatastasthuṣaśca*).
Such is the explanation of the meaning with reference to Sūrya. In the same way the meaning is to be supplied for the other deities, such as Āpaḥ (the waters). The experts in the science of words (the grammarians) understand the words चत्वारि शृंगा (*catvāri śṛṃgā*), with reference to Śabda-brahman, as the four kinds of words: noun, verb, upasarga and nipāta. Others speak in other ways. Therefore the meaning must be made according to each context.
In Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 1, page 401, in explaining the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya introduction, the commentator has explained the meaning of this Ṛk in a slightly different way. It can be seen there.

> *tridhā | hitaṃ | paṇibhiḥ | guhyamānaṃ | gavi | devāsaḥ | ghṛtaṃ | anu | aviṃdan |*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पणिभिरसुरैर्गवि गोषु त्रिधा क्षीरदध्याज्यभेदेन त्रिप्रकारं हितं निहितं
> गुह्यमानं गोपितं धृतं दीप्तं रसरूपं वा द्रव्यं देवासो देवा अन्वविंदन् ।
> अलभंत । तत्रेंद्रं एकं क्षीरं जजान । उदपादयत् । सूर्य एकं जजान ।
> वेनात्कांतिमतोऽग्नेर्गमनवतो वायोर्वैकं धृतं स्वधयान्नेन निमित्तेन
> द्रव्येण वा साधनेन निष्कृतक्षुः । निरपादयन् देवाः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Paṇis, the Asuras, had placed in the cows a substance in three forms (milk, curds and ghee) and kept it hidden. The gods found this ghee, which is either a shining substance or one of the nature of sap. Of the three, Indra produced one, the milk, and Sūrya produced one. The gods fashioned the remaining one out of the radiant Agni, or else out of the moving Vāyu. They did so by means of svadhā, which Sāyaṇa takes as food (as the cause), or as the substance, or as the means.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पणिभिः (*paṇibhiḥ*)—by the Asuras
- गवि (*gavi*)—in the cows
- त्रिधा (*tridhā*)—in three forms (milk, curds, ghee)
- हितं (*hitaṃ*)—placed
- गुह्यमानं (*guhyamānaṃ*)—and hidden
- घृतं (*ghṛtaṃ*)—the ghee
- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—the gods
- अन्वविंदन् (*anvaviṃdan*)—obtained (among them)
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- एकं (*ekaṃ*)—one principle
- जजान (*jajāna*)—produced
- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—Sūrya
- एकं (*ekaṃ*)—another principle
- वेनात् (*venāt*)—from the radiant Agni
- एकं (*ekaṃ*)—the third principle
- स्वधया (*svadhayā*)—for the sake of svadhā
- निष्कृतक्षुः (*niṣkṛtakṣuḥ*)—the gods produced

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods obtained the ghee that the Asuras had placed in the cows in three forms, milk, curds and ghee, and kept hidden. Of these, Indra produced one and Sūrya produced another principle. The gods produced the third principle from the radiant Agni, for the sake of svadhā.

> *etāḥ | arṣaṃti | hṛdyāt | samudrāt | śatavrajāḥ | ripuṇā | na | avacakṣe |*  
> *dhṛtasya | dhārāḥ | abhi | cākaśīmi | hiraṇyayaḥ | vetasaḥ | madhye | āsāṃ ‖ 5 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एता आपो धृतधारा वार्षंति । अधः पतंति । शतव्रजा अपरिमितगतयः सत्यो
> हृद्याद्दृदयंगमात्समुद्रादंतरिक्षाद्रिपुणा जलमोकप्रतिबंधकारिणा शत्रुणा
> वृत्रेण नावचक्षे न अवदर्शनाय यथादृष्टं भवति तथार्षंति । ता धृतस्य धारा
> अभि चाकशीमि । अभिपश्यामि । कुत्रॆति तदुच्यते । हिरण्ययो हिरण्मयो वेतसोऽस्संभवोऽग्निर्वैद्युत आसामपां मध्यॆ वर्तत इति शेषः । अत्र धृतस्य धारा अभि
> चाकशीमीत्यनेन चरमपादेन होमाधारोऽग्निर्वैद्युतोऽग्निरादित्यो वोक्तः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

These waters, in streams of ghee, fall downward. They have countless courses, and they come from the heart-pleasing sea, which is the atmosphere. They move so that Vṛtra, the enemy who obstructs the release of the waters, cannot see them. "I look upon those streams of ghee." Sāyaṇa asks where, and answers: the golden Vetasa, the lightning-fire, abides in the midst of these waters (the verb "abides" is supplied). By the last pāda, "I look upon the streams of ghee", the fire that is the basis of the homa is meant, either the lightning-fire or the fire that is the sun.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हृदात् (*hṛdāt*)—from the heart-pleasing
- समुद्रात् (*samudrāt*)—from the atmosphere
- एताः (*etāḥ*)—these waters
- शतव्रजाः (*śatavrajāḥ*)—having hundreds of courses
- अर्षंति (*arṣaṃti*)—flow (but)
- रिपुणा (*ripuṇā*)—by the obstructing Vṛtra
- न अवचक्षे (*na avacakṣe*)—they are not seen
- धृतस्य (*dhṛtasya*)—of this water
- धाराः (*dhārāḥ*)—the streams
- अभि चाकशीमि (*abhi cākaśīmi*)—I look at all around
- आसां (*āsāṃ*)—of these water-streams
- मध्ये (*madhye*)—in the middle
- हिरण्ययः (*hiraṇyayaḥ*)—of golden form
- वेतसः (*vetasaḥ*)—the lightning-fire (stands)

### Printed p. 657

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

From the heart-pleasing atmosphere the waters flow with hundreds of courses. But they are not seen by Vṛtra, who obstructs their flow. I look at these waters all around. In the midst of these water-streams stands the lightning-fire, of golden form.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)

> धेनाः प्रीणयित्र्यो नद्य इव । अंतर्हृदा मनसा हृदयमध्यगतेन चित्तेन ।

> प्रविशंति तद्वत् । अनेन शैघ्र्यमुक्तं भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Streams of ghee flow together, pour down, upon this Agni. Sāyaṇa asks what they are like and answers: like rivers that are "dhenāḥ", pleasing. They are purified by the mind within the heart, that is, by the mind accompanied by contemplation. These waves of ghee, these saps, go and fall from the ladle upon the fire. They are like deer fleeing from the hunter who hurls his weapon, as those deer enter their lair. By this, swiftness is expressed.

- धृतस्य (*dhṛtasya*)—of the ghee
- एते ऊर्मयः (*ete ūrmayaḥ*)—these streams that are like waves
- अंतर्हृदा (*aṃtarhṛdā*)—lodged in the heart (devotional)
- मनसा (*manasā*)—by the mind
- पूयमानाः (*pūyamānāḥ*)—being purified
- धेनाः (*dhenāḥ*)—satisfying
- सरितः न (*saritaḥ na*)—like rivers
- सम्यक् (*samyak*)—fully
- स्रवंति (*sravaṃti*)—flow
- क्षिपणोः (*kṣipaṇoḥ*)—from the hunter
- ईषमाणाः (*īṣamāṇāḥ*)—escaping and running
- मृगा इव (*mṛgā iva*)—like deer (as deer swiftly enter a thicket)
- अर्षंति (*arṣaṃti*)—enter (the fire)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

These streams of ghee, like waves, are purified by the mind lodged in the heart, that is, a devout mind. They flow fully, like satisfying streams. As deer that have escaped the hunter and run swiftly enter a thicket, so these enter the fire.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
They flow uninterruptedly like pleasing rivers, purified by the mind that is seated in the heart: these streams of Ghi descend (upon the fire), like deer flying from the hunter.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सिंधोः स्यंदमानाया नद्याः सकाशादिवोदकानीव प्राध्वने प्रवणवति देशे
> शूघनास आशुगंत्रः । आशु इति च शु इति च क्षिप्रनामनी भवत इति निरुक्तं । ६-१ ।
> वातप्रमियो वायुवत्कृष्टवेगा यह्वा महत्यो घृतस्य धाराः पतयंति ।
> गच्छंत्यग्नेरुपरि । घृतमुदकमिति पक्षे सिंधोरिवेत्यत्रेवशब्दोऽनर्थकः । स्यंदनसाधनादंतरिक्षादुक्तलक्षणा घृतधारा उदकधाराः पतयंति । गच्छंति भूमा । किंच
> घृतसंस्कृत्यायः काष्ठा मर्यादाभूतान्परिधीन्भिंदन्नूर्मिभी रसैः पिन्वमानो
> वर्धमानो भवति। उदकमिति पक्षे काष्ठाः क्रांत्वा स्थिता दिशोभिंदन्नूर्मिभिस्तरंगैः
> पिन्वमानो भवति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । अरुषो न वाजी आरोचमानो गर्वेण गमनशीलोऽश्व इव । स यथा भिंदन्निन्वमानश्च भवति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Like waters from a flowing river, the streams of ghee are swift-going in a sloping place. Sāyaṇa quotes the Nirukta: आशु इति च शु इति च क्षिप्रनामनी भवत इति निरुक्तं । (*āśu iti ca śu iti ca kṣipranāmanī bhavata iti niruktaṃ |*) (Ni. 6-1). Being large and as fast as the wind, the streams of ghee go onto the fire. On the view that the ghee is water, the word "iva" in "sindhor iva" is without meaning: from the atmosphere, the instrument of flowing, streams of water of the kind described fall and go to the earth. Further, the stream breaks through the paridhis, which are the boundary-sticks of the ghee-offering, and swells with its waves, that is, with its saps. On the water view, it breaks through the quarters that stand beyond, and swells with its billows. The illustration is a bright, proudly moving horse: as that horse breaks through and swells, so does the stream.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्राध्वने (*prādhvane*)—in a mountain-valley region
- शूघनासः (*śūghanāsaḥ*)—flowing swiftly
- सिंधोः इव (*siṃdhoḥ iva*)—like the current of a river
- यह्वाः (*yahvāḥ*)—of abundant measure
- वातप्रमियः (*vātapramiyaḥ*)—swift like the wind
- धृतस्य धाराः (*dhṛtasya dhārāḥ*)—the streams of ghee
- अरुषः (*aruṣaḥ*)—swift-going
- वाजी न (*vājī na*)—like a horse
- काष्ठाः (*kāṣṭhāḥ*)—the sticks (the paridhis)
- भिंदन् (*bhiṃdan*)—breaking through
- ऊर्मिभिः (*ūrmibhiḥ*)—with saps in the form of waves
- पिन्नमानः (*pinnamānaḥ*)—growing
- पतयंति (*patayaṃti*)—enter the fire

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Like the current of a river rushing swiftly downward in a mountain-valley region, the streams of ghee, abundant in measure and swift like the wind, enter the fire. Like a swift-going horse they break through the paridhis, and they grow with saps in the form of waves.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The streams of Ghi fall copious, swift as the wind, and rapid as the waters of a river down a declivity, breaking through the confining banks, and hurrying on with their waves, like a high-spirited steed.

> अग्निं ।  
> घृ॒तस्य॒ धाराः॑ स॒मिधो॑ नसंत॒ ता जु॑षा॒णो ह॑र्यति जा॒तवे॑दाः ॥ ८ ॥

> *abhi pravaṃta samaneva yoṣāḥ kalyāṇyāgaḥ smayamānāso*  
> *agniṃ |*  
> *ghṛtasya dhārāḥ samidho nasaṃta tā juṣāṇo haryati jātavedāḥ ‖ 8 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> *abhi | pravaṃta | samanāiva | yoṣāḥ | kalyāṇyaḥ | smayamānāsaḥ | agniṃ |*  
> *ghṛtasya | dhārāḥ | saṃidhaḥ | nasaṃta | tāḥ | juṣāṇaḥ | haryati | jātavedāḥ ‖ 8 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> धृतस्य धारा अमुमग्निं समनेव समानमनस्का योषा योषितः पतिमिवाभि
> प्रवंत । अभिनमयंति । निमग्नं कुर्वंति । कीदृश्यस्ताः । कल्याण्यो भद्ररूपाः
> स्मयमानासो हसंत्यः । किंच ताः समिधः सम्यग्दीपयित्र्यः सत्यो नसंत ।
> व्याप्नुवंती । ता एव धारा जुषाणः प्रीयमाणः सेवमानो वायं जातवेदा
> हर्यति । कामयते । धृतशब्दस्योदकमिति पक्षेऽग्निजातवेदःशब्दाभ्यां वैद्युतोऽग्निरादित्यो वा गृह्यते । तं देवमुदकधारा अभि प्रवंत नसंत च । स ताश्च हर्यति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The streams of ghee turn toward and bend down to this Agni, as like-minded women go to their husband, and immerse him. They are auspicious in form and smiling. Moreover, kindling him well, they pervade him. Delighted, and serving those very streams, Jātavedas desires them. On the view that the ghee is water, "Agni" and "Jātavedas" denote the lightning-fire or the sun. The streams of water turn toward and pervade that god, and he desires them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कल्याण्यः (*kalyāṇyaḥ*)—of auspicious nature
- स्मयमानासः (*smayamānāsaḥ*)—smiling-faced
- समनाः (*samanāḥ*)—having a corresponding mind
- योषा इव (*yoṣā iva*)—as wives join their husbands
- धृतस्य धाराः (*dhṛtasya dhārāḥ*)—the streams of ghee
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- अभि प्रवंत (*abhi pravaṃta*)—join (as if listening)
- समिधः (*samidhaḥ*)—making (Agni) blaze
- नसंत (*nasaṃta*)—pervade
- जातवेदाः (*jātavedāḥ*)—Agni, who is Jātavedas
- ताः (*tāḥ*)—those streams
- जुषाणः (*juṣāṇaḥ*)—serving
- हर्यति (*haryati*)—accepts

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As wives, auspicious in form, smiling-faced and of corresponding mind, embrace their husbands, so the streams of ghee join Agni as if embracing him. Making Agni blaze, they pervade him. Agni, who is Jātavedas, serving those streams, accepts them.

### Printed p. 661

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The streams of Ghi incline to Agni as devoted wives, auspicious and smiling, to a husband : they feed (the flame) like fuel, and Jatavedas, propitiated, accepts them.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska has given an explanation of this Ṛk:
अभिनमंत समनस इव योषाः । समनं समननाद्वा संमाननाद्वा । कल्याण्यः स्मयमानासो अग्निमित्यौपमिकं । धृतस्य धारा उदकस्य धाराः समिधो नसंत । नसतिराप्नोतिकर्मा वा नमतिकर्मा वा । ता जुषाणो हर्यति जातवेदाः । हर्यतिः प्रेप्पाकर्मा विहयतीति ॥ (*abhinamaṃta samanasa iva yoṣāḥ | samanaṃ samananādvā saṃmānanādvā | kalyāṇyaḥ smayamānāso agnimityaupamikaṃ | dhṛtasya dhārā udakasya dhārāḥ samidho nasaṃta | nasatirāpnotikarmā vā namatikarmā vā | tā juṣāṇo haryati jātavedāḥ | haryatiḥ preppākarmā vihayatīti ‖*) (Ni. 7-12).
If one man has many wives, all of them show an equal mind (affection) toward their one husband. The word समनं (*samanaṃ*) means "those of one kind of mind". For it is understood that all of them, living in one place, breathe (by inhalation and exhalation) the air of that one place; or else that all of them think in one way (about their one husband). That is, it means: as many women whose minds are fixed on one man behave, so (the streams behave). कल्याण्यः (*kalyāṇyaḥ*) means endowed with beauty and youth and possessed of good qualities; स्मयमानासः (*smayamānāsaḥ*) means those who wear a gentle smile. Here a simile is indicated in regard to Agni. As the many wives of one man are of one mind toward their husband, and, endowed with beauty and youth, of good qualities and smiling (with a faint smile), approach their lord and husband in humility, so the streams of water in the atmosphere descend and approach the lightning fire (or the धृत (*dhṛta*), that is the streams of ājya, at the time of the homa approach the terrestrial fire or sacrificial fire). And they become one with that Agni. The root नसति (*nasati*) has the sense of reaching or bending. Agni (the lightning fire of the middle region, or the terrestrial fire), served by these streams of water or of ghee, obtains delight (satisfaction). The root हर्यति (*haryati*) means to desire to obtain again and again. The sense is that Agni longs for the streams of ghee again and again.

> यत्र॒ सोमः॑ सू॒यते॒ यत्र॑ य॒ज्ञो घृ॒तस्य॒ धारा॑ अ॒भि  ॑
> तत्पवंते ॥ ९ ॥

> *kanyā iva vahatumetavā u aṃjyaṃjānā abhi cākaśīmi |*  
> *yatra somaḥ sūyate yatra yajño ghṛtasya dhārā abhi*  
> *tatpavaṃte ‖ 9 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कन्याः इव । वहतुं । एतवै । ऊं इति । अंजि । अंजानाः । अभि । चाकशीमि ।  
> यत्र । सोमः । सूयते । यत्र । यज्ञः । धृतस्य । धाराः । अभि । तत् । पवंते ॥

> *kanyāḥ iva | vahatuṃ | etavai | ūṃ iti | aṃji | aṃjānāḥ | abhi | cākaśīmi |*  
> *yatra | somaḥ | sūyate | yatra | yajñaḥ | dhṛtasya | dhārāḥ | abhi | tat | pavaṃte ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कन्या इवानूढा बालिका इव । ता यथा वहतुमुद्वाहं प्राप्तमेतवा उ
> एतुं पतिं गंतुमंज्यंजकमाभरणं तेजो वांजाना व्यंजयंत्यः । एवंकुर्वत्यः
> कन्या इव स्वभर्तृभूतमाध्वरं वैद्युतं नाग्निमादित्यं ना वहतुमेतुमंजि व्यंजकं
> तदीयं रूपमंजाना व्यंजयंतीर्घृतस्य धारा अभि चाकशीमि । अभिपश्यामि ।
> फृतेनोदकेन च भौमस्य वैद्युतस्य चाग्नेः प्रज्वलनं प्रसिद्धं । किंच ता धाराः
> सोमः सूयते यत्र यत्र चेतरो यज्ञ स्वायते तत्तं यज्ञ मभिलक्ष्य पवंते ।
> गच्छंति खलु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

कन्या इव (*kanyā iva*) means like unmarried girls. As they, when the time of marriage (वहतुं (*vahatuṃ*)) has come, go to their husband, making themselves manifest (अंजानाः (*aṃjānāḥ*)) by ornament, the anointing substance, or by lustre, so, acting thus like maidens, the streams of ghee manifest the form of the lightning fire, the Āditya or the other, which is their own lord, as they go to him; "I look upon (अभि चाकशीमि (*abhi cākaśīmi*)) those streams of ghee." It is well known that the earthly fire and the lightning fire are kindled by ghee and by water. Moreover, those streams, wherever Soma is pressed and wherever any other sacrifice is performed, flow toward that sacrifice. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वहतुं (*vahatuṃ*)—for the purpose of marriage
- एतवै (*etavai*)—to set out
- अंजि (*aṃji*)—with unguent and ornaments
- अंजानाः (*aṃjānāḥ*)—adorned
- कन्या इव (*kanyā iva*)—attractive like maidens
- घृतस्य धाराः (*ghṛtasya dhārāḥ*)—the streams of ghee
- यत्र (*yatra*)—where
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- सूयते (*sūyate*)—is pressed
- यत्र (*yatra*)—where
- यज्ञः (*yajñaḥ*)—the sacrifice
- तत् (*tat*)—that sacrificial fire
- अभि पवंते (*abhi pavaṃte*)—go and join
- अभि चाकशीमि (*abhi cākaśīmi*)—I meditate on (such streams)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The streams of ghee, attractive like maidens adorned with unguent and ornaments to set out for marriage, go and join the sacrificial fire, wherever Soma is pressed and wherever the sacrifice is performed. I meditate on such streams.

### Printed p. 663

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
I contemplate these streams of Ghi as they flow from where the soma
is effused, where the sacrifice (is solemnized), as maidens decorating
themselves with unguents to go to the bridegroom.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> *abhi | arṣata | sustutiṃ | gavyaṃ | ājiṃ | asmāsu | bhadrā | draviṇāni | dhatta |*  
> *imaṃ | yajñaṃ | nayata | devatā | naḥ | ghṛtasya | dhārāḥ | madhumat | pavaṃte ‖ 10‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मदीया ऋत्विजो गव्यं गोसमूहरूपं गोसंबंधिनं वाजिं
> संघातमभ्यर्षत । अभिगच्छत । अभिगमयत ना सुष्टुतिं शोभनां स्तुतिं । अत्र
> गोशब्देनोदकानि गावो वोच्यंते । तत्संघातोऽभिप्रेतः । अस्मासु यजमानेषु
> भद्रा स्तुत्यानि द्रविणानि धत्त । धारयत । स्तुत्या खलु फलं लप्स्यते । किंच नोऽस्मदीयमिमं यज्ञं देवता अत्र यष्टव्यान्देवान्नयत । प्रापयत । घृतस्य धारा
> मधुमद्यथा तथा पवंते । गच्छंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O my priests, drive toward (अभ्यर्षत (*abhyarṣata*), that is, go to; or cause to go) the fair praise (सुष्टुतिं (*suṣṭutiṃ*)) which is the herd of cows, or concerned with cows (गव्यं आजिं (*gavyaṃ ājiṃ*), an assemblage)." Here by the word गो (*go*) the waters are meant as cows; their assemblage is intended. "Place (धत्त (*dhatta*), that is, bring) in us, the sacrificers, good and praiseworthy riches (भद्रा द्रविणानि (*bhadrā draviṇāni*)); for by praise the fruit will be obtained. And lead this our sacrifice to the gods who are to be worshipped here. The streams of ghee flow sweetly."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (ऎलै ऋत्विक्कुगळे (*èlai ṛtvikkugaḷe*))—O priests
- गव्यं (*gavyaṃ*)—of cows
- आजिं (*ājiṃ*)—(the cause) of the herd
- सुष्टुतिं (*suṣṭutiṃ*)—the excellent praise
- अभ्यर्षत (*abhyarṣata*)—recite
- अस्मासु (*asmāsu*)—in us
- भद्रा (*bhadrā*)—praiseworthy
- द्रविणानि (*draviṇāni*)—riches
- धत्त (*dhatta*)—bring and provide
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- इमं यज्ञं (*imaṃ yajñaṃ*)—this sacrifice
- देवता (*devatā*)—to the venerable gods
- नयत (*nayata*)—lead
- घृतस्य (*ghṛtasya*)—of ghee
- धाराः (*dhārāḥ*)—the currents
- मधुमत् (*madhumat*)—sweetly
- पवंते (*pavaṃte*)—enter (Agni)

### Printed p. 664

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O priests, recite for us the praise that is the cause of a herd of cows. Bring us praiseworthy riches. Lead this our sacrifice to the venerable gods. The currents of ghee enter Agni sweetly.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
(Priests) address the pious praise, (the source) of herds of cattle :
bestow upon us auspicious riches: convey this our sacrifice to the gods,
(whereat) the streams of Ghi with sweetness descend.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> धामंत इत्येषोत्तरसूक्तस्याद्या चाध्यायोत्सर्जनोपाकरणयोर्विनियुक्ते । धामन्ते विश्वमिति प्रतीकमुक्ता तदंते द्वृचाः । आ. गृ. ३-५ । इति
> सूत्रितत्वात् ॥
> ते त्वदीये धामन्थामनि तेजःस्थाने विश्वं भुवनमधि श्रितं । अंतः समुद्रे

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk धामंते (*dhāmaṃte*) and the first Ṛk of the next sūkta are applied in the adhyāyotsarjana and the upākaraṇa rites, since it is laid down in the sūtra धामन्ते विश्वमिति प्रतीकमुक्ता तदंते द्वृचाः (*dhāmante viśvamiti pratīkamuktā tadaṃte dvṛcāḥ*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-5). "In your (ते (*te*)) abode (धामन् (*dhāman*)), the place of radiance, the whole world rests. In the ocean (समुद्रे (*samudre*)) as the submarine fire; within the heart (हृदि अंतः (*hṛdi aṃtaḥ*)) of all living beings as Vaiśvānara; in life (आयुषि (*āyuṣi*)), that is in food, as what is eaten by all beings." Or else: आयुषि (*āyuṣi*) is a qualifier of this (the heart): for life is sustained by the digestive fire. "In the assemblage of the waters (अपामनीके (*apāmanīke*)) as the lightning fire; in battle (समिथे (*samithe*)) in the form of the fire of valour." The (धाम (*dhāma*)) thus present in all places: the wave (*ūrmiḥ*), the essence in the form of ghee or of water, which has been established (आभृतः (*ābhṛtaḥ*)) in that abode of yours — that sweet essence, endowed with sweetness, may we attain (अश्याम (*aśyāma*)). **NOTE**

### Printed p. 665

> अपामनीक उदकसंस्थाये वैद्युताग्नित्वेन समिथे संग्रामे च शौर्याग्निरूपेण।
> एवं सर्वेषु स्थानेषु वर्तमानं धाम । तस्मिन्थामनि य ऊर्मिर्घृतरूप
> उदकरूपो वा रस आभृतः स्थापितः ते त्वदीयं तं रसं मधुमंतं माधुर्योपेतमश्याम । व्याप्नुयाम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(Continuing the same bhāṣya.) In the assemblage of the waters it is present as the lightning fire; in battle as the fire of valour. Thus the abode is present in all places. In that abode the wave (*ūrmiḥ*), the essence in the form of ghee or of water, has been established; that essence of yours, endowed with sweetness, may we attain, that is, pervade.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (ऎलै अग्निये (*èlai agniye*))—O Agni
- अंतः समुद्रे (*aṃtaḥ samudre*)—even though you are in the midst of the ocean in the form of the submarine fire
- हृद्यंतः (*hṛdyaṃtaḥ*)—even though in the depth of the heart in the form of Vaiśvānara
- आयुषि (*āyuṣi*)—even though in the form of food you are like life to all
- अपामनीके (*apāmanīke*)—even though in the water in the form of the lightning fire
- समिधे (*samidhe*)—even though on the field of battle in the form of the fire of valour
- ते (*te*)—your
- धामन् (*dhāman*)—in the place that is of the nature of radiance
- विश्वं भुवनं (*viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ*)—the whole world
- आधि श्रितं (*ādhi śritaṃ*)—finds refuge
- ते (*te*)—your
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which essence, in the form of ghee
- आभृतः (*ābhṛtaḥ*)—is established in you
- तं (*taṃ*)—such
- मधुमंतं (*madhumaṃtaṃ*)—and sweet
- ऊर्मि० (*ūrmi0*)—essence
- अश्याम (*aśyāma*)—may we also attain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, whether you are in the midst of the ocean in the form of the submarine fire, in the depth of the heart in the form of Vaiśvānara, in the form of food, in the form of the digestive fire for all, or in the water in the form of the lightning fire, the whole world finds refuge in your place that is of the nature of radiance. May we also attain that sweet essence of yours, in the form of ghee, which is established in you.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The whole world, (Agni), finds an asylum in your effulgence, whether it be in the ocean, in the heart (of man), in the life (of living beings), in the assemblage of the waters, or in warfare: may we attain that sweet-flavoured wave which is established in your (essence).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This Ṛk धामंते (*dhāmaṃte*) and the Ṛk अबोध्यग्निः (*abodhyagniḥ*), the first Ṛk of the next sūkta, are to be recited and offered as homa when the first and last Ṛks of each maṇḍala are used as the principal oblation in the adhyāyotsarjana and upākaraṇa homas; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana-gṛhya-sūtra, in the sūtra धामंते इति प्रतीकमुक्ता तदंते द्वृचाः (*dhāmaṃte iti pratīkamuktā tadaṃte dvṛcāḥ*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-5-7).
ते धामन् विश्वं भुवनं अधि श्रितं (*te dhāman viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ adhi śritaṃ*)—त्वदीये धामनि तेजःस्थाने विश्वं भुवन अधि श्रितं (*tvadīye dhāmani tejaḥsthāne viśvaṃ bhuvana adhi śritaṃ*). O Agni, in your own place, characterised by radiance, the whole world, that is all the worlds, is established. That is, the sense is that you pervade the entire world with your unique radiance.

### Printed p. 666
समुद्रे हृदि अंतः आयुषि (*samudre hṛdi aṃtaḥ āyuṣi*)—It has been said in the previous sentence that Agni pervades the entire world. How that is so, is explained here in detail. समुद्रे वडवा ग्नित्वेन । हृद्यंतः सर्वप्राणिनां हृदये वैश्वानरत्वेन । आयुषि अन्ने सर्वप्राण्याहारत्वेन यद्वा आयुषीत्येतत् हृद्विशेषणं जठराग्निना खल्वायुः धार्यते । अपा मनीके उदकसंस्कृत्याये वैद्युताग्नित्वेन । समिधे संग्रामे शौर्याग्नित्वरूपेण । (*samudre vaḍavā gnitvena | hṛdyaṃtaḥ sarvaprāṇināṃ hṛdaye vaiśvānaratvena | āyuṣi anne sarvaprāṇyāhāratvena yadvā āyuṣītyetat hṛdviśeṣaṇaṃ jaṭharāgninā khalvāyuḥ dhāryate | apā manīke udakasaṃskṛtyāye vaidyutāgnitvena | samidhe saṃgrāme śauryāgnitvarūpeṇa |*). This Agni pervades various regions in various forms. He is in the ocean in the form of the submarine fire; he is in the heart of living beings in the form of the Vaiśvānara fire. Or else, he is in the belly of living beings, digesting their food and so on, in the form of the digestive fire, and is the cause of the increase of life of living beings. And he is in the assemblage of waters (in the clouds) in the form of the lightning fire (lightning); in battles and the like he is in the form of the fire of valour. Thus in all places Agni pervades everything with his various radiance; that is the sense.
य आभृतस्तमश्याम मधुमंतं ते ऊर्मि० (*ya ābhṛtastamaśyāma madhumaṃtaṃ te ūrmi0*)—तस्मिन् धामनि यः ऊर्मिर्घृतरूप उदकरूपो वा रसः स्थापितः त्वदीयं तं रसं माधुर्योपेतं व्याप्पु याम । (*tasmin dhāmani yaḥ ūrmirghṛtarūpa udakarūpo vā rasaḥ sthāpitaḥ tvadīyaṃ taṃ rasaṃ mādhuryopetaṃ vyāppu yāma |*). O Agni, may we obtain that sweet essence (ghee or water), of the nature of ghee or of the nature of water, which is established in your mass of radiance pervading all places. Here it is stated that the essence is of two kinds, of the nature of ghee or of water. The essence that is established in (joins) the terrestrial fire or the sacrificial fire is to be understood as ghee; the essence that is established in the lightning fire, as water.
The concluding verses of the Fourth Maṇḍala: इत्थं श्रीबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यैकधुरंधरः । विद्यातीर्थगुरोर्दृष्टा प्राप्तसार्वज्ञ्यवैभवः ॥ श्रीमत्सायणमंत्रिशः सकलागमतत्त्ववित् । दाशतय्यां माधवीये वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशने ॥ चतुर्थं मंडलं सम्यक् वामदेवेन वीक्षितं । अष्टोत्तरैस्तु पंचाशत्तूकैः पंच शतैरपि ॥ एकोनया नवत्या च युक्तैर्मंत्रैश्च संमितं । व्याकार्षित्सुखबोधार्थं पश्यतैतद्विमत्सराः ॥ (*itthaṃ śrībukkabhūpālasāmrājyaikadhuraṃdharaḥ | vidyātīrthagurordṛṣṭā prāptasārvajñyavaibhavaḥ ‖ śrīmatsāyaṇamaṃtriśaḥ sakalāgamatattvavit | dāśatayyāṃ mādhavīye vedārthasya prakāśane ‖ caturthaṃ maṃḍalaṃ samyak vāmadevena vīkṣitaṃ | aṣṭottaraistu paṃcāśattūkaiḥ paṃca śatairapi ‖ ekonayā navatyā ca yuktairmaṃtraiśca saṃmitaṃ | vyākārṣitsukhabodhārthaṃ paśyataitadvimatsarāḥ ‖*) ॥ इति चतुर्थं मंडलं समाप्तं ॥ (*‖ iti caturthaṃ maṃḍalaṃ samāptaṃ ‖*)

### Printed p. 667

वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थांश्च तुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ (*vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthāṃśca turo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖*)

Thus ends the Fourth Maṇḍala, in the Ṛksaṃhitā-bhāṣya, in the Vedārthaprakāśa of the school of Mādhava, composed by Sāyaṇācārya, bearer of the burden of the empire of the glorious Vīra Bukka, the king, the supreme lord, the promoter of the Vedic path. ओं शत्स्य (*oṃ śatsya*)

Here ends the fourth maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, together with the bhāṣya of Śrī Sāyaṇa and the Kannada translation.

यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्भवेत्। तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोऽस्तुते ॥ (*yadakṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ tu yadbhavet| tatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namo 'stute ‖*)

शुभं भूयात् (*śubhaṃ bhūyāt*) मंगळं (*maṃgaḷaṃ*)

ओं (*oṃ*) श्रीः (*śrīḥ*) श्री गणाधिपतये नमः (*śrī gaṇādhipataye namaḥ*)

वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे । यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननं ॥ (*vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānāmupakrame | yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syustaṃ namāmi gajānanaṃ ‖*)

यस्य निश्वसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् । निर्ममे तमहं वंदे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरं ॥ (*yasya niśvasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat | nirmame tamahaṃ vaṃde vidyātīrthamaheśvaraṃ ‖*)

वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्यायी सदाशिवः । तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥ (*vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyī sadāśivaḥ | tasmātsarvaprayatnena vedameva sadā japet ‖*)

Ṛgveda-saṃhitā with the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya.

Now the Fifth Maṇḍala. The Fifth Maṇḍala.

## Maṇḍala 5

### Introduction (Piṭhike)

**Introduction to the seer Atri, the seer of the maṇḍala.**

Although Atri is named as the seer of the Fifth Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda, other seers too are the seers of the sūktas of this maṇḍala. It cannot be said that all of these belong to the family of Atri. Sāyaṇa has said: पंचमंडलेनुक्तगोत्रमात्रेयं विद्यादिति परिभाषितत्वादात्रेयौ बुधगविष्ठिरावृषी (*paṃcamaṃḍalenuktagotramātreyaṃ vidyāditi paribhāṣitatvādātreyau budhagaviṣṭhirāvṛṣī*). According to this rule, where some seers who are seers of sūktas in the Fifth Maṇḍala are not stated to belong to any particular gotra, they must be regarded as born in the gotra of Atri. From this point of view he says that the two seers Budha and Gaviṣṭhira, the seers of the first sūkta of this maṇḍala, must also be understood to be of the Atreya family. Therefore all the seers of this maṇḍala

### Printed p. 670

must be connected in one way or another with the family of the seer Atri. Besides, many of the seers of this maṇḍala are also seers of many sūktas of other maṇḍalas.
