#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अबो॑ध्य॒ग्निः स॒मिधा॒ जना॑नां॒ प्रति॑ धे॒नुमि॑वाय॒तीमु॒षासं॑।  
> य॒ह्वा इ॑व॒ प्र व॒यामु॒ज्जिहा॑नाः॒ प्र भा॒नवः॑ सिस्त्रते॒ नाक॒मच्छ॑॥

> *abodhyagniḥ samidhā janānāṃ prati dhenumivāyatīmuṣāsaṃ|*  
> *yahvā iva pra vayāmujjihānāḥ pra bhānavaḥ sistrate nākamaccha‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अबोधि । अग्निः । संइधा । जनानां । प्रति । धेनुंइव । आयतीं । उषसं ।  
> यह्वाःइव । प्र । वयां । उत्जिहानाः । प्र । भानवः । सिस्त्रते । नाकं । अच्छ ॥ १ ॥

> *abodhi | agniḥ | saṃidhā | janānāṃ | prati | dhenuṃiva | āyatīṃ | uṣasaṃ |*  
> *yahvāḥiva | pra | vayāṃ | utjihānāḥ | pra | bhānavaḥ | sistrate | nākaṃ | accha ‖ 1 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयमग्निर्जनानामध्वय्यादीनां समिधा समिद्धिरबोधि । प्रबुद्धोऽभूत् ।
> धेनुमिव । अग्निहोत्रार्थधेनुं प्रति यथा प्रातर्बुध्यते तद्वदायतीमागच्छंतीमुषसं प्रति । उषःकाल इत्यर्थः । अथ प्रबुद्धस्याग्नेर्भानवो ज्वाला यह्वा
> महांतो वयां शाखां प्रोज्जिहानाः प्रोद्गमयंतो वृक्षा इव प्रोज्जिहानाः
> स्वाधिष्ठानं त्यजंतो नाकमंतरिक्षमच्छाभिमुख्येन प्रसिस्रते । प्रसरंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Agni has been awakened (अबोधि (*abodhi*), "has become awake") by the kindling of the people, that is, of the adhvaryus and the others. Just as the cow meant for the agnihotra is awakened in the morning, so he is awakened toward the approaching, advancing Uṣas, that is, at the time of dawn. Then the flames (भानवः (*bhānavaḥ*)) of the awakened Agni, being great (यह्वाः (*yahvāḥ*)), spread forward toward the sky (नाकं (*nākaṃ*)) as trees do which send out their branches (वयां (*vayāṃ*)) upward, leaving their own support. अच्छ (*accha*) is explained as "facing toward".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- जनानां (*janānāṃ*)—of the adhvaryus
- समिधा (*samidhā*)—by the fuel-sticks (having been kindled)
- आयतीं (*āyatīṃ*)—who is appearing
- उषसं प्रति (*uṣasaṃ prati*)—facing the Uṣas
- धेनुमिव (*dhenumiva*)—like a cow that gives delight
- अबोधि (*abodhi*)—has become awake
- भानवः (*bhānavaḥ*)—the flames of this Agni
- यह्वाः (*yahvāḥ*)—being of great form
- वयां (*vayāṃ*)—branches
- प्र उज्जिहाना इव (*pra ujjihānā iva*)—like trees that have thrown out and spread their branches in many directions
- नाकं अच्छ (*nākaṃ accha*)—toward the sky
- प्र सिस्रते (*pra sisrate*)—spread and pervade
### Printed p. 711

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, kindled by the fuel-sticks of the adhvaryus, has awakened facing the appearing Uṣas, like a cow that gives delight. The flames of this Agni, being of great form, spread out and pervade toward the sky, like trees that have thrown out and spread their branches in many directions.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni is awakened by the fuel (supplied by) the priests at the dawn, approaching lika a cow (to pasture): his flames rise up to the sky like stately (trees) throwing aloft their branches.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अग्निः जनानां समिधा आयतीं उषसं प्रति धेनुमिव अबोधि (*agniḥ janānāṃ samidhā āyatīṃ uṣasaṃ prati dhenumiva abodhi*)—अध्वर्य्यादीनां ऋत्विजां समिद्धिः उषःकाले (प्रातःकाले) आगच्छंतीं उषसं प्रति यथा अग्निहोत्रार्थं धेनुः प्रातः प्रबुध्यते तथाप्रबुद्धोऽभूत् । (*adhvaryyādīnāṃ ṛtvijāṃ samiddhiḥ uṣaḥkāle (prātaḥkāle) āgacchaṃtīṃ uṣasaṃ prati yathā agnihotrārthaṃ dhenuḥ prātaḥ prabudhyate tathāprabuddho 'bhūt |*). Because milk is needed for the sacrifice when a sacrifice is performed, it is the custom to wake the sleeping cow in the morning, before the time, and to milk her. In the same way, facing Uṣas, that is, as soon as the time of dawn comes, the priests such as the adhvaryu make the fire burn well for the sacrifice with fuel-sticks and other pieces of wood; this is the intended sense. Just as the cow is awakened in the morning to be milked, so the priests such as the adhvaryu kindle Agni at dawn itself with fuel-sticks and other wood. Thus the meaning is explained by giving the cow as an illustration for Agni.
यह्वाः इव वयां प्र उज्जिहानाः भानवः नाकं अच्छ सिस्रते (*yahvāḥ iva vayāṃ pra ujjihānāḥ bhānavaḥ nākaṃ accha sisrate*)—अथ प्रबुद्धस्याग्नेः ज्वालाः महांतः शाखां प्रोद्गमयंतो वृक्षा इव अंतरिक्षमाभिमुख्यन प्रसरंति ॥ (*atha prabuddhasyāgneḥ jvālāḥ mahāṃtaḥ śākhāṃ prodgamayaṃto vṛkṣā iva aṃtarikṣamābhimukhyana prasaraṃti ‖*). As stated in the preceding sentence, Agni, kindled by the priests, spreads his shining flames, as trees stretch their branches high into the sky; this is the intended sense. Here an illustration is given for the flames of Agni and the branches of a tree. As the branches of a tree pervade the highest region in the sky, so the flames of Agni spread very high; that is, the idea suggested here is that Agni is burning very brilliantly.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं होता होमनिष्पादकोऽग्निर्देवान्यष्टव्यान्यजथाय यष्टुमबोधि । बुध्यते । सोऽग्निः प्रातःकाले सुमनाः शोभनमनस्को यजमानानुग्रहबुद्धिः सन् ऊर्ध्वोऽस्थात् । उत्तिष्ठति । समिद्धस्यास्य रुशद्रोचमानं पाजो
> बलं ज्वालालक्षणमदर्शि । दृश्यते । अथ तथाभूतो महान्देवस्तमसोऽंधकारान्निरमोचि । निर्मुक्तोऽभूत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Agni, the Hotā, the accomplisher of the offering, has been awakened (अबोधि (*abodhi*)) in order to sacrifice to (यजथाय (*yajathāya*), "to sacrifice") the gods who are to be worshipped. That Agni, in the morning, being well-minded (सुमनाः (*sumanāḥ*)), that is, with the intention of favouring the sacrificer, has stood up (ऊर्ध्वोऽस्थात् (*ūrdhvo 'sthāt*), "rises up"). Of this kindled Agni the shining (रुशत् (*ruśat*), radiant) vigour (पाजः (*pājaḥ*), strength), which has the form of flame, has been seen (*adarśi*). Then the great god, so constituted, has been freed (निरमोचि (*niramoci*), "has become released") from the darkness.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- होता (*hotā*)—the accomplisher of the offering
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- सुमनाः (*sumanāḥ*)—having a well-disposed mind
- यजथाय (*yajathāya*)—to sacrifice
- देवान् (*devān*)—addressed to the gods
- अबोधि (*abodhi*)—awakens
- प्रातः (*prātaḥ*)—at the time of dawn
- ऊर्ध्वः अस्थात् (*ūrdhvaḥ asthāt*)—rises upward
- समिद्धस्य (*samiddhasya*)—of this kindled Agni
- रुशत् (*ruśat*)—attractive
- पाजः (*pājaḥ*)—power
- आदर्शि (*ādarśi*)—has become visible to all
- महान् (*mahān*)—the great one
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—of divine nature, Agni
- तमसः (*tamasaḥ*)—from darkness
- निरमोचि (*niramoci*)—has come out, freed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, the accomplisher of the offering, with a well-disposed mind, awakens in order to sacrifice to the gods. At the time of dawn he rises upward. The attractive power of this kindled Agni has become visible to all. Agni, the great one and of divine nature, has come out freed from darkness.
### Printed p. 713

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The offerer of the oblation is awakened for the worship of the gods :
favourably minded, Agni has risen up with the dawn : the radiant vigcur
of the kindld (fire) is manifested ; the great deity has been liberated from
the darkness.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

होता अग्निः देवान् यजथाय अबोधि (*hotā agniḥ devān yajathāya abodhi*)—Agni, the accomplisher of the offering, awakens in the morning in order to invite the gods to the sacrifice and worship them. That is, the intended sense is that in the morning, for the sake of performing the sacrifice and of inviting the gods and offering them the oblation in the sacrificial fire, the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice, or the priests, kindle Agni.
सुमनाः सन् ऊर्ध्वः अस्थात् (*sumanāḥ san ūrdhvaḥ asthāt*)—सोऽग्निः प्रातःकाले शोभनमनस्को यजमानानुग्रहबुद्धिः सन् ऊर्ध्व उत्तिष्ठति । (*so 'gniḥ prātaḥkāle śobhanamanasko yajamānānugrahabuddhiḥ san ūrdhva uttiṣṭhati |*). Agni, established in the sacrificial pit, with a good mind, thinking that he must favour the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice, spreads his shining flames upward and blazes.
समिद्धस्य रुशत् पाजः आदर्शि (*samiddhasya ruśat pājaḥ ādarśi*)—अस्वाग्नेः रोचमानं बलं ज्वालालक्षणं सर्वैर्दृश्यते (*asvāgneḥ rocamānaṃ balaṃ jvālālakṣaṇaṃ sarvairdṛśyate*). The word पाजः (*pājaḥ*) is read among the names of strength. Here रुशत् पाजः (*ruśat pājaḥ*), shining strength, means the flame of fire burning very brilliantly. Agni, well kindled and blazing well with his shining flames, is visible to all.
महान् देवः तमसः निरमोचि (*mahān devaḥ tamasaḥ niramoci*)—एवंभूतः महान् देव अंधकारात् निर्मुक्तोऽभूत् (*evaṃbhūtaḥ mahān deva aṃdhakārāt nirmukto 'bhūt*). The intended sense is that Agni, of such great glory, released from the darkness that had enveloped all around in the dusk of the morning, is shining.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । ईं । गणस्य । रशनां । अजीगरिति । शुचिः । अंक्त्ये । शुचिभिः । गोभिः । अग्निः ।  
> आत् । दक्षिणा । युज्यते । वाजयंती । उत्तानां । ऊर्ध्वः । अधयत् । जुहूभिः ॥

> *yat | īṃ | gaṇasya | raśanāṃ | ajīgariti | śuciḥ | aṃktye | śucibhiḥ | gobhiḥ | agniḥ |*  
> *āt | dakṣiṇā | yujyate | vājayaṃtī | uttānāṃ | ūrdhvaḥ | adhayat | juhūbhiḥ ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यद्यदेमयमग्निर्गणस्य संघात्मकस्य जगतो रशनां रज्जुरिव व्यापारप्रतिबंधकं तमोऽजीगः । गिरति गृह्णाति वा । समिद्धो भवतीत्यर्थः । तदा शुचिर्दिपोऽग्निः शुचिभिर्गॊभिर्दिप्नैः रश्मिभिरंक्ते । व्यनक्ति विश्वं जगत् । आदनंतरमेव
> दक्षिणा प्रवृद्धा वाजयंत्यन्नमिच्छंत्याज्यधारा युज्यते । युक्ता भवति । अथवा
> दक्षिणा प्रव्यद्धाज्यधारा युज्यते । तां च धारामुत्तानामूर्ध्वतानामुपरि
> विस्त्रतामूर्ध्व उन्नतः सन् जुहूभिरधयत् । पिबति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When this Agni swallows or seizes (अजीगः (*ajīgaḥ*)) the girdle (रशनां (*raśanāṃ*)), which like a rope obstructs the activity, namely the darkness, of the world (गणस्य (*gaṇasya*)) which is of the nature of a collection, that is, when he becomes kindled, then the bright Agni (शुचिः (*śuciḥ*), "shining") makes the whole world manifest (अंक्ते (*aṃkte*)) with bright rays (गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)). Immediately after that the dakṣiṇā, the increased stream of ghee that desires food (वाजयंती (*vājayaṃtī*)), is joined (युज्यते (*yujyate*), "becomes joined"). Or else the dakṣiṇā is the stream of ghee प्रव्यद्धाज्यधारा (*pravyaddhājyadhārā*)**NOTE**. And this stream (उत्तानां (*uttānāṃ*), spread out above), Agni, being raised up (ऊर्ध्वः (*ūrdhvaḥ*)), drinks (अधयत् (*adhayat*)) with the juhūs.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- ईं (*īṃ*)—Agni
- गणस्य (*gaṇasya*)—of the world, which is of the nature of a collection
- रशनां (*raśanāṃ*)—the darkness that obstructs like a rope
- अजीगः (*ajīgaḥ*)—seizes so that it is in his own power (then)
- शुचिः (*śuciḥ*)—shining
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- शुचिभिः (*śucibhiḥ*)—with radiant
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—rays
- अंक्त्ये (*aṃktye*)—makes (the whole universe) shine
- अत् (*at*)—immediately thereafter
- दक्षिणा (*dakṣiṇā*)—the increased one
- वाजयंती (*vājayaṃtī*)—the one desiring food, the stream of ghee
- युज्यते (*yujyate*)—is offered
- उत्तानां (*uttānāṃ*)—this stream of ghee offered upon himself
- ऊर्ध्वः (*ūrdhvaḥ*)—facing upward
- जुहूभिः (*juhūbhiḥ*)—from the juhū vessels
- अधयत् (*adhayat*)—drinks

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When Agni has seized the darkness, which obstructs the world that is of the nature of a collection, so that it is in his own power, then the shining Agni makes the whole universe shine with radiant rays. Immediately thereafter the increased stream of ghee that desires food is offered. Facing upward, he drinks this stream of ghee offered upon himself from the juhū vessels.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
When he seized upon the (confining) girdle of the aggregated (world), then, bright-shining, he makes all manifest with brilliant rays : thereupon the precious food-desiring (oblation) is added (to the flame), and Agni soaring aloft, drinks it as it is (spread out) recumbent by the ladies.
### Printed p. 715

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

यत् ईं गणस्य रशनां अजीगः (*yat īṃ gaṇasya raśanāṃ ajīgaḥ*) (then) शचिः अग्निः शुचिभिः गोभिः अंक्ते (*śaciḥ agniḥ śucibhiḥ gobhiḥ aṃkte*)—यदा आयमग्निः संघात्मकस्य जगतः रज्जुमिव व्यापारप्रतिबंधकं तमः गृह्णाति तदा दीप्तोऽयमग्निः दीप्तै रश्मिभिर्विश्वं जगत् व्यनक्ति (*yadā āyamagniḥ saṃghātmakasya jagataḥ rajjumiva vyāpārapratibaṃdhakaṃ tamaḥ gṛhṇāti tadā dīpto 'yamagniḥ dīptai raśmibhirviśvaṃ jagat vyanakti*). Darkness has spread and pervades all places, as if it had bound this whole world with a rope. Agni, with his shining rays (as one binds with a rope and keeps in one's power), by casting his light, has made it bright everywhere, and thus has seized such darkness.
आत् दक्षिणा वाजयंती युज्यते (*āt dakṣiṇā vājayaṃtī yujyate*)—अनंतरमेव प्रवृद्धा अन्नमिच्छंत्याज्य धारा युक्ता भवति । (*anaṃtarameva pravṛddhā annamicchaṃtyājya dhārā yuktā bhavati |*). अथवा दक्षिणा प्रवृद्धाज्यधारा युज्यते (*athavā dakṣiṇā pravṛddhājyadhārā yujyate*). "Afterwards" means: when Agni is well kindled, the sacrificers and other people who desire food and other nourishment offer much ghee (clarified butter) into Agni.
उत्तानां ऊध्वः जुहूभिः अधयत् (*uttānāṃ ūdhvaḥ juhūbhiḥ adhayat*)—तां च धारां ऊर्ध्वतानामुपरि विस्तृतां उन्नतः सन् जुहूभिः पिबति । (*tāṃ ca dhārāṃ ūrdhvatānāmupari vistṛtāṃ unnataḥ san juhūbhiḥ pibati |*). Juhū means the wooden ladles used for offering ghee into the fire. Thus Agni, stretching his flames upward, drinks the stream of ghee (clarified butter) that the priests and the sacrificer are offering into Agni with the wooden ladles called juhū (pouring it from a height). It is natural that the more ghee is offered into the fire, the higher the flame rises. That very matter is described here in another way: Agni spreads his flames upward and drinks the ghee.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्निं देवमच्छाभिमुख्येन देवयतां देवानात्मन इच्छतां यजमानानां
> मनांसि सं चरंति । देवा यष्टव्यास्तदर्थं कदायं वर्धिष्यतीति ध्यायंतीत्यर्थः ।
> चक्षूंषीव सर्वॆषां प्राणिनां यथा सूर्ये संचरंति तद्वत् । यद्यदेमेनमग्निमुषसा सह विरूपे नानारूपे द्यावापृथिव्य सुवाते । जनयतः । तदानीं
> श्वेतः प्रकृष्टवर्णोपेतो वाजी वेजनवानग्निरह्नामग्र उदयकाले जायिते ।
> प्रवर्धत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The minds of the sacrificers who desire the gods for themselves move together (सं चरंति (*saṃ caraṃti*)) towards Agni, facing him. The sense is that they meditate: "The gods are to be worshipped; when will he grow strong for that purpose?" They move as the eyes of all living beings move towards the sun. When heaven and earth, of many forms, bring forth this Agni together with Uṣas, then Agni, white (of excellent colour) and swift (वाजी (*vājī*), possessing speed), is born at the beginning of the days, at the time of sunrise. The meaning is that he grows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूर्ये (*sūrye*)—fixed on the sun
- चक्षूंषीव (*cakṣūṃṣīva*)—like the eyes (of men)
- देवयतां (*devayatāṃ*)—of the sacrificers who wish to gain the favour of the gods
- मनांसि (*manāṃsi*)—the minds
- अग्निं अच्च (*agniṃ acca*)—facing Agni
- सं चरंति (*saṃ caraṃti*)—move about
- विरूपे (*virūpe*)—heaven and earth, of many forms
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- ईं (*īṃ*)—this Agni
- उषसा सह (*uṣasā saha*)—together with Uṣas
- सुवते (*suvate*)—bring forth (then)
- श्वेतः (*śvetaḥ*)—possessing excellent colour
- वाजी (*vājī*)—swift
- अह्नां अग्रे (*ahnāṃ agre*)—at the time of sunrise
- जायते (*jāyate*)—is born

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Like the eyes of men fixed on the sun, the minds of the sacrificers who wish to gain the favour of the gods move facing Agni. As soon as heaven and earth, of many forms, bring forth this Agni together with Uṣas, Agni, of excellent colour and swift, is born at the time of sunrise.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The minds of the devout turn to Agni, as the eyes (of mcn) look
towords the the sun : when the multiform (heaven and earth) bring him
forth along with the dawn, he is born as a white courser in the beginning
of the days.

### Printed p. 717

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

"The minds of those who wish for the gods move towards Agni, like eyes in the sun": as people who wish to see the sun lift their eyes and look up, so people who wish to worship the gods in the sacrificial fire stand facing Agni and look at Agni alone, with the eager thought, "When will this Agni blaze up well to receive the oblation in the sacrifice?" This is the meaning.
"When heaven and earth, of many forms, bring forth together with Uṣas, the white swift one is born at the beginning of the days": heaven and earth, accompanied by things of many forms, produce at the time of dawn both Uṣas and Agni. That is, Agni is established at dawn itself. At such a time, that is in the morning, he quickly spreads in the firewood and the like, and shines brilliantly.
#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दमे॑दमे स॒प्त रत्ना॒ दधा॑नो॒ऽग्नि होता॒ नि ष॑सादा॒ यजी॑यान् ॥ ५ ॥

> *janiṣṭa | hi | jenyaḥ | agre | āhnāṃ | hitaḥ | hiteṣu | aruṣaḥ | vaneṣu |*  
> *damedame | sapta | ratnā | dadhānaḥ | agniḥ | hotā | ni | sasāda | yajīyān ‖ 5 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयमग्निर्जेन्य उत्पादनीयोऽह्नामग्र उदयकाले जनिष्ट । प्रादुरभूत् ।
> पश्चात् हितेषु वनेषु वनोत्थेषु काष्ठॆष्टरुष आरोचमानः सन् हितः । स्थापितः ।
> पश्चाद्दमे दमे तत्तद्यागगृहे सप्त रत्ना रमणीयाः सप्त ज्वाला दधानो
> धारयमाणः । अथवा यजमानेभ्यः सप्तविधानि रत्नानि दधानोऽग्निर्होता
> होमनिष्पादकः सन् यजीयान्यष्टव्यः सन् नि षसाद । निषण्णो भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Agni, fit to be produced (जेन्यः (*jenyaḥ*)), was born at the beginning of the days, at sunrise; he appeared. Afterwards he was established, shining in the friendly woods, that is, in firewood from the forest. Afterwards, in each house of sacrifice, he bears seven lovely (रत्ना (*ratnā*), "delightful") flames. Or else, bestowing seven kinds of jewels on the sacrificers, Agni, as hotā, the accomplisher of the oblation, and as one to be worshipped, sat down; that is, he is seated.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जेन्यः (*jenyaḥ*)—Agni, fit to be born
- अह्नां अग्रे (*ahnāṃ agre*)—at the time of sunrise
- जनिष्ट (*janiṣṭa*)—was born (afterwards)
- हितेषु (*hiteṣu*)—favourable to his spreading

### Printed p. 718
- वनेषु (*vaneṣu*)—in the woods
- अरुषः (*aruṣaḥ*)—shining
- हितः (*hitaḥ*)—has been established (afterwards)
- दमेदमे (*damedame*)—in every house of sacrifice
- सप्तरत्ना (*saptaratnā*)—his seven lovely flames
- दधानः (*dadhānaḥ*)—bearing
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- होता (*hotā*)—as the accomplisher of the oblation
- यजीयान् (*yajīyān*)—as worthy of sacrifice
- निषसाद (*niṣasāda*)—is seated (has sat down)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, fit to be born, becomes manifest at sunrise and first is established in the forest wood and the like that favour his spreading. Then, in every house of sacrifice, bearing his seven lovely flames, he is seated as the accomplisher of the oblation and as one worthy of sacrifice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
(Agni), capable of birth, is born in the beginning of the days ; radiant, he is deposited in the friendly woods, and then the adorable Agni, the offerer of the oblation, displaying seven precions (rays), is seated in every house.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

जेन्यः अह्नां अग्रे जनिष्ट (*jenyaḥ ahnāṃ agre janiṣṭa*), हितेषु वनेषु अरुषः (*hiteṣu vaneṣu aruṣaḥ*): this Agni, to be produced, appeared at sunrise; afterwards he was established shining in firewood grown in the forest. Established in the sacrificial pit in the morning itself for the sake of the sacrifice, this Agni spreads in the wood and the like that are laid down so that he may kindle well; that is, burning the wood and the like, he shines blazing.
Afterwards, in each house of sacrifice, bearing the lovely seven flames, or bestowing seven kinds of jewels on the sacrificers, Agni, the accomplisher of the oblation, is seated, to be worshipped. This Agni then shines in every house of sacrifice with his seven kinds of flames, or shines as the giver of seven kinds of jewels to the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice. Thus Agni, the accomplisher of the oblation, sits in the fire-pit for the conduct of the sacrifice, that is, he shines. In the Purāṇas and elsewhere the seven kinds of flames of Agni have names such as Kālī and Karālī; these flames are also called the tongues of Agni.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> जीवति यजमाने मृत इति शब्दो यदि स्यात्तदानीं सुरभिमतीष्टिः कार्या।
> तत्रेयमनुवाक्य । सूत्रितं च । अग्निर्होता न्यसीदद्यजीयान्ताध्वीमकर्देववितिं नो आद्य । ऐ. ब्रां. ७_९ । इति ॥
> अयमग्निर्होता होमनिष्पादकः सन् यजीयान्यष्टव्यश्च सन् न्यसीदत् ।
> निषसाद । कुत्रेति तदुच्यते। मातुः सर्वस्य निर्मातुर्भूम्या उपस्थ उत्संगे तत्रापि

> युवा नित्यतरुणः सर्वत्र मिश्रितो ना कविर्मधावी पुरुनिःष्ठो बहुस्थान ऋतावा
> यज्ञवान्धर्ता सर्वस्य धारक एवंभूतः सन् कृष्णीनामृत्विग्यजमानानां मध्य इद्दः
> समिद्धः सन् वर्तत इति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

If, while the sacrificer is alive, the report "he is dead" should arise, the Surabhimatī iṣṭi is to be performed. This verse is the anuvākyā there. It is prescribed (in the sūtra): अग्निर्होता न्यसीदद्यजीयान्ताध्वीमकर्देववितिं नो आद्य (*agnirhotā nyasīdadyajīyāntādhvīmakardevavitiṃ no ādya*) (Ai. Brā. 7-9). This Agni, being hotā, the accomplisher of the oblation, and worthy of worship, sat down. Where? That is stated: in the lap (उपस्थे (*upasthe*)) of the mother, the maker of all, namely the earth; and there in a place (लोके (*loke*)) fragrant with the scent of ghee and the like, a place that all should see, which is marked as the altar. And further, he is ever young, मिश्रितो ना (*miśrito nā*) **NOTE**, wise (कविः (*kaviḥ*), intelligent), many-stationed (पुरुनिःष्ठ (*puruniḥṣṭha*)), possessed of the sacrifice (ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*)), the supporter of all. Being such, he is kindled amid the men (कृष्टीनां (*kṛṣṭīnāṃ*): the priests and sacrificers); "he is" (वर्तत (*vartata*)) is to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- होता (*hotā*)—as the accomplisher of the oblation
- यजीयान् (*yajīyān*)—as worthy of sacrifice
- मातुः (*mātuḥ*)—of his mother, the earth
- उपस्थे (*upasthe*)—which is like the lap
- सुरभौ (*surabhau*)—fragrant
- लोके (*loke*)—on the sacrificial altar
- न्यसीदत् (*nyasīdat*)—has sat down
- उत (*uta*)—and
- युवा (*yuvā*)—ever young
- कविः (*kaviḥ*)—wise
- पुरुनिष्ठः (*puruniṣṭhaḥ*)—stationed in many places
- ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*)—possessed of the sacrifice
- धर्ता (*dhartā*)—the supporter of the whole world
- कृष्णीनां (*kṛṣṇīnāṃ*)—of the sacrificers and others
- मध्यॆ (*madhyè*)—in the midst
- इद्दः (*iddaḥ*)—is kindled

### Printed p. 720

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, being the accomplisher of the oblation and worthy of sacrifice, has sat down on the sacrificial altar, which is like the lap of his mother the earth and is fragrant. And, ever young, wise, stationed in many places, possessed of the sacrifice and the supporter of the whole world, he is kindled in the midst of the priests, the sacrificer and the others.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The adorable Agni, the offerer of the oblation has sat down in
a fragrant place on the top of his mother (earth) : youthful, wise, many-
stationed, the celebrator of sacrifice, the sustainer (of all), kindled
(he abides) amongst men.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

If the report spreads that the sacrificer, though alive, has died, the iṣṭi called Surabhimatī must be performed to remove that fault. Then, at the time of the oblation, this Ṛk beginning अग्निर्होता (*agnirhotā*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra; so the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa sentence अग्निर्होता न्यसीदद्यजीयान्ताध्वीमकर्देवनीतिं नो आद्य (*agnirhotā nyasīdadyajīyāntādhvīmakardevanītiṃ no ādya*) directs (Ai. Brā. 7-9). **NOTE**
Agni is kindled for the oblation. On the sacrificial altar, which is pure, clean and endowed with a good fragrance, Agni shines well. Around this Agni the priests and the sacrificer have gathered for the sacrifice. This Agni is able to be present at one time in many houses of sacrifice; he is the chief means of the sacrifice, and the protector of the world or of the sacrifice. Such is the main purport of this Ṛk: Agni, endowed with such qualities, shines kindled on the sacrificial altar.

> त्यं तमग्निं नमोभिः स्तुतिभिर्नु क्षिप्रं प्रेळते । स्तुवंति । कीदृशं तं । विप्रं
> मेधाविनमध्वरेषु साधुं फलसाधकं होतारं होमनिष्पादकं । यो देवो
> रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यावृतेनोदकेना ततान । विस्तारितवान् । अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतेरादित्यद्वारा वृष्टुत्पादकत्वात् । अथवा ऋतेन सत्यभूतेन हविषा दिवं तथाभूतेन
> वृष्ट्यादिफलेन भुवं चा ततान । वाजिनमन्नवंतं देवं यजमाना नित्यं
> घृतेनोदकेनाज्येन वा मृजंति । परिचरंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

They praise (ईळते (*īḷate*)) that Agni quickly (नु (*nu*), "quickly") with praises (नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)). What sort of Agni? Wise (विप्रं (*vipraṃ*)), efficacious in sacrifices (साधुं (*sādhuṃ*): the accomplisher of fruit), the hotā, the accomplisher of the oblation. The god who spread out (आ ततान (*ā tatāna*)) heaven and earth (रोदसी (*rodasī*)) with ṛta, that is, with water, because the oblations cast into the fire produce rain through the Āditya. Or else, with ṛta as true oblation, he spread heaven, and with the result of that kind, rain and the like, he spread the earth. The sacrificers ever serve (मृजंति (*mṛjaṃti*)) the god possessed of food (वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)) with ghee (घृतेन (*ghṛtena*)), which is water or ājya.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Agni who
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth
- ऋतेन (*ṛtena*)—with water (or with the oblation of the nature of truth)
- आ ततान (*ā tatāna*)—made to extend
- त्यं (*tyaṃ*)—such
- विप्रं (*vipraṃ*)—wise
- अध्वरेषु (*adhvareṣu*)—in sacrifices
- साधुं (*sādhuṃ*)—the accomplisher of fruit
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—the accomplisher of the oblation
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)—with praises
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- ईळते (*īḷate*)—they praise
- वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)—Agni, possessed of food
- नित्यं (*nityaṃ*)—every day
- धृतेन (*dhṛtena*)—with ghee **NOTE**
- मृजंति (*mṛjaṃti*)—they attend and worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

They extol with praises the Agni who made both heaven and earth extend by the oblation of the nature of truth and also by rain; such is he, wise, the accomplisher of fruit in sacrifices, the accomplisher of the oblation. And they attend every day, with ghee, on Agni, the possessor of food.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
They glorify at present with hymns that Agni, who is intelligent, the fullfiller (of desires) at sacrifices, the offerer of oblations, who has charged heaven and earth with water, and whom they always worship with clarified butter as the bestower of food.

### Printed p. 722

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

यः रोदसी ऋतेन आ ततान (*yaḥ rodasī ṛtena ā tatāna*): the god (Agni) extended heaven and earth with water, अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतेरादित्यद्वारा वृष्टुत्पादकत्वात् (*agnau prāstāhuterādityadvārā vṛṣṭutpādakatvāt*). Or else: अथवा ऋतेन सत्यभूतेन हविषा दिव्यं तथाभूतेन वृष्ट्यादिफलेन भुवं च आ ततान । (*athavā ṛtena satyabhūtena haviṣā divyaṃ tathābhūtena vṛṣṭyādiphalena bhuvaṃ ca ā tatāna |*). Sāyaṇa has explained this sentence in two ways. Agni (also the lightning fire) made heaven and earth (the earth and the atmosphere) extend and be pervaded with the water of rain. Or, the oblations offered in Agni reach the Āditya in heaven and satisfy him; and through the Āditya the earth and the atmosphere were pervaded by the water of rain. This is one kind of meaning.
Or, if the word ṛta is taken to mean truth, then by the oblation of the nature of truth, that is, by the oblations and the like offered in the fire, heaven is satisfied, that is, the gods who are in heaven. Thus, when oblations are offered, the gods are pleased and provide the earth with the fruit in the form of rain. So the earth too is satisfied. In this way it is described here that Agni pervaded both heaven and earth.

> स्थाने । कीदृशोऽयं । दमूना दानमना दांतमना वा कविप्रशस्त्रः कविभिर्मेधा-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni is to be cleansed (मार्जाल्यः (*mārjālyaḥ*)); he is cleansed, that is, attended, in his own place. What is he like? दमूना (*damūnā*): of a giving mind or of a controlled mind; कविप्रशस्तः (*kavipraśastaḥ*): praised by the poets, the wise … (the block breaks off here; the next window continues it).

### Printed p. 723

> विभिः प्रशस्तः प्रकर्षेण स्तुत्यो नोऽस्माकमतिथिरतिथिवत्पूज्यः शिवः सुखकरश्च ।
> सहस्रशृंगोऽपरिमितज्वालो वृषभो वर्षिता फलानां तदोजाः । यत्पसिद्धं
> बलं तेजो वास्ति तदेवौजो यस्य तादृशः । सर्वबलस्वरूप इत्यर्थः । अथ प्रत्यक्षवादः । हे अग्ने विश्वानन्यान् स्वव्यतिरिक्तान् सर्वान् सहसा बलेन प्रासि । प्रेति
> परेत्यर्थे । पराभवसि । व्याप्तं वा प्रभवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues his gloss of Ṛk 8. Agni is the one to be served, and he is served in his own place. He is kind-hearted, praised by sages, and honoured as a guest and as a bringer of happiness. He has a thousand horns, that is, boundless flames. He is the showerer of fruits. "Of that might" (तदोजाः (*tadojāḥ*)) means that he has that well-known strength or brilliance; he is of the nature of all strength. Then he turns to direct address: "O Agni, you surpass (प्रासि (*prāsi*)) all others, all besides yourself, by your force." Here प्र (*pra*) is in the sense of परा (*parā*), so you overcome them; or, you prevail by pervading them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दमूनाः (*damūnāḥ*)—one whose mind is given to giving
- कविप्रशस्तः (*kavipraśastaḥ*)—praised by the sages
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- अतिथिः (*atithiḥ*)—worthy of worship like a guest
- शिवः (*śivaḥ*)—the auspicious one
- सहस्रशृंगः (*sahasraśṛṃgaḥ*)—one who has thousands of flames
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—the showerer of desires
- तदोजाः (*tadojāḥ*)—one of well-known strength
- मार्जाल्यः (*mārjālyaḥ*)—Agni, who is worthy of worship
- स्वे (*sve*)—in his own house of sacrifice
- मृज्यते (*mṛjyate*)—is worshipped
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- विश्वान् अन्यान् (*viśvān anyān*)—all others than you
- सहसा (*sahasā*)—by (your) power
- प्रासि (*prāsi*)—you are one whose power overcomes (them)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who is of generous mind, praised by the sages, worthy of worship like a guest to all of us, auspicious, with thousands of flames, the showerer of desires, of well-known strength, and worthy of worship, is worshipped in his own house of sacrifice. O Agni, by your power you are one whose might overcomes all others than yourself.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Entitled to worship, he is worshipped in his own (abode); humble-minded, eminent amongst sages, our auspicious guest, the thousand-rayed the showerer (of benefits). of well-known might, you, Agni, surpass all others in strength.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

मार्जाल्यः—संमार्जनीयोऽयमग्निः । मृज्यते परिचर्यते (*mārjālyaḥ—saṃmārjanīyo 'yamagniḥ | mṛjyate paricaryate*). The root मृज (*mṛja*) has the sense "to attend, to serve", so the word मार्जाल्यः (*mārjālyaḥ*) formed from that root means "one who is worshipped, one who is served", and is an epithet of Agni.

दमूना (*damūnā*)—Yāska gives the etymology of this word: दमूनाः । दमूना दममना वा, दानमना वा दांतमना वा । अपि वा दम इति गृहनाम तन्मनाःस्यात् । मनो मनोतेः ॥ (*damūnāḥ | damūnā damamanā vā, dānamanā vā dāṃtamanā vā | api vā dama iti gṛhanāma tanmanāḥsyāt | mano manoteḥ ‖*) (Ni. 4+4) **NOTE**
### Printed p. 724
That is, the word दमूनाः (*damūnāḥ*) has a threefold meaning: one who is not cruel, or who is compassionate; or one whose mind is set on giving gifts; or one who keeps his own mind under his own control and restraint. Or, since दम (*dama*) means "house", दमूनाः (*damūnāḥ*) may be understood as one who is fond of dwelling in a house. The word मनः (*manaḥ*) is formed from the root मन् (*man*), which means "to think".

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । सद्यः । अग्ने । अति । एषि । अन्यान् । आविः । यस्मै । चारुतमः । बभूथ ।  
> ईळेन्यः । वपुष्यः । विभावा । प्रियः । विशां । अतिथिः । मानुषीणां ॥ ९ ॥

> *pra | sadyaḥ | agne | ati | eṣi | anyān | āviḥ | yasmai | cārutamaḥ | babhūtha |*  
> *īḷenyaḥ | vapuṣyaḥ | vibhāvā | priyaḥ | viśāṃ | atithiḥ | mānuṣīṇāṃ ‖ 9 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वं यज्ञमासाद्य सद्यस्तदानीमेवान्यान् स्वसमानानत्येषि
> अतिक्रामसि । यस्मै चारुतमः सन्नाविर्बभूव । किंच त्वमीळेन्यः स्तुत्यो वपुष्यो
> वपुष्करो दीप्ति करो वा विभावा विशिष्टदीप्तिमान् प्रियः प्रियभूतो विशां
> सर्वेषां प्राणिनां तथातिथिः पूज्यो मानुषीणां प्रजानां भवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, having reached the sacrifice, you at once surpass (अत्येषि (*atyeṣi*)) others like yourself, that is, you go beyond them, for the sake of whom you become manifest as the most beautiful." Further: you are to be praised (ईळेन्यः (*īḷenyaḥ*)); वपुष्यः (*vapuṣyaḥ*) is the maker of the body or the maker of splendour; विभावा (*vibhāvā*) is one of distinguished radiance. You are dear to all (विशां (*viśāṃ*)) living beings, and you are, like a guest, to be honoured by the human peoples (मानुषीणां (*mānuṣīṇāṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- यस्मै (*yasmai*)—for whichever sacrificer
- चारुतमः (*cārutamaḥ*)—having a most attractive form
- प्र (*pra*)—exceedingly
- आविर्बभूथ (*āvirbabhūtha*)—you become manifest
- सद्यः (*sadyaḥ*)—at once
- अन्यान् (*anyān*)—to others as well
- अत्येषि (*atyeṣi*)—you pass over
- ईळेन्यः (*īḷenyaḥ*)—one to be praised
- वपुष्यः (*vapuṣyaḥ*)—one of beautiful form
- विभावा (*vibhāvā*)—one of excessive splendour
- प्रियः (*priyaḥ*)—one who is dear
- मानुषीणां विशां (*mānuṣīṇāṃ viśāṃ*)—to all the human peoples
- अतिथिः (*atithiḥ*)—worthy of worship like a guest (you are)
### Printed p. 725

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, for whichever sacrificer you become manifest, with a most excellent bodily form, at that very moment you pass on to others. You are one to be praised, of beautiful form, of exceeding radiance, dear, and worthy of worship to all human peoples.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
(Too) quickly, Agni, you pass to others from him to whom you have been manifest: most beautiful, adorable, radiant, many-shinning, the loved of people, the guest of men.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The main sense is this: O Agni, the sacrificer for whom you shine in his house of sacrifice, with the intention of helping him, with an attractive form, that is, most brilliant, you do not leave him and go to the other sacrificers. All praise you. Your form is very attractive and lustrous. Therefore you are dear to all and worthy of worship like a guest.

अतिथिः (*atithiḥ*)—For the word अतिथि (*atithi*) Yāska gives the etymology अतिथिरभ्यतितो गृहान् भवति । अभ्येति तिथिसु परकुलानीति वा परगृहाणीति वा । अयमपीतरोऽतिथिरेतस्मादेव (*atithirabhyatito gṛhān bhavati | abhyeti tithisu parakulānīti vā paragṛhāṇīti vā | ayamapītaro 'tithiretasmādeva*) (Ni. 4-4). That is, the word means one who, wandering outside, comes to houses without prior notice; or one who comes on business, on the तिथि (*tithi*) days such as the full-moon day, to the houses of others who are not of his own family or house. Or, since he goes to the house of others on whatever day it may be, without fixed days (तिथि (*tithi*)), he can be explained as "the one without a fixed day".

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तुभ्यं॑ भरंति क्षि॒तयो॑ यविष्ठ ब॒लिम॑ग्ने॒ अंति॑त॒ ओत दू॒रात् ।  
> आ भंदि॑ष्ठस्य सुम॒तिं चि॑किद्दि बृ॒हत्ते॑ अग्ने॒ महि॒ शर्म॑ भ॒द्रं ॥

> *tubhyaṃ bharaṃti kṣitayo yaviṣṭha balimagne aṃtita ota dūrāt |*  
> *ā bhaṃdiṣṭhasya sumatiṃ cikiddi bṛhatte agne mahi śarma bhadraṃ ‖*

### Printed p. 726

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तुभ्यं । भरंति । क्षितयः । यविष्ठ । बलिं । अग्ने । अंतितः । अ । उत । दूरात् ।  
> आ । भंदिष्ठस्य । सुमतिं । चिकिद्दि । बृहत् । ते । अग्ने । महि । शर्म । भद्रं ॥ १० ॥

> *tubhyaṃ | bharaṃti | kṣitayaḥ | yaviṣṭha | baliṃ | agne | aṃtitaḥ | a | uta | dūrāt |*  
> *ā | bhaṃdiṣṭhasya | sumatiṃ | cikiddi | bṛhat | te | agne | mahi | śarma | bhadraṃ ‖ 10 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे यविष्ठ युवतमाग्ने तुभ्यं क्षितयो मनुष्या भरंति । संपादयंति ।
> किं । बलिं पूजां हविर्लक्षणामंतितोऽंतिकादुतापि च दूरात् । आ इति चार्थे ।
> किंच भंदिष्ठ स्यातिशयेन स्तोतुः सुमतिं स्तुतिमा चिकिद्दि । आजानीहि । हे अग्ने ते
> तव शर्म सुखमस्मभ्यं दातव्यं बृहन्महद्भद्रं स्तुत्यं च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O youngest Agni (यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*)), the people (क्षितयः (*kṣitayaḥ*), men) bring (भरंति (*bharaṃti*)) to you", that is, they prepare. What? An offering (बलिं (*baliṃ*)), worship in the form of oblation, from near and also from far; आ (*ā*) is in the sense of "and". Further, grasp (चिकिद्दि (*cikiddi*)), that is, know, the good thought (सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*)), the praise, of the worshipper who most delights you (भंदिष्ठस्य (*bhaṃdiṣṭhasya*)). O Agni, your happiness (शर्म (*śarma*)), which is to be given to us, is great, vast, auspicious and praiseworthy.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*)—exceedingly young
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- क्षितयः (*kṣitayaḥ*)—the sacrificers, in the form of men
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you
- बलिं (*baliṃ*)—worship together with the oblation
- भरंति (*bharaṃti*)—they prepare
- अंतितः (*aṃtitaḥ*)—whether from near
- उत (*uta*)—or
- दूरात् (*dūrāt*)—from a far region
- भंदिष्ठस्य (*bhaṃdiṣṭhasya*)—of the worshipper who praises exceedingly
- सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*)—the excellent praise
- आ चिकिद्दि (*ā cikiddi*)—know well (and accept)
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- ते (*te*)—(given) by you
- शर्म (*śarma*)—the happiness
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—abundant
- महि (*mahi*)—great
- भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*)—and auspicious in nature (it is)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, exceedingly young, the sacrificers in the form of men prepare and offer to you worship together with the oblation. Whether from near or from a far region, know well and accept the excellent praise of the worshipper who praises you exceedingly. O Agni, the happiness given by you to us is abundant, great and auspicious in nature.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
To you, youngest (of the gods), men present oblations, whether
nigh or from far : accept the praise of him who most extols you ; for the
felicity (which you confer), Agni, is great, vast, auspicious.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

क्षितयः (*kṣitayaḥ*)—Since the word क्षितयः (*kṣitayaḥ*) is read among the twenty-five names of man beginning मनुष्याः (*manuṣyāḥ*), नरः (*naraḥ*) (Ni. 3-7), क्षितयः (*kṣitayaḥ*) means men.
### Printed p. 727

यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*)—युवतम (*yuvatama*). Addressing Agni by the word यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*) is a particular usage in the Ṛgveda. When fuel, wood and the like are put on a burning fire, it keeps burning well. When men or animals, in their middle age, grown by nourishing food and the like and endowed with full strength and capacity, are said to be young, that is, in the state of greatest strength and capacity in their lifetime. In the same way fire burns well when wood and the like are put on it, and this is compared with the state of the young. The youth of men and other beings lasts only for some time, then diminishes and at last is lost. But it is not so with Agni. As long as wood and the like are put on to kindle him, he burns well for any length of time; so in many contexts he is praised with the epithets "ever-young" and "always a youth".

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आद्य रथं॑ भानुमो भानु॒मंत॒मग्ने॒ तिष्ठ॑ यज॒तेभिः॒  ॑

> वि॒द्वान्प॑थी॒नामु॒र्व१॒॑गन्तरी॑क्ष॒मेह दे॒वान्ह॑वि॒रद्या॑य वक्षि ॥ ११ ॥

> *ādya rathaṃ bhānumo bhānumaṃtamagne tiṣṭha yajatebhiḥ*  
> *samaṃtaṃ |*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विद्वान् । पथीनां । उरु । अंतरिक्षं । आ । इह । देवान् । हविःs आद्याय । वक्षि ॥१०॥

> *ā | adya | rathaṃ | bhānumaḥ | bhānumaṃtaṃ | āgne | tiṣṭha | yajatebhiḥ | saṃaṃtaṃ |*  
> *vidvān | pathīnāṃ | uru | aṃtarikṣaṃ | ā | iha | devān | haviḥs ādyāya | vakṣi ‖10‖*

**NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे भानुमो दीप्तिमन्नग्ने अद्यास्मिन्यागदिने भानुमंतं दीप्तिमंतं
> समंतं समीचीनप्रांतोपेतं रथं यजतेभिर्यष्टवैर्देवैः सहा तिष्ठ । आरोह ।
> विद्वान्यष्टव्यदेवपरिज्ञानवांत्वं पथीनां देवयजनमार्गान्प्रति ॥ द्वितीयार्थे
> षष्ठि ॥ उर्वंतरिक्षं प्रभूते०तरिक्षे देवान्यष्टव्यान्हविरद्याय हविर्भक्षणायेहा
> वक्षि । आवहसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O radiant Agni (भानुमः (*bhānumaḥ*)), today, on this day of sacrifice, mount (तिष्ठ (*tiṣṭha*), ascend) together with the gods to be worshipped (यजतेभिः (*yajatebhiḥ*)) the chariot which is radiant (भानुमंतं (*bhānumaṃtaṃ*)) and has well-formed (समंतं (*samaṃtaṃ*)) edges. Knowing the gods to be worshipped, knowing the paths (पथीनां (*pathīnāṃ*)) of the divine sacrifice (here the genitive stands in the sense of the accusative), bring (वक्षि (*vakṣi*)) hither, through the vast firmament (उरु अंतरिक्षं (*uru aṃtarikṣaṃ*)), the gods to be worshipped, to eat the oblation (हविरद्याय (*haviradyāya*))."

### Printed p. 728

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- भानुमः (*bhānumaḥ*)—O one of splendour
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- अद्य (*adya*)—today, this day of the sacrifice
- यजतेभिः (*yajatebhiḥ*)—together with the other gods worthy of the sacrifice
- भानुमंतं (*bhānumaṃtaṃ*)—lustrous
- समंतं (*samaṃtaṃ*)—having decorated edges
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—your chariot
- आ तिष्ठ (*ā tiṣṭha*)—mount and sit
- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—you who know everything
- उर्वंतरिक्षं (*urvaṃtarikṣaṃ*)—in the vast firmament
- पथीनां (*pathīnāṃ*)—by the path of going to the sacrifice **NOTE**
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods
- हविरद्याय (*haviradyāya*)—in order to receive the oblation
- इह (*iha*)—to this sacrifice
- आ वक्षि (*ā vakṣi*)—bring

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, full of splendour, today, the day of this sacrifice, mount and sit in your chariot, lustrous and with decorated edges, together with the other gods worthy of the sacrifice. You, the all-knowing, through the vast firmament, by the path of going to the sacrifice, bring the gods to this sacrifice to receive and eat the oblation.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Ascend to-day, radiant Agni, your resplendent, well-conducted
chariot, together with the adorable (gods): cognizant of the ways (of
worship), bring hither, by the vast firmament, the gods to partake of
the oblation.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk Agni is prayed to come to the place of sacrifice seated in his chariot and to bring the gods worthy of the sacrifice. It is described that the chariot of Agni is exceedingly brilliant, and that, seated in such a chariot, he should bring through the path of the firmament the invited gods to eat the oblation offered in the sacrifice.

> गविष्ठिरः । नमसा । स्तोमं । अग्नौ । दिविइव । रुक्ष्मं । उरुव्यंचं । अश्रेत् ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वयमात्रेयाः कवये मेधाविने मेध्याय मेधार्हाय वृषभाय
> वर्षकाय फलानां वृष्णे सेक्रे यूने वंदारु वंदनशीलं वचः स्तोत्रमवोचाम । अथ ऋषिरात्मानं परोक्षेणैव निर्दिष्ट स्तुतिमुपसंहरति । गविष्ठिरोऽयमृषिर्नमसा नमस्कारेण हविषा वा युक्तं स्तोमं स्तोत्रमग्नावश्रेत् । श्रयति
> स्म । दिवि रुक्ष्मं रोचमानमुरुव्यंचमुरुगमनमादित्यमिव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We Ātreyas have uttered a praise that bows in homage to the wise (कवये (*kavaye*)), the worthy of sacrificial wisdom (मेध्याय (*medhyāya*)), the bull (वृषभाय (*vṛṣabhāya*)), the showerer of fruits, the sprinkler (वृष्णे (*vṛṣṇe*)), the young one. Then the seer, referring to himself in the third person, brings the praise to a close. This seer Gaviṣṭhira has resorted to Agni with a hymn (स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)) joined with homage, or with an oblation. The hymn is addressed to Agni, who shines in the sky and moves widely, like the sun.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कवये (*kavaye*)—wise one
- मेध्याय (*medhyāya*)—worthy of worship
- वृषभाय (*vṛṣabhāya*)—showerer of desires
- वृष्णे (*vṛṣṇe*)—young one; (we speak) to Agni
- वंदारु (*vaṃdāru*)—praise worthy of worship
- वचः (*vacaḥ*)—the praise
- अवोचाम (*avocāma*)—we recite
- गविष्ठिरः (*gaviṣṭhiraḥ*)—this seer named Gaviṣṭhira
- नमसा (*namasā*)—with homage
- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—the hymn
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the sky
- रुक्ष्मं (*rukṣmaṃ*)—the one who shines with a golden hue
- उरुव्यंचं (*uruvyaṃcaṃ*)—the one who pervades widely like the sun
- अग्नौ (*agnau*)—in Agni
- अश्रेत् (*aśret*)—has offered

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We recite praise worthy of worship, addressed to Agni, the wise, the worthy of worship, the showerer of desires, the young. This seer, named Gaviṣṭhira, has offered his own hymn, accompanied by homage, to Agni, who shines in the sky with a golden hue and pervades widely like the sun.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We have uttered aloud this encomiastic praise to the wise, holy, vigorous (Agni), the showerer (of benefits): Gavishthira offers with reverence (this) praise to Agni, like the wide-sojourning (sun), effulgent in the sky.

### Printed p. 730

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this last Ṛk, which concludes the sūkta, the seer Gaviṣṭhira, who saw the sūkta, names himself. He says that he has praised Agni with excellent words, and that he has offered to Agni, who shines with splendour like the sun, a hymn accompanied by homage, and an oblation, and so he commends his own conduct. Although two seers, Budha and Gaviṣṭhira, are the seers of this sūkta, only the name of one seer, Gaviṣṭhira, is recited here. The name of the seer Budha is not mentioned.

## Sūkta 2 (Maṇḍala 5)
This is the second sūkta.

Introduction.

Kumāra, Vṛśa and Jāna are declared to be the seers of the second sūkta in the fifth maṇḍala. Kumāra is one of the synonyms of Agni. In this sūkta Agni is specifically denoted by that very word kumāra, and it is also stated to be the name of the seer. For this reason the sūkta may be called the Kaumāra sūkta. How Agni came to be named Kumāra is told in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa as follows.

तद्यानि तानि भूतानि । ऋतवस्तेऽथ यः स भूतानां पतिः संवत्सरः सोऽथ या सोषाः पत्न्यौषसी सा तानिमानि भूतानि च भूतानां पतिः संवत्सर उषसि रेतोऽसिंचन्त्स संवत्सरे कुमारोऽजायत........ ॥ (*tadyāni tāni bhūtāni | ṛtavaste 'tha yaḥ sa bhūtānāṃ patiḥ saṃvatsaraḥ so 'tha yā soṣāḥ patnyauṣasī sā tānimāni bhūtāni ca bhūtānāṃ patiḥ saṃvatsara uṣasi reto 'siṃcantsa saṃvatsare kumāro 'jāyata........ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 6-1-3-8)

These beings are the seasons. The lord of beings is the year. Uṣas is the wife. The seasons, who are of the nature of beings, and the year, the lord of beings, poured seed into Uṣas, the wife. As a result Kumāra was born. This Kumāra is the ninth form of Agni. Since Agni of such a nature is praised, the name of the seer of this sūkta is also Kumāra.

Besides this, it is conjectured that a seer named Vṛśa Jāna is also the author of this sūkta. The story of Vṛśa Jāna is told briefly in the Bṛhaddevatā as follows.

ऐक्ष्वाकुस्त्यरुणो राजा त्रैवृष्णो रथमास्थितः । संजग्राहाश्वरश्मींश्च वृशो जानः पुरोहितः ॥ (*aikṣvākustyaruṇo rājā traivṛṣṇo rathamāsthitaḥ | saṃjagrāhāśvaraśmīṃśca vṛśo jānaḥ purohitaḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 5-14)

### Printed p. 731
Tryaruṇa, born in the Ikṣvāku line, the son of Trivṛṣṇa, once set out seated in a chariot. Then his house-priest Vṛśa, the son of Jana, held the reins of the horses and drove the chariot.

स ब्राह्मणकुमारस्य रथो गच्छच्चिरोऽच्चिनत् । एनस्वीत्यब्रवीच्चैव स राज्यैनं पुरोहितं ॥ (*sa brāhmaṇakumārasya ratho gacchacciro 'ccinat | enasvītyabravīccaiva sa rājyainaṃ purohitaṃ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 5-15)

This chariot, driven by Vṛśa Jāna, ran over the body of a young Brahmin boy, and because of this his head was cut off. Then Traiyaruṇa said sharply to his priest: "Since you were driving the chariot, you alone share the sin arising from this killing."

सोऽथर्वांगिरसान् मंत्रान् दृष्ट्वा संजीव्य तं शिशुं । क्रोधात्संत्सज्य राजानमन्यदेशं समाश्रितः ॥ ( (*so 'tharvāṃgirasān maṃtrān dṛṣṭvā saṃjīvya taṃ śiśuṃ | krodhātsaṃtsajya rājānamanyadeśaṃ samāśritaḥ ‖ (*) (Bṛ. Pe. 25-16) **NOTE**

When the king spoke so harshly, disgust arose in Vṛśa's mind. At once he had a direct vision of the Atharvāṅgirasa mantras and recited them. By the power of those mantras the life of the child returned. Even so, displeased by the king's harsh words, he abandoned that king in anger and went off to take refuge with a king of another country.

हरोऽप्यग्नेर्ननाशास्य तस्यापक्रमणादृषेः । अग्नौ प्रास्तानि हव्यानि न ह्यपच्यंत कानिचित् ॥ (*haro 'pyagnernanāśāsya tasyāpakramaṇādṛṣeḥ | agnau prāstāni havyāni na hyapacyaṃta kānicit ‖*) (5-17)

As a result of the priest's going off in anger, the heat of Agni too was lost in that king's house. None of the oblations he offered was cooked, and all his efforts at sacrifice failed.

ततः प्रव्यथितो राजा सोऽभिगम्य प्रसाद्य तं । अनीत्वा स वृशं जानं पुनरेव पुरोदधे ॥ (*tataḥ pravyathito rājā so 'bhigamya prasādya taṃ | anītvā sa vṛśaṃ jānaṃ punareva purodadhe ‖*) (5-18)

Since the priest had gone and, as a result, the power of Agni too had vanished, the king was greatly grieved. Afterwards he went to the place where Vṛśa Jāna was, honoured him with worship and the like, brought him back, and again made him his own priest.

### Printed p. 732
स प्रसन्नो वृशोऽन्वैच्छद्धरमग्नेर्नृपक्षये । अविंदत पिशाचीं तां जायां तस्य च भूपतेः ॥ (*sa prasanno vṛśo 'nvaicchaddharamagnernṛpakṣaye | aviṃdata piśācīṃ tāṃ jāyāṃ tasya ca bhūpateḥ ‖*) (5-19)

Vṛśa Jāna, appeased by the king's repentance and by his acts of worship, accepted his priesthood again. Then he established Agni in the king's house and prayed that the heat of that Agni might arise again. But as the result of that prayer he saw that the king had obtained a wife in the form of a piśācī.

निषण्णस्स तया सार्धं आसंद्यां कशिपावपि । तामुपामंत्रयांचक्रे कमेतं त्वमिति त्वृचा ॥ (*niṣaṇṇassa tayā sārdhaṃ āsaṃdyāṃ kaśipāvapi | tāmupāmaṃtrayāṃcakre kametaṃ tvamiti tvṛcā ‖*) (5-20)

Then he himself sat on a seat with that wife of the king, who was in the form of a piśācī, recited the mantra कमेतं त्वं (*kametaṃ tvaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-2-2), and asked her: "O young woman, who is this boy whom you rear, having taken the form of a piśācī?" and so on.

हरः कुमाररूपेण ब्रुवंस्तामभ्यभाषत । विज्योतिषेति चोक्तायां सहसाग्नि रुदज्वलत् ॥ (*haraḥ kumārarūpeṇa bruvaṃstāmabhyabhāṣata | vijyotiṣeti coktāyāṃ sahasāgni rudajvalat ‖*) (5-2) **NOTE**

Designating the heat of Agni as the boy (kumāra), as soon as he had questioned that piśācī woman with the mantra stated above (5-2-2), he recited again the mantra वि ज्योतिषा (*vi jyotiṣā*) (5-2-9). The purport of that mantra is: "Agni shines with great flames full of variety; he makes his flames very sharp." As soon as this mantra was recited, the great flame of Agni appeared.

सहमानः समायांतं प्रकाशं च प्रकाशयन् । पिशाचीमदहत्तां स यत्र चोपविवेश सा ॥ (*sahamānaḥ samāyāṃtaṃ prakāśaṃ ca prakāśayan | piśācīmadahattāṃ sa yatra copaviveśa sā ‖*) (5-22)

That great flame of Agni, shining with its great radiance and driving far away all who approached it, finally burned that woman in piśācī form to ashes on the very spot where she sat. This is the story that describes the great power of Vṛśa Jāna. The mantras 5-2-2 and 5-2-9, which commend this greatness, are also commended in other places.

एष एव परामृष्टो भाल्लविब्राह्मणे द्वृचः । निदानसंज्ञके ग्रंथे छंदोगानामिति श्रुतिः ॥ (*eṣa eva parāmṛṣṭo bhāllavibrāhmaṇe dvṛcaḥ | nidānasaṃjñake graṃthe chaṃdogānāmiti śrutiḥ ‖*) (5-23)

### Printed p. 733
Both these mantras are cited in the Bhāllavī Brāhmaṇa, and are also commended in the Nidāna treatise of the Chandogas. This is the occasion that shows the greatness of Vṛśa Jāna. This very story, cited above, Sāyaṇa has told in the context of his commentary on the mantra Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-2-1.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कुमारं मातेति द्वादशर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तं । अत्रेः पुत्रः कुमारः
> ऋषिर्जननाम्नः पुत्रो वृशो वोभौ वात्र ऋषी । कमेतं त्वं वि ज्योतिषेत्यनयोस्तु वृश एव नोभौ न कुमारः । अंत्या षट्पंचाशदक्षरा शक्वरी शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुभः ।
> अग्निर्देवता । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । कुमारं कुमारो वृशो वा जान उभौ वा
> शक्वर्यंतं कं वीत्यचोस्तु वृश एवेति ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोरस्यापि सूक्तस्य
> विनियोग उक्तः पूर्वसूक्तेन सह ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The second sūkta, कुमारं माता (*kumāraṃ mātā*), has twelve Ṛks. Its seer is Kumāra, son of Atri; or Vṛśa, son of the man named Jana; or both are the seers here. But for the two Ṛks कमेतं त्वं (*kametaṃ tvaṃ*) and वि ज्योतिषा (*vi jyotiṣā*) Vṛśa alone is the seer, not Kumāra, and not both. The last Ṛk is a Śakvarī of fifty-six syllables; the rest are Triṣṭubh. The deity is Agni. Sāyaṇa cites the Anukramaṇikā: कुमारं कुमारो वृशो वा जान उभौ वा शक्वर्यंतं कं वीत्यचोस्तु वृश एव (*kumāraṃ kumāro vṛśo vā jāna ubhau vā śakvaryaṃtaṃ kaṃ vītyacostu vṛśa eva*). The application (viniyoga) of this sūkta, in the Prātaranuvāka and in the recitation of the Āśvina śastra, has been stated together with the previous sūkta.

Anuvāda: this sūkta, कुमारं माता (*kumāraṃ mātā*), is the second sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has twelve Ṛks. Its seer is Kumāra, son of the seer Atri; or Vṛśa, son of the seer named Jana; or both may be the seers of this sūkta. But for these two Ṛks of the sūkta, कमेतं त्वं (*kametaṃ tvaṃ*) (the 2nd Ṛk) and वि ज्योतिषा (*vi jyotiṣā*) (the 9th Ṛk), Vṛśa alone is the seer; neither Kumāra, as said above, nor both. Agni is the deity. The last Ṛk of this sūkta is in the metre called Śakvarī of fifty-six syllables. All the remaining Ṛks are in the Triṣṭubh metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is stated: कुमारं कुमारो वृशो वा जान उभौ ना शक्वर्यंतं कं वीत्य चोस्तु वृश एव (*kumāraṃ kumāro vṛśo vā jāna ubhau nā śakvaryaṃtaṃ kaṃ vītya costu vṛśa eva*). The application of this sūkta for the recitation of the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvinaśastra mantras has been stated in the application of the preceding sūkta.

Sūkta 2. Maṇḍala 5, Anuvāka 1, Sūkta 2. Aṣṭaka 3, Adhyāya 8, Vargas 14, 15. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 12.

Seer: 1, 3–4, 10–12. Kumāra Ātreya, or Vṛśa Jāna, or both. 2, 9. Vṛśa Jāna.

Deity: Agni.

Metre: 1–11 Triṣṭubh; 12 Śakvarī.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that the story told in the Śāṭyāyana Brāhmaṇa is related here. Tryaruṇa, the Aikṣvāka king of the line of Trivṛṣṇa, had as his priest the seer Vṛśa Jāna. Priests take the reins of kings' chariots for their protection, and so Vṛśa took Tryaruṇa's reins. A boy, Kumāra, playing in the road, was killed by the chariot wheel; the boy was cut by the wheel and the priest was sorrowful. The king said to the priest, "You are the slayer"; the priest said to the king, "Not I." Since the priest was the controller of the chariot's speed, the king said he had killed the boy; the priest said the king, as master of the chariot, was the killer. Disputing thus, they went to ask the Ikṣvākus, "By whom was this boy killed, O Brahmins?" They named the driver, the slayer, called Vṛśa. Vṛśa revived the boy with the Vārśa sāman. Having narrated this, Sāyaṇa tells another version. Because the Ikṣvākus in anger called the seer a slayer, Agni's heat left their houses, and cooking and the like did not occur in the house. They reflected on the reason: "Because we called Vṛśa the slayer of the boy, the heat of Agni has gone away; let us call Vṛśa." So they respectfully invited that seer. Wishing that Agni's heat might quickly return to them, he desired it as before through the Pārśa sāman. Singing thus, the seer took the brahmahatyā born from the wife of King Trasadasyu, in the form of a piśācī, and led her from the house of Agni and set her on a seat. The heat looked on well, was satisfied, and afterwards joined Agni again with the sāman. Then Agni became splendid, and the cooking and the rest were as before. **NOTE**
Thus, Sāyaṇa says, it was told by Śāṭyāyana; now what is said in the Kāṇḍaka is stated: वृशः पुरोधा अभवत्र- (*vṛśaḥ purodhā abhavatra-*) (the block breaks off here; the next window continues).

> सदस्योर्महीपतेः ॥ स रथं धावयन्नाजा ब्राह्मणस्य कुमारकं । चिच्छेद रथचक्रेण
> प्रमादात्सोऽब्रवीद्वशं ॥ पुरोहिते वर्तमाने त्वयि मां हंति रागता । एषा
> त्वयापनेतव्या ऋषिमित्यब्रवीन्मृपः ॥ स ऋषिर्वार्शसाम्ना तं कुमारमुदजीवयत् ॥ माता कुमारस्योत्पादयित्री युवतिर्यौवनोपेता कुमारं पथि संचरंतं
> समुब्धं चक्रेण हतं गुहा गुहायां भिभर्ति । धारयति । न ददाति पित्रे तस्य
> जनताय । यद्वा । माता सर्वस्य निर्मात्रि पृथीवी समुब्धं सम्यक् निगूढं गुहा
> बिभर्ति । न ददाति पित्रे । अस्य कुमारस्यानीकं रूपं मिनत् हिंसितं जनासो जना
> न पश्यंति । किंतु अरतावरमणे देशे निहितं स्थितं पुरः पुरोदेशे पश्यंति ।
> आथवायं वृशेन पुनरुज्जिवितः कुमार आत्मानमपरोक्षतया वक्ति । कथयति ।
> जानो वा तं जीवयित्वा वक्ति । अथवा सूक्तस्याग्नेयत्वात्कुमार इत्यग्निरुच्यते ।
> तं मातारणियुवतिर्मिश्रयंती समुब्धं निगूढं गुहायां बिभर्ति । पित्र
> उत्पादकाय यजमानाय न ददाति । अस्याग्निर्मिनत् हिंसत् दाहकमनीकं तेजो
> जना न पश्यंति । किंतु अरतावरण्यां हितं पश्यंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues the story. Vṛśa became the purohita of King Trasadasyu. While driving the chariot the king, in a moment of carelessness, cut down a Brahmin's little boy with the chariot wheel. He said to Vṛśa: "While you are my purohita, this guilt has fallen upon me; you must remove it", and the Ṛṣi revived the boy with the Vārśa sāman.

He then explains the verse. The mother, the young woman in her youth, holds the boy, who was struck down by the wheel as he moved about on the road, hidden in a cave (गुहा गुहायां (*guhā guhāyāṃ*)). She does not give him to his father, the one who begot him.

Alternatively, the "mother" is the Earth, the maker of all, who holds him well hidden in a cave and does not give him to the father. People do not see the form of this boy, which is "injured"; but they see him placed in the अरतौ (*aratau*) (a place of no delight), in front of them.

Or else the boy, revived by Vṛśa, tells of himself directly; or Jāna, having revived him, speaks of him.

Or else, because the sūkta is addressed to Agni, "kumāra" means Agni. His mother is the young araṇi (fire-stick), who holds him hidden in the cave. She does not give him to his "father", the sacrificer who is the begetter. People do not see the burning splendour of this Agni that "injures"; they see it placed in the araṇi, in the woodland.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- युवतिः (*yuvatiḥ*)—the young mother, endowed with youth
- माता (*mātā*)—the mother
- समुब्बं (*samubbaṃ*)—injured by the wheel
- कुमारं (*kumāraṃ*)—the son
- गुहा (*guhā*)—in secret
- बिभर्ति (*bibharti*)—holds
- पित्रे (*pitre*)—to the father of the son
- न ददाति (*na dadāti*)—does not hand over
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this boy
- मिनत् (*minat*)—injured
- अनीकं (*anīkaṃ*)—the form
- जनासः (*janāsaḥ*)—people
- न पश्यंति (*na paśyaṃti*)—do not see (but)
- पुरः (*puraḥ*)—in front of themselves
- अरतौ (*aratau*)—in an unsettled state
- निहितं (*nihitaṃ*)—the son who is placed (only)
- पश्यंति (*paśyaṃti*)—they see

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The young mother holds in secret her son, who was injured by the wheel. She does not hand him over to the son's father. But people see only the son who is placed before them in an unsettled state.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The young mother cherishes her mutilated boy in secret, and gives him not up to the father : men behold not his mutilated form, but (see him) when placed before (them) in an unresting (position).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Concerning the matter described in the first Ṛk of this sūkta, the commentator has set out as follows the story-setting told in the Śāṭyāyana-brāhmaṇa of the Sāmaveda:

शाट्यायनब्राह्मणोक्त इतिहास इहोच्यते । राजा त्रैवृष्ण ऐक्ष्वाकः त्रुणोभवदस्य च ॥ पुरोहितो वृशो जान ऋषिरासीत्तदा खलु । संगृह्णंति रथान् राजां रक्षणाय पुरोहिताः ॥ (*śāṭyāyanabrāhmaṇokta itihāsa ihocyate | rājā traivṛṣṇa aikṣvākaḥ truṇobhavadasya ca ‖ purohito vṛśo jāna ṛṣirāsīttadā khalu | saṃgṛhṇaṃti rathān rājāṃ rakṣaṇāya purohitāḥ ‖*)
त्रुणस्य वृशो रश्मिं संजग्राह पुरोहितः । कुमारो वर्त्मनि क्रीडन्रथचक्रेण घातितः ॥ (*truṇasya vṛśo raśmiṃ saṃjagrāha purohitaḥ | kumāro vartmani krīḍanrathacakreṇa ghātitaḥ ‖*)
छिन्नः कुमारश्च क्रेण ममाराध पुरोहितः । त्वं हंतास्येति राजानं राजा चापि पुरोहितं ॥ (*chinnaḥ kumāraśca kreṇa mamārādha purohitaḥ | tvaṃ haṃtāsyeti rājānaṃ rājā cāpi purohitaṃ ‖*)
त्वं हंतास्य कुमारस्य नाहमित्यब्रवीत्तदा । यतस्त्वं रथवेगस्य नियंतातस्त्वया हतः ॥ (*tvaṃ haṃtāsya kumārasya nāhamityabravīttadā | yatastvaṃ rathavegasya niyaṃtātastvayā hataḥ ‖*)
रथस्वामी यतो राजन् तस्मात्त्वं तस्य घातकः । एवं विवदमानौ ताविक्ष्वाकून्ष्टुमागत् ॥ (*rathasvāmī yato rājan tasmāttvaṃ tasya ghātakaḥ | evaṃ vivadamānau tāvikṣvākūnṣṭumāgat ‖*)
तौ पप्रच्छतुरिक्ष्वा कून् केनास् निहतो द्विजः । तेऽब्रुवन्रथयंतारं हंतारं वृशसंज्ञकं ॥ (*tau papracchaturikṣvā kūn kenās nihato dvijaḥ | te 'bruvanrathayaṃtāraṃ haṃtāraṃ vṛśasaṃjñakaṃ ‖*)
स वृशो वार्शसाम्मा तं कुमारं समजीवयत् । एवमाख्यायि तत्रैव पुनरन्यदुदीरितं ॥ (*sa vṛśo vārśasāmmā taṃ kumāraṃ samajīvayat | evamākhyāyi tatraiva punaranyadudīritaṃ ‖*)
यत इष्टाकवो रागाद्दंतरामृषिमब्रुवन् । तस्मात्तेषां गृहेष्वग्नेस्तेजो निर्गतमेषु च ॥ (*yata iṣṭākavo rāgāddaṃtarāmṛṣimabruvan | tasmātteṣāṃ gṛheṣvagnestejo nirgatameṣu ca ‖*)
गृहे पाकादयो नासन् तत्कारणमचिंतयन् । वृशं कुमारहंतारं यदवोचाम तेन नः ॥ (*gṛhe pākādayo nāsan tatkāraṇamaciṃtayan | vṛśaṃ kumārahaṃtāraṃ yadavocāma tena naḥ ‖*)
अपाक्रमद्धरो वह्नेराह्वयाम (*apākramaddharo vahnerāhvayāma*) … *ādarāt ‖* **NOTE**
समागत्य ततः शीघ्रं तेषामग्निर्हरो भवेत् । इति वार्शेन साम्ना सावकामयत पूर्ववत् ॥ (*samāgatya tataḥ śīghraṃ teṣāmagnirharo bhavet | iti vārśena sāmnā sāvakāmayata pūrvavat ‖*)
एवं गायन् स ऋषिब्रह्महत्यां भार्याजातां त्रसदस्योर्नृपस्य । पिताचवेषां हर आदाय चाग्नेर्गृहान्नीत्वा कशिप् स्थापयंतीं ॥ (*evaṃ gāyan sa ṛṣibrahmahatyāṃ bhāryājātāṃ trasadasyornṛpasya | pitācaveṣāṃ hara ādāya cāgnergṛhānnītvā kaśip sthāpayaṃtīṃ ‖*)

### Printed p. 737

दृष्ट्वा सम्यक् तद्धरस्तोषयित्वा साम्या पश्चाद्योजयामास चाग्निं । ततः सतेजाः संजातोऽभवत्पाकादि पूर्ववत् । एवं शाट्यायनेनोक्तं तांड्यकोक्तमथोच्यते ॥ (*dṛṣṭvā samyak taddharastoṣayitvā sāmyā paścādyojayāmāsa cāgniṃ | tataḥ satejāḥ saṃjāto 'bhavatpākādi pūrvavat | evaṃ śāṭyāyanenoktaṃ tāṃḍyakoktamathocyate ‖*)
वृशः पुरोधा अभवत्रसदस्योर्महीपतेः । स रथं धावयन्नाजा ब्राह्मणस्य कुमारकं ॥ चिच्छेद रथचक्रेण प्रमादात्सोऽब्रवीद्भृशं । पुरोहिते वर्तमाने त्वयि मा हंतिरागता ॥ एषा त्वयापनेतव्या ऋषिमित्यब्रवीन्नृपः । स ऋषिर्वार्शसामान्या तं कुमारमुदजीवयत् ॥ (*vṛśaḥ purodhā abhavatrasadasyormahīpateḥ | sa rathaṃ dhāvayannājā brāhmaṇasya kumārakaṃ ‖ ciccheda rathacakreṇa pramādātso 'bravīdbhṛśaṃ | purohite vartamāne tvayi mā haṃtirāgatā ‖ eṣā tvayāpanetavyā ṛṣimityabravīnnṛpaḥ | sa ṛṣirvārśasāmānyā taṃ kumāramudajīvayat ‖*)

In the Ikṣvāku line there was a king named Tryaruṇa, the son of Trivṛṣṭa. He had a purohita named Vṛśa, the son of Jana and a great Ṛṣi. There was a custom that when the king and the purohita went out together, the purohita should act as charioteer and drive the chariot. Accordingly Vṛśa, holding the reins of the horses, was driving the chariot. On this occasion a Brahmin's boy was playing on the path of the chariot. The wheel of the chariot ran over the boy, and the boy died at once. A dispute arose between the two as to who was a sharer in the sin arising from the death. The king said that the purohita himself, since he was driving the chariot, was the sharer in the sin; the purohita said that the king, since he was the master of the chariot, was the sharer. Thus each began to lay the fault on the other. Then the two put their dispute before the assembly of the Ikṣvākus. There it was decided that the fault was the purohita's. (That the dispute was thus put before the assembly, and that the assembly announced its decision, is not in the Bṛhaddevatā verses quoted earlier.) As soon as it was decided that he was the sharer in the sin, because restraining the speed of the chariot is the duty of the charioteer and Vṛśa, being the charioteer, had not done it, the Ṛṣi received the vision of a sāman-mantra called the Vārśa-sāman, recited that mantra, and by its power brought the dead boy back to life. But he became angry with the Ikṣvākus, who had wrongly laid the fault upon him and pronounced a decision against him, and cursed them: "In their house let vigour and splendour be lost to the fire that is kindled there." And he abandoned them and went away. (There is a Bṛhaddevatā statement that he went to the king of that country and joined him.) As a result of that curse all the splendour of the fire established in the house of the Ikṣvākus was lost. अग्नौ प्रास्तानि हव्यानि न हैपच्यंत कानिचित् (*agnau prāstāni havyāni na haipacyaṃta kānicit*). Because the splendour of the fire was lost, the oblations and the like offered in that fire were not cooked, and since there was no fire in the kitchen either, cooking and the like could not be done.

So they all, in distress, went to the place where Vṛśa was, entreated him, and brought him back. Then, when he again recited the Vārśa-sāman, the mantra he had recited before, the lost splendour of the fire reappeared. (Up to here the story fits the setting. But the same matter is continued and the story is further developed.) Because he had cursed them as soon as he was displeased earlier, the guilt of Brahmin-slaying, dwelling in the form of the wife of Trasadasyu and in the guise of a Piśācī, carried off the splendour of the fire and hid it in her garment. Vṛśa discovered this, freed the haras (the splendour of the fire) from there and joined it again to the fire. At once the fire blazed up and began to cook the oblations and the like offered in it. (The Bṛhaddevatā tells that Vṛśa recited the mantra with reference to the guilt of Brahmin-slaying in the form of a Piśācī. This was quoted earlier.)

The story told so far has been set out as Śāṭyāyana the great Ṛṣi has told it. Now the difference in the part of the story told in the Tāṇḍya-brāhmaṇa will be set out. When King Trasadasyu entreated Vṛśa to become his purohita and remove his guilt of Brahmin-slaying, Vṛśa became his purohita again, and by the power of the Vārśa-sāman he revived the dead boy. Thus the greatness of Vṛśa is praised. This is the setting of the story.

Because there is this introduction in story form, it must be said that in the present mantra the word युवतिः (*yuvatiḥ*) points to the Piśācī woman in the form of Tryaruṇa's wife. How this meaning is to be stated: the Bṛhaddevatā verse itself is the support for it.
निषण्णस्स तया सार्धं आसंद्यां कशिपावपि । तामुपामंतयांचक्रे कमेतं त्वमिति त्वृचा ॥ (*niṣaṇṇassa tayā sārdhaṃ āsaṃdyāṃ kaśipāvapi | tāmupāmaṃtayāṃcakre kametaṃ tvamiti tvṛcā ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. 5-20)
It says that Vṛśa, seated on one seat with that wife of Tryaruṇa in the form of a Piśācī, recited the mantra कमेतं त्वं युवते कुमारं (*kametaṃ tvaṃ yuvate kumāraṃ*) (5-2-2). Since Sāyaṇa there (5-2-2) explains पेषी हिंसिका पिशाचिका सती (*peṣī hiṃsikā piśācikā satī*) **NOTE** as "a young woman who is a Piśācī", it would not be unsuitable to explain the word युवति (*yuvati*) in the first mantra, that is, in the present mantra, also as the Piśācī woman. One kind of meaning can be given: she does not give to the protector, the sacrificer, the fire in the form of a boy (अग्नेरुत्पाद्यमानत्वात् कुमारशब्देन व्यवहारः (*agnerutpādyamānatvāt kumāraśabdena vyavahāraḥ*)), having hidden him. This meaning fits the setting of the story and the explanation given in the Bṛhaddevatā.

### Printed p. 740

But Sāyaṇa has explained the word कुमार (*kumāra*) as the boy killed by the chariot wheel, and said that this young woman, not offering him to his father, keeps him hidden within herself, and that therefore this is the praise. This meaning does not seem so appropriate. Moreover, the second half has not been explained so as to agree with it. Therefore it is proper to explain the word "kumāra" here as Agni. Sāyaṇa's second, alternative explanation supports this meaning. It is this:
माता सर्वस्य निर्मात्री पृथिवी समुब्बं सम्यक् निगूढं गुहा बिभर्ति । न ददाति पित्रे । (*mātā sarvasya nirmātrī pṛthivī samubbaṃ samyak nigūḍhaṃ guhā bibharti | na dadāti pitre |*)
One meaning is that the Earth, maker of all, holds this Agni, who has come into being, secretly, and does not readily offer him to the protector, the sacrificer. Or else he has given another meaning for the word "mother", namely the araṇi. सूक्तस्य आग्नेयत्वात् कुमार इत्यग्निरुच्यते (*sūktasya āgneyatvāt kumāra ityagnirucyate*). Since this sūkta is indicated as Agni's, the word "kumāra" here means Agni. The araṇi is this Agni's mother. Men do not see the splendour of the Agni that lies within the aranī; this is the last explanation given. But how the name "Kumāra" came to be known for Agni must be examined.

In the introduction to this sūkta a passage of the Śatapatha-brāhmaṇa is quoted, and it tells how Agni arose and that "Kumāra" is described as the ninth name of Agni, together with the eight names beginning with Rudra. This same Agni is praised in many contexts in the Ṛk-saṃhitā also as a child and as a boy. For example:

तमिद्दच्छंति जुह्वंस्तमर्वतीर्विश्वान्येकः शृणवद्वचांसि मे । पुरुप्रैषस्ततुरिय्यज्ञसाधनोऽच्छिद्रोतिः शिशुरादत्त सं रभः ॥ (*tamiddacchaṃti juhvaṃstamarvatīrviśvānyekaḥ śṛṇavadvacāṃsi me | purupraiṣastaturiyyajñasādhano 'cchidrotiḥ śiśurādatta saṃ rabhaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-145-3)
स ईं वृषाजनयत्तासु गर्भं स ईं शिशुर्धयति तं रिहंति । (*sa īṃ vṛṣājanayattāsu garbhaṃ sa īṃ śiśurdhayati taṃ rihaṃti |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-35-13)

In these and many other contexts Agni is praised as one who, though in the form of a child, does extraordinary deeds. Besides this, there is room to say that in some other places also the word "kumāra" is a synonym of Agni. Just as the word "kumāra" is explained as Agni in the present sūkta, the meaning can be stated in the same way in those contexts also. For example:

बोधद्यन्ना हरिभ्यां कुमारः साहदेव्यः । अच्छा न हूत उदरं । (*bodhadyannā haribhyāṃ kumāraḥ sāhadevyaḥ | acchā na hūta udaraṃ |*)
(4-15-7)
उत क्या यजता हरी कुमारात्साहदेव्यात् । प्रयता सद्य आ ददे ॥ (*uta kyā yajatā harī kumārātsāhadevyāt | prayatā sadya ā dade ‖*)
(4-15-8)

Here the circumstance is told of Vāmadeva obtaining horses from Kumāra, the son of Sahadeva. It is understood from Sāyaṇa's commentary that this is a sūkta directed to Agni.

सोग्निं तु पंचदशभिरिंद्रं षोडशभिः परैः (*sogniṃ tu paṃcadaśabhiriṃdraṃ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ paraiḥ*)
(Bṛ. De. 4-12)
The Bṛhaddevatā says that the first 15 sūktas in the fourth maṇḍala are directed to Agni. But when telling certain special matters, indicating only the two mantras quoted above, it says:

लिंगोक्तदैवते सूक्ते एके प्रत्यग्निरेवतु । ऋषिबोधदिति द्वाभ्यां स्तौति सोमकमेव तु ॥ (*liṃgoktadaivate sūkte eke pratyagnirevatu | ṛṣibodhaditi dvābhyāṃ stauti somakameva tu ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. 9-129) **NOTE**
(Bṛ. De. 9-12)

Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-13 and 4-14 **NOTE**, the sūktas, are recited in praise of the individual qualities of their respective deities. But only the two mantras बोधद्यन्ना (*bodhadyannā*) **NOTE** and उत त्या यजता (*uta tyā yajatā*) are said by some to be directed to Agni and by others to be addressed to Soma-ka. This amounts to saying that stating a definite meaning for these two mantras is an effort. On the basis of Vedic statements such as this, "kumāra" here can be explained as Agni. And the two horses indicate the Aśvin deities; the word "sahadeva" can be explained as the presence of the deity. The two horses are the Aśvin deities themselves, who reflect day and night or the bright and dark fortnights. Such explanations in this context have been given by some scholars. But if "kumāra" is explained as Agni in these quoted mantras, the other words too must be given purports suited to it. This is laborious. Without the support of exact Vedic statements this meaning cannot be accepted. Even so, it is understood from the very statement of the author of the Bṛhaddevatā that the meaning of these mantras is deep. Therefore explaining it as Agni is in a way proper too.

To explain the word युवति (*yuvati*) as the Piśācī woman is one way. Or उषस्संदर्भमावुदु (*uṣassaṃdarbhamāvudu*) **NOTE** is another way. But if it is said that according to the setting of the story it can be explained simply as the Piśācī woman, that too is not exact. Sāyaṇa himself has given three kinds of meaning for the word युवति (*yuvati*). Therefore to explain युवति (*yuvati*) as Uṣas also would be appropriate in the present case. How, will be told in the special topics of the next mantra.

### Printed p. 741

Concerning the explanation of this Ṛk, the scholar Wilson has spoken as follows:

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
According to what is no doubt the most accurate interpretation of
this verse, and of those which follow, they contain only a metaphorically
obscure allusion to the lighting of the sacrificial fire : the mother is the two
pieces of touch-wood. which retain fire. the child, and will not sponta-
neously give it up to the father, the yajamana, until forced by attrition :
till then, also, people, the priests. do not behold it, but they see it when burst-
ing into ignition : this however, has not satisfied the commentators, and a
curious and strange legend has been devised for the interpretation of the
text, or has been perhaps, applied to it by way of expianation, having
been previously current : it is more probably, however, suggested by, than
suggestive of, the verses : Sayana quotes the Shatyayana Brahmana as the
authority : the story is this : Raja Tryaruna, the son of Trivrisha cf the
race of Ikshwakus had for his Purohita Vrsina the son of Jara : it was the
custom, it is said, when a Raja and his Purohit went out in the same
chariot, that the latter should drive. and on an occasion of this kind, the
chariot went over a Brahman boy who was playing in the road, and killed
him : a dispute ensued between the Raja and the priest as to which was
the murderer, the former accusing the latter because he was drivipg, the
the Purohit retorting, that as the chariot was the Raja's, he was the
responsible person : they referred the matter to an assembly of the
Ikshwakus, who decided against the Purohit : Vrsia restored the boy to
life by the prayer thenceforth called after him the Varsha-samaan, but
being offended with the Ikshwakus for what he considered their partiality,
fire thenceforth ceased to perform its functions in their dwellings and the
ccoking of their food and other offices ceased : attributing this to the
displeasure of the Rishi, the Ikshwakus respecfully invoked his presence,
and with the same mantra. he prayed that the energy of fire would be
restored to them, which accordingly took place : this energy or activity is
designated by the unusual term of Haras, Agner haras : so far the legend
is intelligible, but what follows is rather obscure : Sayana proceeds : so

### Printed p. 742

singing, the Rishi having seen distinctly Brahmanicide become the wife of
the king Trasadasyu, in the garb of a Pishachi, and that she, having taken
the Haras away from the fire-chamber, was concealing it in her regal
clothing (kashipau?) he, having propitiated that Haras by Varsha Sama ,
re-united it with Agni, upon which the offices of fire, in cooking and the
like, were discharged as before : Sayana adds to his version a quotation
from the Tandya which stops with the restarotion of the boy to life : Niti-
manjari cites the legend from the Brihad-devata, the first part of which is
the same as that given above but there is some slight variation in the con
clusion : after the decision against the Purohit, this authority continues, the
Atharvan having seen (or composed) the Angirasa mantras, restored the boy
to life, but beeing in wrath, desertedthe king, and went to another country :
upon his departure, the Haras or function of Agni ceased, and there were
no more burnt-offerings : the Raja, being much distressed, went to the
Rishi, and pacified and brought him back, and prevailed upon him to
become his Purohit once more : still the fire withheld its activity, until the
Rishi discovered that the queen was in reality a Pishachi, with whom the
Haras had associated, and was seated on the throne with her, and hidden
in her robe : on discovering this, the Rishi repeated the second star za ef **NOTE**
this Suktha, " Young mother, etc.,," to which Haras, in the form of
a boy, replied: the Rishi then recited the ninth stanza. "Agni shines etc."
on which the flame burst forth and consumed the Pishachi, after which
things went on as before : if there be any meaning in this legend, it may
possibly intimate some quarrel between the princes and priests, and a
consequent temporary discontinuance of worship with fire.
