> पूजनीयारणिरेनं जजान । अजनयत् । तदेवाद । गर्भः शिशोर्ग्राहकोऽरण्याः
> संबंधी गर्भो हि यस्मात्तूर्विः शरदो गताननेकान् संवत्सरान्वर्ध ।
> ववृधे । अहं च ततो जातमपश्यं । यद्यस्मान्मातारणिरसूत । उदपादयत् ।
> राजकुमार पक्षे हे युवते भूदेवि: कमेतं कुमारं पेषी सती बिभर्षि ।
> अवशिष्टं कुमारजननपरतया योज्यं । एवमुत्तरत्रापि कुमाराग्निहरसोः परत्वेन
> यथोचितं व्याख्येयं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Because Agni is being produced here, he is spoken of by the word कुमार (*kumāra*) ("boy"). "O young woman, which boy is this whom you, being a पेषी (*peṣī*) (a harming, demonic woman), carry?" So the great seer named Vṛśa speaks of Agni, who has been hidden by Kaśipu.**NOTE** The meaning is that, since the boy was not produced by you, your carrying him is improper. The great, venerable महिषी (*mahiṣī*), the araṇi (fire-stick), gave birth to him. गर्भः (*garbhaḥ*): the embryo, the seizer of the child, belonging to the araṇi, has grown through many past autumns (years); and I saw him born when the mother, the araṇi, brought him forth. On the alternative of the king's son: "O young woman, the Earth-goddess, you, being a पेषी (*peṣī*), carry which boy?" The rest is to be construed as referring to the birth of the boy. Likewise in the following verses the explanation is to be made as fits, referring to Kumāra, Agni or Hara.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- युवते (*yuvate*)—O young woman
- पेषी (*peṣī*)—possessing a nature of harming
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- कं एतं कुमारं (*kaṃ etaṃ kumāraṃ*)—which this boy
- बिभर्षि (*bibharṣi*)—are you nourishing? (who is this boy you are nourishing?)
- महिषी (*mahiṣī*)—the venerable mother
- जजान (*jajāna*)—gave birth (to him)
- गर्भः (*garbhaḥ*)—the embryo of this son
- पूर्वी शरदः (*pūrvī śaradaḥ*)—for many years
- ववर्ध हि (*vavardha hi*)—grew indeed
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- माता (*mātā*)—the mother
- असूत (*asūta*)—gave birth (then)
- जातं (*jātaṃ*)—this son who was born
- अपश्यं (*apaśyaṃ*)—I saw

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O young woman, who is this boy that you, who have a nature of harming, are nourishing? The venerable great mother bore him. The embryo of this son grew for many years. I saw this son who was born when his mother brought him forth.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Young mother, what boy is this whom you, (become) a malevolent spirit, foster? The mighty (queen) has given him birth; the embryo has

### Printed p. 744
thriven through many years : I have seen him born as the mother brought him forth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this mantra Sāyaṇa says अग्नेरुत्पाद्यमानत्वात् कुमारशब्देन व्यवहारः (*agnerutpādyamānatvāt kumāraśabdena vyavahāraḥ*), that is, because he is being produced, Agni is here denoted by the word कुमार (*kumāra*); and he has explained the word युवति (*yuvati*) as a demonic (paiśācī) woman. But further on in this mantra there is the description महषी जजान (*mahaṣī jajāna*), "the venerable mother bore this son", and गर्भः पूर्विः शरदः ववर्ध हि (*garbhaḥ pūrviḥ śaradaḥ vavardha hi*), "this embryo grew for many years". Even if, in keeping with the setting of the story, one explains it here as a demonic woman, that demonic woman, who was the wife of Trayaṇa,**NOTE** only hid Agni; she neither bore him nor carried him. Therefore it is proper here to explain the word युवति (*yuvati*) as Uṣas, the mother of Agni.
एता उ त्याः प्रत्यदृश्रन् पुरस्ताज्योतिर्यच्छंतीरुषसो विभातीः । अजीजनन्सूर्यं यज्ञमग्निमपाचीनं तमो अगादजुष्टं ॥ (*etā u tyāḥ pratyadṛśran purastājyotiryacchaṃtīruṣaso vibhātīḥ | ajījanansūryaṃ yajñamagnimapācīnaṃ tamo agādajuṣṭaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-78-3)
In passages such as this it is stated explicitly that Uṣas is the mother of Agni. Moreover, in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa passage quoted earlier in the introduction to this sūkta, Agni, from Uṣas, became **NOTE** the one marked with the name Kumāra, and obtained the other eight names, Rudra and the rest; this too is stated.
एषा दिवो दुहिता प्रत्यदर्शि व्युच्छंती युवतिः शुक्रवासाः । विश्वस्येशाना पार्थिवस्य वस्व उषो अद्येह सुभगे व्युच्छ ॥ (*eṣā divo duhitā pratyadarśi vyucchaṃtī yuvatiḥ śukravāsāḥ | viśvasyeśānā pārthivasya vasva uṣo adyeha subhage vyuccha ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-7)
In many mantras like this, Uṣas's youthfulness and the beauty befitting it are described. How the epithet पेषी (*peṣī*) applies to Uṣas, who is Agni's mother and a young woman, is something to be examined. If it be said that this epithet is proper for a demonic woman but does not fit Uṣas, the answer is that one may freely say that पेषी (*peṣī*) is an epithet describing the nature of Uṣas.
एतद्वेदुत वीर्यंमिंद्र चकर्थ पौंस्यं । स्त्रियं युद्दु र्हणायुवं वधीर्दुहितरं दिवः ॥ (*etadveduta vīryaṃmiṃdra cakartha pauṃsyaṃ | striyaṃ yuddu rhaṇāyuvaṃ vadhīrduhitaraṃ divaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-30-8)

### Printed p. 745
दिवश्चिद्वा दुहितरं महान् महियमानां । उषासमिंद्र सं पिणक् ॥ (*divaścidvā duhitaraṃ mahān mahiyamānāṃ | uṣāsamiṃdra saṃ piṇak ‖*) (4-30-9)
This Indra is mighty. He struck forcefully Uṣas, the daughter of the heavenly world. Indra thoroughly crushed Uṣas, who was intent on her own self-praise.
अपोषा अनसः सरत्संपिष्टादह बिभ्युषी । नि यत्सीं शिश्नधद्वृषा ॥ (*apoṣā anasaḥ saratsaṃpiṣṭādaha bibhyuṣī | ni yatsīṃ śiśnadhadvṛṣā ‖*)
एतदस्या अनः शये सुसंपिष्टं विपाश्या । ससार सीं परावतः ॥ (*etadasyā anaḥ śaye susaṃpiṣṭaṃ vipāśyā | sasāra sīṃ parāvataḥ ‖*) (4-30-10, 11)
As soon as Uṣas's chariot was shattered, she fled in fear of Indra. The chariot she left behind remained there shattered. In this way Uṣas, harmed by Indra, is extolled in mantras with the epithets सं पिणक् (*saṃ piṇak*) and सु संपिष्ट (*su saṃpiṣṭa*). सं पिणक् (*saṃ piṇak*) states her condition; सु संपिष्ट (*su saṃpiṣṭa*) states the condition of her chariot. Therefore in the present mantra too the epithet पेषी (*peṣī*) may state the harmed state of Uṣas. If this meaning fits, one may say that it is described that Uṣas, harmed by Indra, carried and nourished her son Agni, that Agni blazes up as soon as Uṣas appears, and that afterwards the sacrificer sees Agni.

> अहमस्मा अग्नयेmमृतमविनाश्यमृतत्वसाधनं ना विपृक्वत्सर्वतो व्याप्तं हविः
> स्तोत्रं वा ददानः । दातास्मि । मामनिंद्राः । इंद्रः परमैश्वयोऽग्निः । तद्रहिता

> कृणवन् । किं कुर्युः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

हिरण्यदंतं (*hiraṇyadaṃtaṃ*): Agni endowed with flames that stand in the place of teeth resembling gold; शुचिवर्णं (*śucivarṇaṃ*): of blazing colour; आयुधा (*āyudhā*): weapons, that is, sparks or flames standing in the place of weapons, which he fashions (मिमानं (*mimānaṃ*)). Such an Agni may I see (अपश्यं (*apaśyaṃ*) glossed पश्येयं (*paśyeyaṃ*)) आरात् (*ārāt*), nearby, क्षेत्रात् (*kṣetrāt*), in the place. Thus Vṛśa wishes.**NOTE** "I am the giver, to this Agni, of अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*), imperishable, the means of immortality, विपृक्वत् (*vipṛkvat*), pervading everywhere, oblation or praise." इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*) is supreme lordship, Agni; those devoid of it are अनिंद्राः (*aniṃdrāḥ*), the meaning being that they do not worship Indra. The अनुक्थाः (*anukthāḥ*), those who do not praise, who do not extol Indra: what can they do to me?

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हिरण्यदंतं (*hiraṇyadaṃtaṃ*)—possessing flames shining like teeth made of gold
- शुचिवर्णं (*śucivarṇaṃ*)—of radiant colour
- आयुधा (*āyudhā*)—sparks like weapons
- मिमानं (*mimānaṃ*)—producing; the Agni
- आरात् (*ārāt*)—nearby
- क्षेत्रात् (*kṣetrāt*)—in the place
- अपश्यं (*apaśyaṃ*)—I have seen
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—to this Agni
- अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—that which brings immortality
- विपृक्वत् (*vipṛkvat*)—that which pervades everywhere; the oblation
- ददानः (*dadānaḥ*)—offering
- मां (*māṃ*)—me
- अनिंद्राः (*aniṃdrāḥ*)—those who do not worship Agni, who has supreme lordship
- अनुक्थाः (*anukthāḥ*)—those who do not offer him praise; the unbelievers
- किं कृणवन् (*kiṃ kṛṇavan*)—what indeed can they do?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I have seen, in a nearby place, Agni, possessing flames shining like teeth made of gold, of radiant colour, producing sparks like weapons. Unbelievers, who do not worship Agni, endowed with supreme lordship, and who do not offer him praise, cannot harm me, who offer to such an Agni the oblation that brings immortality and pervades everywhere.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
I have seen him from a near place, golden-toothed, bright-coloured wielding (flames-like) weapons, (when) offering to him the ambrosial, all-diffusing (oblation) : what can those who acknowledge not Indra, who repeat not his praise, do unto me?

### Printed p. 747

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the present mantra Agni is praised with epithets such as हिरण्यदंतं (*hiraṇyadaṃtaṃ*). But here it is necessary to understand the import of the word अनिंद्राः (*aniṃdrāḥ*). Sāyaṇa's explanation of this word is as follows.
इंद्रः परमैश्वर्यः अग्निः । तद्रहिताः अनिंद्राः । इंद्रमयजंत इत्यर्थः । (*iṃdraḥ paramaiśvaryaḥ agniḥ | tadrahitāḥ aniṃdrāḥ | iṃdramayajaṃta ityarthaḥ |*)
The word इंद्र (*iṃdra*) means supreme lordship. Because he is endowed with this lordship, Agni too is denoted by the word इंद्र (*iṃdra*). Therefore अनिंद्राः (*aniṃdrāḥ*) here means those who are not worshippers of Indra, that is, non-Vedic people who are not worshippers of Agni. This explanation is one of the many explanations of the word इंद्र (*iṃdra*) given by the Nirukta authors; all of them have been set out in detail earlier. But since Agni is denoted by the word इंद्र (*iṃdra*), the precise meaning of this word must be understood; afterwards the identity of Indra and Agni may be examined. The meaning of the word इंद्र (*iṃdra*) was explained even before the Nirukta authors.
इंधो ह वै नामैष योऽयं दक्षिणेऽक्षन् पुरुषस्तं वा एतमिंधं संतमिंद्र इत्याचक्षते परोक्षेणैव परोक्षप्रिया इव हि देवाः प्रत्यक्षद्विषः । (*iṃdho ha vai nāmaiṣa yo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣan puruṣastaṃ vā etamiṃdhaṃ saṃtamiṃdra ityācakṣate parokṣeṇaiva parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ pratyakṣadviṣaḥ |*) (Śa. Brā. 14-6-11-2; Bṛ. U. 4-2-2)
The person in the right eye is denoted by the word इंद्र (*iṃdra*) because of his special quality of blazing. (This is the quality of Agni, that is, of brightness.) It is stated that because he is endowed with brightness, the knowing ones designate this person as Indra. The same is stated more fully elsewhere as follows.
स योऽयं मध्ये प्राणः । एष एवेंद्र स्तानेष प्राणान्मध्यत इंद्रियेणैंध यदैंध तस्मादिंद इंथो ह वै तमिंद्र इत्याचक्षते ॥ (*sa yo 'yaṃ madhye prāṇaḥ | eṣa eveṃdra stāneṣa prāṇānmadhyata iṃdriyeṇaiṃdha yadaiṃdha tasmādiṃda iṃtho ha vai tamiṃdra ityācakṣate ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 6-1-1-2)
This vital breath in the middle of the body is Indra. This principle supplies vitality and brightness to the other vital breaths of the body. Because it thus supplies brightness to the other beings, it is said that this principle is denoted by the word इंद्र (*iṃdra*). The same meaning is given in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa also, in "आस्मिन् ना इदमिंद्रियं" (*"āsmin nā idamiṃdriyaṃ"*) and so on (Tai. Brā. 2-2-10-4). Besides, about fifteen kinds of explanation by Yāska were quoted and set out earlier.
In this way the root इंद् (*iṃd*) is the basic form of the words that give the meaning of blazing brightness. The word is used not only for the well-known Indra but also for other deities endowed with brightness.

### Printed p. 748
अभूदुषा इंद्रतमा मघोन्यजीजनत्सुविताय श्रवांसि । वि दिवो देवी दुहिता दधात्यंगिरस्तमा सुकृते वसूनि ॥ (*abhūduṣā iṃdratamā maghonyajījanatsuvitāya śravāṃsi | vi divo devī duhitā dadhātyaṃgirastamā sukṛte vasūni ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-29-3)
Here Sāyaṇa has explained इंद्रतमा (*iṃdratamā*) as सर्वस्य ईश्वरतमा (*sarvasya īśvaratamā*), but, as stated above in Brāhmaṇa passages such as the Śatapatha, the meaning "exceedingly bright" is the natural one here too. Likewise in
इंद्रतमा हि धिष्ण्या मरुत्तमा दस्रा दंसिष्ठा रथ्या रथीतमा । (*iṃdratamā hi dhiṣṇyā maruttamā dasrā daṃsiṣṭhā rathyā rathītamā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-182-2)
where it is used as an epithet of the Aśvin deities, this same meaning has to be given. Indra too, because he has this quality of brightness, is described as doing work that is carried out by Agni. For example:
इंद्रः समत्सु यजमानमार्यं................ । धक्षन्न विश्वं ततृषाणमोषति न्यर्शसानमोषति ॥ (*iṃdraḥ samatsu yajamānamāryaṃ................ | dhakṣanna viśvaṃ tatṛṣāṇamoṣati nyarśasānamoṣati ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-130-8)
It is described that Indra burned to ashes the asuras and others who were without rites, and their followers. (Burning is the work of Agni.) And:
भीमस्तुविष्मान् चर्षणिभ्य आतपः शिशीते वज्रं तेजसे न वंसगः । (*bhīmastuviṣmān carṣaṇibhya ātapaḥ śiśīte vajraṃ tejase na vaṃsagaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-55-1)
Here too आतसः (*ātasaḥ*) is an epithet showing Indra's quality; it means one who causes heat all around. This too is the work of Agni and is an epithet of Indra. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-31-10, although प्रश्नॆस्य रेतसः (*praśnèsya retasaḥ*) is a description of Indra, in this context it states the nature of Āditya. That is, one may also say that Indra himself has the quality of Āditya. Therefore one may also say that identity between Āditya, a transformed form of Agni, and Indra is stated. Likewise, just as Indra is said to be one who performs the works done by Agni, who is bright and who burns enemies, so Agni too is often described as one who performs the works assigned to Indra.
प्र नू महित्वं वृषभस्य वोचं यं पूरवो वृत्रहणं सचंते । वैश्वानरो दस्युमग्निर्जघन्वा अधूनोत्कृष्टा अव शंबरं भेत् ॥ (*pra nū mahitvaṃ vṛṣabhasya vocaṃ yaṃ pūravo vṛtrahaṇaṃ sacaṃte | vaiśvānaro dasyumagnirjaghanvā adhūnotkṛṣṭā ava śaṃbaraṃ bhet ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-59-6)

### Printed p. 749

in which Agni is described as the slayer of Vṛtra and the splitter of the asura Śambara. Both of these are well-known deeds of Indra. Likewise, in तमु त्वा वृत्रहंतमं........ (*tamu tvā vṛtrahaṃtamaṃ........*) and the like (1-78-4), Agni is described in many places in this way. Moreover, there are also plenty of passages that state outright the identity of Indra and Agni. For example:

अथ यत्रैतत्त्वदीपो भवति । उच्चैर्धूमः परमया जूत्या बल्पलीति तर्हि हैष भवतींद्रः ॥ (*atha yatraitattvadīpo bhavati | uccairdhūmaḥ paramayā jūtyā balpalīti tarhi haiṣa bhavatīṃdraḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 2-3-2-11).

When this same Agni is fully ablaze, pervading with his flames, spreading smoke, and rushing swiftly upward, people praise him as Indra.

स उपहवमिष्ट्वा भक्षयति मधु हुतमिंद्रतमेग्नाविति । (*sa upahavamiṣṭvā bhakṣayati madhu hutamiṃdratamegnāviti |*) (Śa. Brā. 14-2-2-42).

In sentences of this kind Agni is praised as the most excellent Indra. Since the identity of Indra and Agni is thus described in many places, the word अनिंद्राः (*aniṃdrāḥ*), a specific designation of Agni, is appropriate in the present context.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> क्षेत्रा॑दपश्यं सनु॒तश्चरं॑तं सु॒मद्यू॒थं न पु॒रु शोभ॑मानं ।  
> न ता अ॑गृभ्र॒न्न ज॑निष्ट॒ हि षः पलि॑क्की॒रिद्यु॑व॒तयो॑ भवंति ॥ ४ ॥

> *kṣetrādapaśyaṃ sanutaścaraṃtaṃ sumadyūthaṃ na puru śobhamānaṃ |*  
> *na tā agṛbhranna janiṣṭa hi ṣaḥ palikkīridyuvatayo bhavaṃti ‖ 4 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> क्षेत्रात् । अपश्यं । सनुतरिति । चरंतं । सुमत् । यूथं । न । पुरु । शोभमानं ।  
> न । ताः । अगृभ्रन् । अजनिष्ट । हि । सः । पलिक्किः । इत् । युव तयः । भवंति ॥ ४ ॥

> *kṣetrāt | apaśyaṃ | sanutariti | caraṃtaṃ | sumat | yūthaṃ | na | puru | śobhamānaṃ |*  
> *na | tāḥ | agṛbhran | ajaniṣṭa | hi | saḥ | palikkiḥ | it | yuva tayaḥ | bhavaṃti ‖ 4 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अहं वृश इदानीं क्षेत्रात् क्षेत्रे सुनुतः । अंतर्हितनामैतत् । निगूढं
> चरंतमरण्यां यूथं न गवां समूहमिव सुमत्सयमेव पुरु बहु शोभमा..

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"I, Vṛśa, now see him from the field, in the field." सनुतः (*sanutaḥ*) is a name meaning "hidden". He moves concealed in the forest, like a herd of cows, of his own accord, shining greatly (the text breaks off at शोभमा.. (*śobhamā..*); the sentence continues on the next page). **NOTE**

### Printed p. 750

> नमपश्यं । पश्यामि । पुरा हरसः पिशाच्याक्रमणकाले ता ज्वाला निर्वीर्या
> नागृभ्रन् । नागृह्णंत नराः । इदानीं सोऽग्निरजनिष्ट हि । हरसा प्रादुरभूत्खलु । अत
> एव हेतोः पलिक्कीरित्पलिक्ष्यः पलिता जीर्णा ज्वाला एवेदानीं युवतयो भवंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

He completes the verb अपश्यं (*apaśyaṃ*): "I see". Formerly, at the time when Piśācī attacked by force, those flames were powerless and men did not seize them. Now that Agni has been born, he has indeed appeared by force. For that very reason the grey, aged flames now become young.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- क्षेत्रात् (*kṣetrāt*)—from one region (to another region)
- सनुतः (*sanutaḥ*)—secretly
- सुमत् (*sumat*)—of his own accord
- चरंतं (*caraṃtaṃ*)—moving about
- यूथं न (*yūthaṃ na*)—like a herd of cattle
- पुरु (*puru*)—greatly
- शोभमानं (*śobhamānaṃ*)—shining; (such) Agni
- अपश्यं (*apaśyaṃ*)—I see
- ताः (*tāḥ*)—those flames that had grown before
- न अगृभ्रन् (*na agṛbhran*)—no one could see
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Agni
- अजनिष्ट हि (*ajaniṣṭa hi*)—has been born again
- पलिक्कीरित् (*palikkīrit*)—those same flames that had reached old age
- युवतयः (*yuvatayaḥ*)—having attained youth
- भवंति (*bhavaṃti*)—have become

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I see Agni, who moves of himself from one region to another like a herd of cattle and shines exceedingly. No one could see those flames of his that had grown before. That same Agni has been born again. Those same flames that had reached old age have become young again.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
I have seen him passing secretly from place (to place) like a herd (of cattle), shining brightly of his own accord : they apprehended not those (flames of his), but he has (again) been born, and they which had become grey-haired are (once more; young.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सनुतः (*sanutaḥ*)—This word is read among hidden names such as निण्यं (*niṇyaṃ*) and स्वसः (*svasaḥ*) (Ni. 3-25). It is used in the sense of something secret, ordinarily not coming within the view of others. The word is used especially often in passages praying "drive off the wicked and keep out of sight".

यूयं देवाः प्रमतिर्यायनोजोयूयं द्वेषांसि सनुतर्युयोत (*yūyaṃ devāḥ pramatiryāyanojoyūyaṃ dveṣāṃsi sanutaryuyota*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-29-2)

आरे द्वेषांसि सनुतर्दधामायाम प्रांचो यजमानमच्छ । (*āre dveṣāṃsi sanutardadhāmāyāma prāṃco yajamānamaccha |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-45-5)

### Printed p. 751

स्वैः ष एवैर्मुमुरत्पोप्यं रयिं सनुतर्धेहि तं ततः (*svaiḥ ṣa evairmumuratpopyaṃ rayiṃ sanutardhehi taṃ tataḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-97-3);
विदानासो वसवो राध्यस्या राष्ट्चिद्वेषस्सनुतर्युयोत (*vidānāso vasavo rādhyasyā rāṣṭcidveṣassanutaryuyota*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-77-6).

It is a peculiarity that the word is used just in such prayers: "keep the hostile far away". Of these, however, only for the word सनुतः (*sanutaḥ*) in mantra 5-45-5 has Sāyaṇa given a different meaning. Showing it as a word ending in ṛ, सनुतृ (*sanutṛ*), he explains सनुतः द्वेषांसि (*sanutaḥ dveṣāṃsi*) as संभक्त्वान् शत्रून् (*saṃbhaktvān śatrūn*), that is, enemies who desire to share in our wealth. There too, it would not be wrong if he had given the same meaning that he gives elsewhere for सनुतः (*sanutaḥ*) as an indeclinable; but saying संभक्त्वान् (*saṃbhaktvān*) is not inappropriate either.

In the present mantra the hidden movement of Agni is described. The purport is: one who moves in a way that is visible to no one.

सुमत् (*sumat*)—The word सुमत् (*sumat*) means "of oneself" (Ni. 6-22). It is used in the sense of carrying out something oneself, without the prompting of others. The author of the Nirukta explains the sense of this word by citing the mantra उप प्रागात्सुमन्मेधायि (*upa prāgātsumanmedhāyi*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-162-7). In उप प्रागात्सुमत् (*upa prāgātsumat*) the prayer is: may the object I desire come and join me of its own accord. That this word is also used in the senses of auspicious, beautiful and the like has been stated earlier.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> के मे॑ मर्य॒कं वि य॑वंत॒ गोभि॒र्न येषां॑ गो॒पा  ॒॑॑
> अर॑णश्चि॒दास॑ ।  
> य ईं॑ जगृ॒भुरव॒ ते सृ॑जं॒त्वाजा॑ति प॒श्व उप॑ नश्चि कि॒त्वान् ॥ ५ ॥

> *ke me maryakaṃ vi yavaṃta gobhirna yeṣāṃ gopā*  
> *araṇaścidāsa |*  
> *ya īṃ jagṛbhurava te sṛjaṃtvājāti paśva upa naści kitvān ‖ 5 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> के । मे । मर्यकं । वि । यवंत । गोभिः । न । येषां ! गोपाः । अरणः । चित् ।  
> आस ।  
> ये । ईं । जगृभुः । अव । ते । सृजंतु । आ । अजाति । पश्वः । उप । नः । चिकित्वान् ॥

> *ke | me | maryakaṃ | vi | yavaṃta | gobhiḥ | na | yeṣāṃ ! gopāḥ | araṇaḥ | cit |*  
> *āsa |*  
> *ye | īṃ | jagṛbhuḥ | ava | te | sṛjaṃtu | ā | ajāti | paśvaḥ | upa | naḥ | cikitvān ‖*

### Printed p. 752

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> के मे मदीयं मर्यकं मर्त्यसंघं राष्ट्रं गोभिः सह वि यवंत ।
> वियुक्तमकुर्वन् । गा भृत्यांश्च व्ययोजयन् । येषां गोपा अस्माकं
> गोपयितारणश्चिदभिगंता नास । बभूव । सोऽयमग्निः । ये द्वेषिण ईमेनं
> जनसंघं राष्ट्रं जगृभुः ! गृह्णंति । तेऽव सृजंतु । नश्यंतु । किंच चिकित्वान्
> चेतनावानस्मद्विषयज्ञानवानग्निर्नोऽस्माकं पश्वः पशूनुपाजाति । उपागच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Who have separated my मर्यकं (*maryakaṃ*), my host of mortals, my realm, from the cows?" They made it separated; they parted the cows and the servants. Those whose protector, our guardian, an approacher, was not there, namely this Agni. Those enemies who seize this host of people, this realm, let them perish (अव सृजंतु (*ava sṛjaṃtu*) = नश्यंतु (*naśyaṃtu*)). Moreover, Agni, चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*), the possessor of awareness, who knows our situation, comes to our cattle (पश्वः (*paśvaḥ*) = *paśūn*), approaches them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- येषां (*yeṣāṃ*)—of whom: my servants and cattle
- गोपाः (*gopāḥ*)—protector
- अरणश्चित् (*araṇaścit*)—as one who confronts (the enemies)
- न आस (*na āsa*)—was not there; such
- मे (*me*)—belonging to me
- मर्यकं (*maryakaṃ*)—people (in the form of servants)
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—from the cows
- के (*ke*)—who
- वि यवंत (*vi yavaṃta*)—have separated
- ये (*ye*)—which enemies
- ईं (*īṃ*)—this host of servants
- जगृभुः (*jagṛbhuḥ*)—have seized
- ते (*te*)—they
- अव सृजंतु (*ava sṛjaṃtu*)—let them meet destruction
- चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*)—Agni, who knows our distress
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- पश्वः (*paśvaḥ*)—cattle (to protect)
- उप आजाति (*upa ājāti*)—let him come near

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When Agni, the protector of my servants and cattle and the one who confronts enemies, was not near, who bound my people and separated them from the cows? May the enemies who have bound this host of my servants perish. May Agni, who knows our troubles, come near us to protect our cattle.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Who have disunited my people from cattle? Was there not for them an invincible protector ? May they who have seized upon that (people) perish, for he who knows (our wishes) approaches to (protect) the cattle.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अरण (*araṇa*)—The word अरण (*araṇa*) is formed from the root रण् (*raṇ*) and indicates its negation. The word रण (*raṇa*) is used in the sense of joy and also in the sense of battle.

कृते चिदत्र मरुतो रणंतानवद्यासः शुचयः पावकाः । (*kṛte cidatra maruto raṇaṃtānavadyāsaḥ śucayaḥ pāvakāḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-57-5)

In mantras of this kind it is a word indicating a sound of joy. In many places it is a synonym of battle. Therefore the word अरण (*araṇa*) indicates the absence of joy. The author of the Nirukta

### Printed p. 753

cites the mantra
नहि ग्रभायारणः सुशेवोऽन्योदर्यो मनसा मंतवा उ । (*nahi grabhāyāraṇaḥ suśevo 'nyodaryo manasā maṃtavā u |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-4-8)
(Ni. 3-2) and states only the context of the use of this word. In the mantra cited by Sāyaṇa, the word means अरममाणः (*aramamāṇaḥ*), one who neither rejoices himself nor gladdens others. The sense is that another's son does not become a source of joy. Or, because it gives this very sense, it can also mean an enemy. The word is used in this sense too. For example:

इम इंद्र भरतस्य पुत्रा अपपित्वं चिकितुर्न प्रपित्वं । हिन्वंत्यश्वमरणं न नित्यं ज्यावाजं परि णयंत्याज् ॥ (*ima iṃdra bharatasya putrā apapitvaṃ cikiturna prapitvaṃ | hinvaṃtyaśvamaraṇaṃ na nityaṃ jyāvājaṃ pari ṇayaṃtyāj ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-53-24)

O Indra, these sons of Bharata desire separation from the Vasiṣṭhas, not unity. In this mantra, whose purport is that they are always ready to fight them like perpetual enemies, the word अरण (*araṇa*) means an enemy. Because he is not a source of joy, there are also contexts in which it is a synonym for a non-giver:

वेशं वा नित्यं वरुणारणं वा यत्सीमागश्च कृमा शिश्रथस्तत् । (*veśaṃ vā nityaṃ varuṇāraṇaṃ vā yatsīmāgaśca kṛmā śiśrathastat |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-85-7)

Here, for the word अरण (*araṇa*), one meaning, "soundless", and another, "non-giver", are stated as alternatives. Thus, although meanings are given according to context, the root remains the root रण् (*raṇ*), which means joy. The absence of joy is the purport of the word अरण (*araṇa*). In the present Ṛk, the meaning अभिगंता (*abhigaṃtā*) may be taken to imply one who confronts and strikes enemies.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> व॒सां राजा॑नं वस॒तिं जना॑ना॒मरा॑तयो॒ नि द॑धु॒र्मत्ये॑षु ।  
> ब्रह्मा॒ण्यत्रे॒रव॒ तं सृ॑जंतु निंदि॒तारो॒ निंद्या॑सो भवंतु ॥

> *vasāṃ rājānaṃ vasatiṃ janānāmarātayo ni dadhurmatyeṣu |*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वसां वसतां प्राणिनां राजानं स्वामिनं जनानां प्राणिनां वसतिमावासभूतं त्र्यरुणमुक्तलक्षणमग्निं वारातयो नि दॆधुः । अगोपयन् । मर्त्येषु
> लोकेषु मध्यॆ । अत्रेरत्रिगोत्रस्य वृशस्य ब्रह्माणि मंत्राः स्तोत्राणि वा तं
> कुमारमग्निं वाव सृजंतु । अथवात्रेरत्रिगोत्रस्य कुमारं ब्रह्माणि । यद्वा! वृशस्य
> ब्रह्माण्यत्रेरत्रिगोत्रं ॥ कर्मणि षष्ठी ॥ तं कुमारमव सृजंतु । विसृजंतु ।
> निंदितारोऽस्मन्निंदका निंद्यासोऽस्माभिरिंद्या भवंतु । अत्रेर्ब्रह्माणीत्येतदुपजीव्य वृशमप्यात्रेयं वदंति । आत्रेयः कुमार इति पक्षे स एव प्राणमयमात्मानमवसृजंत्यित्याशास्त्रे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

वसां (*vasāṃ*) means of the dwelling beings; "king" is the lord; वसतिं (*vasatiṃ*) is the abode of the people, living beings. This is Agni, of the characteristic described as त्र्यरुण (*tryaruṇa*), or else the enemies नि दधुः (*ni dadhuḥ*), hid him. मर्त्येषु (*martyeṣu*) means among the worlds. अत्रेः (*atreḥ*): the ब्रह्माणि (*brahmāṇi*), the mantras or hymns, of Vṛśa of the Atri lineage, let them set that Kumāra, Agni, free (अव सृजंतु (*ava sṛjaṃtu*)). Or else the prayers are of the Kumāra of the Atri lineage. Or else the prayers of Vṛśa regard the Atri lineage as the object, with the genitive in the sense of the accusative (कर्मणि षष्ठी (*karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī*)): let them release that Kumāra. निंदितारः (*niṃditāraḥ*) are those who revile us; let them become निंद्यासः (*niṃdyāsaḥ*), reviled by us. Relying on *atrerbrahmāṇi*, they call Vṛśa also Ātreya. On the view that the Kumāra is Ātreya, they release his own vital self (*prāṇamayamātmānaṃ*). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वसां (*vasāṃ*)—for living beings
- राजानं (*rājānaṃ*)—the lord
- जनानां (*janānāṃ*)—for all humans
- वसतिं (*vasatiṃ*)—the abode; (such) Agni
- अरातयः (*arātayaḥ*)—the enemies
- मर्त्येषु (*martyeṣu*)—among the worlds of mortals
- न दधुः (*na dadhuḥ*)—hid away
- अत्रेः (*atreḥ*)—of Vṛśa, a descendant of the great seer Atri
- ब्रह्माणि (*brahmāṇi*)—hymns
- तं (*taṃ*)—that Agni
- अव सृजंतु (*ava sṛjaṃtu*)—let them make him come out from hiding
- निंदितारः (*niṃditāraḥ*)—the enemies who revile us
- निंद्यासः (*niṃdyāsaḥ*)—being subject to our censure
- भवंतु (*bhavaṃtu*)—let them be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The enemies hid Agni, lord of all living beings and abode of all humans, among the worlds of mortals. May the hymns of Vṛśa, a descendant of the great seer Atri, make the hidden Agni come out. May the enemies who revile us become subject to our censure.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Enemies have secreted amongst mortals, the king of living beings, the asylum of men : may the prayers of Atri set him free; may those who revile be reviled.

### Printed p. 755

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

As explained earlier, the situation at hand is that Vṛśa's praise made the hidden Agni visible to the sacrificer. This is the situation in which Vṛśa prays to Agni.
अत्रेः ब्रह्माणि अव सृजंतु (*atreḥ brahmāṇi ava sṛjaṃtu*)—may the hymns of Vṛśa, born in the Atri lineage, make the hidden Agni come out; this is the prayer.
Brahmāṇi—the word brahma is read among the names of food and among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9). It is derived from the root bṛh, meaning "to grow"; the sense is a rite that causes growth, or food.
तस्मिन् बह्माणि पूर्वथेंद्र उक्ता समग्मतार्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं । (*tasmin bahmāṇi pūrvatheṃdra uktā samagmatārcannanu svarājyaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-80-16)
In Ṛks such as this it is explained as food in the form of oblation. This is the meaning in Sāyaṇa's bhāṣya. The Nirukta-writers quote this same sentence and, with तस्मिन् ब्रह्माणि कर्माणि (*tasmin brahmāṇi karmāṇi*), explain the word brahma as "rite". Besides this, the sense "praise" is also well known.
प्राणद्ब्रह्मापि सुप्रीतः सुताय तदथर्वणः । स चौभवदृषिस्तेन ब्रह्मणा दीप्तिमत्तरः ॥ (*prāṇadbrahmāpi suprītaḥ sutāya tadatharvaṇaḥ | sa caubhavadṛṣistena brahmaṇā dīptimattaraḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 3-18)
Here the situation is described in which Indra taught Atharvan a mantra in the form of praise. The sage Dadhīci received that brahma (the mantra in the form of praise) and became exceedingly radiant; thus the sense of the word brahma as "mantra" is stated. In the present mantra too, the meaning is taken as praise or mantra. How the many senses of this word — food, rite, mantra, the supreme Brahman and so on — are possible, and in which situations each usage occurs, will be shown elsewhere.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अंजःसव अहवनीयोपस्थाने शुनश्चिच्छेपमित्येषा । अग्निमाहवनीयमुपस्थापयांचकार शुनश्चिच्छेपं निदितं सहस्रात् । ऐ. ब्रां. ७-१७ । इति ब्राह्मणं ॥
> हे अग्ने निदितं नितरां बद्धं शुनःशेपमृषिं सहस्रादनेकरूपाद्योपादमुंचॆः । अमोचयः । चिदिति पूरणः । शुनःशेपमिति पदस्य मध्ये पदांतरस्य
> संहितायां व्यत्ययेनावस्थितिः । स ऋषिरशमिष्ट हि । शांतवान् खलु । यद्वा । स हि
> यस्मादशमिष्ट । स्तुतिकर्मैतत् । तस्तावीत् । तस्मादमुंच इति संबंधः ।
> एवैवमस्मदस्मत्तः पाशान्नि मुमुग्नि । विमोचय । हे होतर्हे चिकित्सश्चेतनवान्नाग्ने
> इह तु वेद्यां निषद्यावस्थाय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the añjaḥsava, in the worship of the Āhavanīya fire, the Ṛk शुनश्चिच्छेपं (*śunaścicchepaṃ*) is used. The Brāhmaṇa says that he (Śunaḥśepa) approached the Āhavanīya Agni with शुनश्चिच्छेपं निदितं सहस्रात् (*śunaścicchepaṃ niditaṃ sahasrāt*) (Ai. Brā. 7-17). "O Agni, you released the seer Śunaḥśepa, tightly bound, from a thousand — manifold — stakes (yūpa)." Cit is a filler. The placing of another word in the middle of the word Śunaḥśepa in the Saṃhitā is by transposition. "That seer was indeed calmed." Or else: because he praised (praising is the meaning of अशमिष्ट (*aśamiṣṭa*)), therefore you released him; this is the connection. "So release the bonds from us. O Hotṛ, O wise Agni, having sat down here on the altar (do so)."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (ऎलै अग्निये (*èlai agniye*))—O Agni
- निदितं (*niditaṃ*)—the fully bound
- शुनःशेफं (*śunaḥśephaṃ*)—the seer named Śunaḥśepa
- सहस्रात् (*sahasrāt*)—from thousands
- यूपात् (*yūpāt*)—from bonds
- आमुंचः (*āmuṃcaḥ*)—you have released
- सः (*saḥ*)—that seer
- अशमिष्ट (*aśamiṣṭa*)—remained calm of mind
- होतः (*hotaḥ*)—accomplisher of the oblation
- चिकित्स्यः (*cikitsyaḥ*)—the wise one
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- इह तु (*iha tu*)—right here on this sacrificial altar
- निषद्य (*niṣadya*)—having sat down
- एव (*eva*)—just as you freed Śunaḥśepa
- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—from us
- पाशान् (*pāśān*)—the nooses
- वि मुमुग्नि (*vi mumugni*)—release

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you freed the seer Śunaḥśepa, fully bound to thousands of posts, from all his bonds. In the same way, O Agni, accomplisher of the oblation and wise one, sitting right here on this sacrificial altar, free us from all our nooses.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
You have liberated fettered Shunahshepa from a thousand stakes, for he was patient in endurance: so, Agni, free us from our bonds, having sat down here (at our sacrifice), intelligent offerer of oblations.

### Printed p. 757

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Here the seer prays to Agni to free him from nooses in the form of sin or of sorrow. In this prayer there is a comparison with Śunaḥśepa: the praise is that, as Agni protected Śunaḥśepa and freed him from the noose, he should free the seer too. The same story of Śunaḥśepa, as told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, has been given at length in the Special Topics of Ṛ. Saṃ. sūkta 1-27 (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, part 3). It says that he prayed in turn to deities such as Agni, Savitṛ, Varuṇa and Indra, and by the grace of all of them, above all of Indra, had his noose loosed. This story of Śunaḥśepa is a principal episode from the viewpoint of modern critics, and in many respects it is open to criticism. Earlier, only the sequence of the story was given, and the inner meaning of the narrative was not examined. It is proper now to examine what the principle of the Śunaḥśepa narrative is; after that the fitness of this comparison in the present mantra can be understood.
Among the well-known narratives of Vedic literature, none has the importance and fame of the Śunaḥśepa narrative. For that reason it is quoted and recited again and again both in Vedic works such as the Brāhmaṇas and in worldly works such as the Purāṇas.
This narrative is recited in full in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (7-3). The story told there is that Śunaḥśepa was accepted as the sacrificial victim in place of Rohita, son of Hariścandra, and that by Viśvāmitra's favour Śunaḥśepa praised Varuṇa and the others and was freed from the noose. On the basis of this story, some modern scholars have suggested that human sacrifice was practised in the Vedic age. But the Śruti texts do not give that view such firm support. If the setting of the story is examined, the situation is as follows.
After all the preliminary rites forming the limbs of the sacrifice were completed, at the time in the principal sacrifice when the victim was to be tied and slaughtered, no one agreed to bind Śunaḥśepa to the sacrificial post. Then Ajīgarta himself (the father) agreed to help in this act. Moreover, he consented even to cut down his own son like an animal. Then Śunaḥśepa, trembling that he would be cut like a beast, cried out to the gods. In order he prayed to Prajāpati, Agni, Savitṛ, Varuṇa, Indra, the Aśvins and Uṣas, and sought their help. As the mantras praising Uṣas were recited one by one, all his bonds were fully loosened

### Printed p. 758
and he was freed (Hariścandra's disease was destroyed). Then Śunaḥśepa was asked to join the officiating priests. Knowing the procedure of the añjaḥsava, he performed the pressing rite accordingly.
Afterwards he refused to accept Ajīgarta as his father and obtained sonship to Viśvāmitra. This is the story told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. But it cannot be said that the Ṛksaṃhitā wholly supports this full story. The narrative is nowhere recited in full in the Ṛksaṃhitā. Even so, the setting is indicated in many places. It is well known that the pressing rite in the form of the añjaḥsava was first seen by Śunaḥśepa himself. In this the Ṛksaṃhitā texts are the principal praise-verses, all recited by Śunaḥśepa. If one first knows which they are, the inner principle of the narrative is then easily understood. The order of the mantras recited by Śunaḥśepa at the time of the añjaḥsava rite is as follows:—
1. कस्य नूनं कतमस्यामृतानां (*kasya nūnaṃ katamasyāmṛtānāṃ*) (1-24-1): prayer to Prajāpati.
2. अग्नेर्वयं प्रथमस्यामृतानां (*agnervayaṃ prathamasyāmṛtānāṃ*) (1-24-2): praise of Agni.
3. अभि त्वा देव सवितः (*abhi tvā deva savitaḥ*) (1-24-3 to 5): praise of Savitṛ.
4. न हि ते क्षत्रं न सहो न मन्युं (*na hi te kṣatraṃ na saho na manyuṃ*) (1-24-6 to 15) and 1-25-1 to 21: these 31 mantras are praise of Varuṇa.
5. वसिष्वा हि मियेध्य (*vasiṣvā hi miyedhya*) (1-26-) and 1-27-1 to 12: these 22 mantras are again praises of Agni.
6. नमो महद्भो (*namo mahadbho*) (1-27-13): prayer to the Viśvedevas.
7. यच्चिद्धि सत्य सोमपा (*yacciddhi satya somapā*) (1-29-1; 1-30-1 to 15): these mantras are in praise of Indra.
Pleased with these mantras, Indra gives Śunaḥśepa a golden chariot. Then Śunaḥśepa recites mantras such as शश्वदिंद्र (*śaśvadiṃdra*) (1-30-6) and accepts it. Then he prays to and praises the Aśvins and Uṣas. Thereupon he is fully freed from bondage.
(Scholars such as Keith hold that these mantras have no connection with the story told in the Brāhmaṇa; Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society 1911, p. 988. This point has to be examined and settled on the basis of Śruti texts.)

### Printed p. 759
The same Aitareya Brāhmaṇa story is told in the Śāṅkhāyana Śrautasūtra (15-17-2), though with variant readings. The Bṛhaddevatā describes the same setting thus:
सूयमानः शश्वदिति प्रीतस्तु मनसा दद् । शुनःशेफाय दिव्यं तु रथं सर्वं हिरण्मयं ॥ (*sūyamānaḥ śaśvaditi prītastu manasā dad | śunaḥśephāya divyaṃ tu rathaṃ sarvaṃ hiraṇmayaṃ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 3-103)
Indra, pleased by the praises beginning शश्वत् (*śaśvat*) (1-3-16), satisfied in his own mind, gave to Śunaḥśepa a divine, wholly golden chariot.**NOTE**
कस्य पंचोनाजीगर्तिः शुनःशेफः स कृत्रिमो वैश्वामित्रो देवरातः । (*kasya paṃconājīgartiḥ śunaḥśephaḥ sa kṛtrimo vaiśvāmitro devarātaḥ |*) (Sarvānukramaṇī.)
The Sarvānukramaṇī says that Śunaḥśepa, who was Ajīgarta's son, afterwards became the son of Viśvāmitra.**NOTE**
The same story is recited in the Itihāsas and Purāṇas with some difference. In the Rāmāyaṇa Śunaḥśepa is said to be the son of Ṛcīka; instead of Hariścandra there is the emperor Ambarīṣa. In the Mahābhārata Śunaḥśepa is a son of Ṛcīka, but there is no Ambarīṣa; Hariścandra is the king. In the Purāṇas the setting is described in two ways: the Bhāgavata and the Devībhāgavata follow the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa story, and the Vedāntara (?) follows the Rāmāyaṇa story.**NOTE**
Thus three lines are seen in this narrative: 1. Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, 2. Rāmāyaṇa, 3. Mahābhārata; in them the main part of the story is one, with slight differences in the account.
In the present case the point to be understood is whether the mention of Śunaḥśepa in the Ṛksaṃhitā, and the mantras composed and recited by him, fully underlie the narrative given in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, or whether some main episodes told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa were imagined later. Then it must be examined whether this narrative supports the view that human sacrifice was practised in the Vedic age.
In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa three points chiefly deserve notice: 1. The agreement between Hariścandra and Varuṇa, as a result of which Hariścandra got a son named Rohita. 2. The episode of Ajīgarta and Śunaḥśepa. 3. The dialogue between Viśvāmitra and his sons, and Viśvāmitra's accepting Śunaḥśepa as his son.

### Printed p. 760
Hariścandra, Rohita, Ajīgarta and, in this setting, Viśvāmitra's entry — none of these is described in the Ṛksaṃhitā. For that reason English scholars such as Roth hold that the Ṛksaṃhitā is not the basis of this full story, and that the 100 mantras mentioned above were incorporated, as fitting that occasion, into the story imagined in the Brāhmaṇa in support of it. According to their view, the seer Śunaḥśepa, caught in some calamity, prayed to deities such as Varuṇa, obtained their favour and was freed from bondage (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-12; 1-24-13; 5-2-7). This is the basis in the Ṛksaṃhitā. The Brāhmaṇas and the rest developed this into the Hariścandra story, extending it until Śunaḥśepa is made a sacrificial victim, is then freed with Viśvāmitra's help and obtains sonship to him; this is the view of that opinion. The Ṛksaṃhitā has only the description of bondage; or, if it is said that because the word यूपात् (*yūpāt*) is used in the present mantra (5-2-7) a sacrificial victim must be understood — there is the qualifier सहस्रात् (*sahasrāt*).**NOTE**
Therefore some hold that the word yūpa here should not be taken in its direct sense of a post to which the sacrificial animal is tied, but that the figurative yūpa-form may be taken to mean "bondage", and then the sense of a human victim does not arise. Sāyaṇa explains सहस्रात् (*sahasrāt*) as "of a thousand forms". A post for tying an animal is not of a thousand forms. Therefore, some hold, the figurative sense should be given: he was freed from bonds of many kinds.
Even if it be said that yūpa gives the meaning "sacrificial post", it cannot be said from this one example alone that human sacrifice was current like the other sacrifices. Śunaḥśepa's binding was merely accidental; as a result of the agreement between Varuṇa and Hariścandra it ends in this binding. And the very events of this episode show a protest against human sacrifice. To cut down an animal bound to the sacrificial post, the help of the officiating priests is necessary. None of the priests belonging to that sacrificial place agrees to help in this base act. The shamitṛ appointed for that work also holds back. Only the father, base and greedy, comes forward for this work. It is also made clear by this that this is not the act of an Ārya but of a non-Ārya. The notion that all Brāhmaṇas are Āryas is not in the Ṛksaṃhitā either; and, as shown earlier in many places in the Ṛksaṃhitā texts, all those without Vedic rites are described together as non-Āryas. The name of Śunaḥśepa's father and the names of his brothers confirm this. Ajīgarta means one who has nothing to swallow, that is, extremely poor. Names such as Śunaḥpuccha also show his baseness. But mere poverty is not non-Āryahood; his other dealings also show his baseness. And when the shamitṛs appointed to cut the sacrificial victim do not agree to this act, this base father to this act

### Printed p. 761
[Kannada prose, continuing:] Since he agreed to it, Śunaḥśepa, released from bondage as a punishment for that sinful act of his, refuses to accept Ajīgarta as his father again. And since he had received the vision of divine hymns, he himself also became qualified to be an ṛtvij. These many circumstances show clearly how sinful those who followed the Vedic path considered human sacrifice (naramedha) to be.

"स होवाच शुनशेफो यः सकृत्पातकं कुर्यात्कुर्यादेनत्ततोपरं । नापगाः शौद्रान्यायादसंधेयं त्वया कृतमित्यसंधेयमिति ह विश्वामित्र उपपपाद स होवाच विश्वामित्रो भीम एव सौयवसिः शासेन विशिशासिसुः । अस्मान्मैतस्य पुत्रो भूः................ (*sa hovāca śunaśepho yaḥ sakṛtpātakaṃ kuryātkuryādenattatoparaṃ | nāpagāḥ śaudrānyāyādasaṃdheyaṃ tvayā kṛtamityasaṃdheyamiti ha viśvāmitra upapapāda sa hovāca viśvāmitro bhīma eva sauyavasiḥ śāsena viśiśāsisuḥ | asmānmaitasya putro bhūḥ................*)"
(Ai. Brā. 7-17)

When Ajīgarta said, "Child, what I did before was wrong. I shall remove this sin; come home," Śunaḥśepa replied, "You who did not shrink from this sinful act once will not hesitate to do such a deed again and again. For this deed of yours there is no expiation." Viśvāmitra also confirms: "No, for such a deed there is no expiation." Again he instructs: "When he held up his hand for your slaughter, Ajīgarta was of terrible form. Do not become his son again."

When the loathing contained in the story is itself so clear, no other evidence is needed in this matter. The scholar Max Muller, stating his own view on this matter, has also said: "It does not necessarily follow from this legend that the Rishis, the authors of thc Vedic Hymns offered human sacrifices."

It is clear that from this episode alone it cannot be said that the sages of the Vedic age offered a human oblation at sacrifices.
[History of Ancient Sanskrit Literature 1926 Ed. p. 221]

Weber has stated that human sacrifice (puruṣamedha) was in vogue. Opposing that view, the scholar Eggling says:
"This legeud, so far from bearing witness to the existence of human sacrifices as a generally recognised practice."
(Sacred Books of the East, Vol. 44, p. XXXVI).
He has made clear that there is not the slightest substance in saying, from these episodes alone, that human sacrifice was customary.

### Printed p. 762
Therefore, where it says "from a thousand posts" (sahasrāt yūpāt), in the present mantra it must be understood as the bondage that is sin. In the same way the seer prays to Agni to release him too from bondage.

> हे अग्ने हृणीयमानः क्रुद्यंस्त्वं मत् मत्तोऽपैयेर्हि । अपागाः
> खलु ॥ ई गतावित्यस्मात् श्यन्विकरणाल्लजि मध्यमे छांदसे परस्मैपद आडागमे

> ददर्श । तेनानुशिष्टोऽहं हे अग्ने त्वामागामिति । एवं वृश आह ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, being angry, you have gone away from me. The verb is from *ī gatau*, with the Vedic forms of the second person. "Indra, the protector of the gods' rites, has spoken to me"; he alone, being wise, has looked upon you, has seen you. Instructed by him, O Agni, I have come to you. Thus Vṛśa speaks.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हृणीयमानः (*hṛṇīyamānaḥ*)—you, angered (by my offences)
- मत् (*mat*)—from me
- अप ऐयेः हि (*apa aiyeḥ hi*)—have you not gone far away?
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—of the gods
- व्रतपाः (*vratapāḥ*)—the protector of rites
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- मे (*me*)—to me
- प्र उवाच (*pra uvāca*)—has told
- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—he himself, who knows your nature
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- अनु चचक्ष (*anu cacakṣa*)—has chosen and looked upon
- तेन (*tena*)—by that Indra
- अनुशिष्टः (*anuśiṣṭaḥ*)—instructed
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- आगां (*āgāṃ*)—I have come near you

### Printed p. 763

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, angered by my offences, have you not gone far away from me? Indra, the protector of the gods' rites, has told me about you. He, who knows your nature, has chosen and looked upon you. Instructed by that Indra, I have come near you.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
When angered, (Agni), depart from me: the protector of the worship of the gods, (Indra), has spoken to me : the wise Indra has looked upon you, and instructed by him, I have come, Agni, to you.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

1. Agni's departure because of King Vṛśa (Trairuṇa).
2. Again, the recitation of an Atharvāṅgirasa mantra, making Agni appear.
3. Indra's teaching of this very fire-kindling technique. All three points are indicated in this mantra.

हृणीयमानः मत्तः अप ऐयेः (*hṛṇīyamānaḥ mattaḥ apa aiyeḥ*): "Angry, you went away from me" — Agni is addressed thus. It was stated earlier how Agni's oblation departed, Trayaruṇa's oblations and the like were not cooked, and Trayaruṇa again obtained Vṛśa's help; and also how the dead boy was made to live by reciting the Atharvāṅgirasa mantra, and how Agni's oblation was made to appear again. How Indra taught this Atharvāṅgirasa mantra was also stated earlier. Quoting the mantra "स हेंद्रेणोक्त आस............ (*sa heṃdreṇokta āsa............*)" (Śa. Brā. 14-1-1-19) (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā Part 11, p. 85), the greatness of the Atharvāṅgirasa mantra taught by Indra was shown. But there the occasion is the account of the sage Dadhīci. In the present case a teacher–pupil relation between Indra and Vṛśa is stated. Since it says "सोऽथर्वांगिरसान्मंत्रान्‌दृष्ट्वा (*so 'tharvāṃgirasānmaṃtrāndṛṣṭvā*)", here too it indicates the teacher–pupil relation between Vṛśa and Indra.

Trayaruṇa was born in the Atri gotra. Atri was born in the line of Atharvāṅgirasa.
"अत्रेयादात्रेयो मांटेः ............ अथर्वणाद्दध्यज् (*atreyādātreyo māṃṭeḥ ............ atharvaṇāddadhyaj*)"
(Bṛ. U. 9-6-3)
Thus in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka there is the sequence of sages born in Atri's line. But Vṛśa may have been a son of Atharvāṅgirasa. In the present case it is said that Vṛśa saw and recited the Atharvāṅgirasa mantra. Therefore

### Printed p. 764
here the circumstance cannot be stated precisely. But mantras such as अग्निर्जातो अथर्वणा (*agnirjāto atharvaṇā*) (10-21-5) show that the activity of Atharvāṅgiras was the cause of Agni's first blazing.

> तथाभूतः सन् महित्वा स्वमहत्वेन विश्वानि सर्वाणि पदार्थजातान्याविष्कृणुते ।

> दुःखगमनाः प्रसहते । अभिभवति । किंच शितीते । तीक्ष्णीकरोति । शृंगे शृंगाणि ।

> रक्षसो नाशाय । निश्यति शृंगे रक्षसो विनिक्षणनाय । नि. ४-१८ । इति यास्कः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Agni shines forth with great light, i.e. brilliance; he is brightly lit. Being so, by his own greatness he makes all things manifest. Thus grown, Agni overcomes the undivine (adevīḥ), i.e. non-playing, demonic deceits (māyāḥ), which are hard to traverse (दुरेवा (*durevā*): going to sorrow). Moreover he sharpens his horns, i.e. sharpens horn-like, destructive flames. For what? To destroy the Rakṣas; "he sharpens his horns for the destruction of the Rakṣas." So Yāska (Ni. 4-18).

- दुरेवाः (*durevāḥ*)—and causing sorrow
- मायाः (*māyāḥ*)—evil powers
- प्र सहते (*pra sahate*)—tramples down
- शृंगे (*śṛṃge*)—his horn-like flames
- रक्षसे (*rakṣase*)—of the demonic power
- विनिक्षे (*vinikṣe*)—for the destruction
- शितीते (*śitīte*)—makes sharp

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni shines with his exceeding brilliance. By his greatness he illumines all beings. He tramples down the evil powers, of demonic nature and causing sorrow. He sharpens his horn-like flames for the destruction of the demonic power.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Agni shines with great and varied radiance ; he makes all things manifest by his might ; he overcomes undivine malignant delusions ; he sharpens his horns for the destruction of the Rakshasas.

> प्रादुर्भवंतु । किमर्थं । तिग्मायुधास्तीक्ष्णायुधस्थानीया ज्वालाः । रक्षसे हंतवा

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And may Agni's roaring (svānāsaḥ) flames be manifest in heaven, i.e. appear in the sky. For what? The flames, like sharp weapons, to slay the Rakṣas; उ (*u*) is an expletive. Even in exhilaration (mada), i.e. joy, Agni's rays (bhāmāḥ), wrath or splendours, break the Rakṣas utterly or afflict them. The adevīḥ, non-playing demonic armies (paribādhaḥ), tormentors on every side, do not ward him off.

- तिग्मायुधाः (*tigmāyudhāḥ*)—flames destructive like sharp weapons
- रक्षसे (*rakṣase*)—of the demonic power
- हन्तवा उ (*hantavā u*)—

—for the destruction indeed
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the sky
- षंतु (*ṣaṃtu*)—let them appear
- मदे चित् (*made cit*)—when joy arises
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Agni
- भामाः (*bhāmāḥ*)—the radiances
- प्र रुजंति (*pra rujaṃti*)—wholly afflict (the asuras)
- परिबाधः (*paribādhaḥ*)—those who seek to torment all round
- अदेवीः (*adevīḥ*)—enemies of demonic nature
- न वरंते (*na varaṃte*)—cannot withstand (these rays of Agni)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Agni's flames, roaring and destructive like sharp weapons, appear in the sky for the destruction of the demonic power. When these radiances of Agni are exhilarated, they wholly afflict the asuras. The enemies, lying in wait to cause torment on every side and of demonic nature, cannot withstand these rays of Agni.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May your roaring (flames), Agni, be manifest in the sky as sharp weapons wherewith to slay the Rakshasas : in his exhilaration his shining (rays) infliet (destruction), and undivine opposing (hosts) arrest him not.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे तुविजात बहुभावमापन्नाग्ने ते त्वदर्थमेतं स्तोममेतत्सोत्रं
> विप्रो मेधावी स्तोता रथं न रथमिव धीरः स्वपाः शोभनकर्माहमतक्षं ।
> समपादयं । हे अग्ने देव त्वं यदीदेनं स्तोमं प्रति हर्याः । प्रतिकामयेथाः। तर्हि स्वर्वतोः स्वरणवतीर्व्याप्तिमतीरप एनैनेन जयेम। प्राप्नुयाम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, born in many forms (tuvijāta), for you I, the wise (vipra) and steady praiser, of good works (svapāḥ), have fashioned (atakṣam), i.e. produced, this hymn, as one fashions a chariot. O divine Agni, if you favour (prati haryāḥ), i.e. desire, this hymn, then with it may we win the waters (apaḥ), svarvatīḥ, i.e. resounding and extensive; may we obtain them.

O Agni, who appear in many forms: I, who am wise, of excellent understanding and of good works, have fashioned this praise for you as one skilfully builds a chariot. ##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तुविग्रीवो बहुज्वालः प्रभूतग्रीवो ना वृषभो वर्षिता कामानां
> ववृधानो वर्धमानोऽग्निरर्योऽरेर्वेदो धनमशत्त्वकंटकं समजाति ।
> संयोजयति ! इतीममर्थमग्निममृता अन्ये देवा आवोचन् ! यस्मादेवं

> यच्छतु । हविष्मते च शर्म यंसत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni is "thick-necked", that is, many-flamed (the "neck" being his flames); he is the showerer of desires and is growing. He gathers together the wealth of the enemy, which is without opposition (free of thorns). The other gods, the immortals, have declared this about Agni. Since that is so, he is to bestow happiness on the human worshipper, the man who has the sacrifice, and likewise on the man who has the oblation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तुविग्रीवः (*tuvigrīvaḥ*)—the one with many flames like necks
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—the showerer of desires
- ववृधानः (*vavṛdhānaḥ*)—the one who grows; Agni who is such
- आर्यः (*āryaḥ*)—of the enemy
- वेदः (*vedaḥ*)—the wealth
- अशत्रु (*aśatru*)—without opposition
- समजाति (*samajāti*)—gathers
- इतीमं (*itīmaṃ*)—such, endowed with wealth
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- अमृताः (*amṛtāḥ*)—all the (other) gods
- अवोचन् (*avocan*)—praise (and by the power of this praise)
- बर्हिष्मते (*barhiṣmate*)—to the one who has the sacrifice
- मनवे (*manave*)—to the sacrificer
- शर्म (*śarma*)—happiness
- यंसत् (*yaṃsat*)—may he give
- हविष्यते मनवे (*haviṣyate manave*)—to the sacrificer who offers oblations
- शर्म (*śarma*)—happiness
- यंसत् (*yaṃsat*)—may he give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who has many flames in the form of necks, who showers desires and who grows, gathers the wealth of the enemy without any opposition. All the other gods praise Agni, who is endowed with such wealth. By the power of this praise, may Agni bring happiness to the sacrificer who has the sacrifice and offers the oblation.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The many-necked, the showerer (of benefits), ever increasing,
collects together the wealth of the enemy without opposition: the immortals
have enjoined Agni that he will bestow happiness on the man who offers
sacrifice; that he will bestow happiness on the man who offers oblations.

## Sūkta 3 (Maṇḍala 5)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्वमग्ने वरुण इति द्वादशर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तमात्रेयस्य वसुश्रुतस्यार્ષं
> त्रैष्टुभमाग्नेयं । त्वमग्ने वसुश्रुत इत्यनुक्रांतं ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोर्विनियोगोऽबोध्यग्निरित्युक्तः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The twelve-verse third hymn, त्वमग्ने वरुण (*tvamagne varuṇa*), has Vasuśruta of the Ātreya line as seer, Agni as deity and Triṣṭubh as metre. The Anukramaṇī says त्वमग्ने वसुश्रुत (*tvamagne vasuśruta*). Its use (viniyoga) in the Prātaranuvāka and the Aśvinaśastra was stated with the hymn अबोध्यग्निः (*abodhyagniḥ*).

##### Anuvāda

This hymn beginning त्वमग्ने वरुणः (*tvamagne varuṇaḥ*) is the third hymn in the first anuvāka. It has twelve ṛks. Its seer is Vasuśruta, born in the Atri lineage; the deity is Agni; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said त्वमग्ने वसुश्रुतः (*tvamagne vasuśrutaḥ*). The use of this hymn for reciting the mantras of the Prātaranuvāka and the Aśvinaśastra was stated in the viniyoga of the hymn अबोध्यग्निः (*abodhyagniḥ*) (the first hymn of this maṇḍala).

Hymn 3. Maṇḍala 5; Anuvāka 1; Sūkta 3; Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 8; Vargas 16, 17. Number of ṛks in the hymn: 12. Seer: Vasuśruta Ātreya. Deity: Agni. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

> त्वे विश्वे॑ सहसस्पुत्र दे॒वास्त्विंद्रो॑ दा॒शुषे॒ मर्त्या॑य ॥

> *tve viśve sahasasputra devāstviṃdro dāśuṣe martyāya ‖*

> तै इति । विश्वे । सहसः । पुत्र । देवाः । त्वं । इंद्रः । दातुषे । मर्त्याय ॥ १ ॥

> *tvaṃ | agne | varuṇaḥ | jāyase | yat | tvaṃ | mitraḥ | bhavasi | yat | saṃiddhaḥ |*

### Printed p. 770

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वं वरुणस्तमसां वारको रात्रभिमानी देवोऽपि त्वमेव
> यद्यदा जायसे । किंच त्वं मित्रोऽहरभिमानी देवः प्रमितेस्त्राता यद्यदा
> समिद्धः । त्वमुत्पन्नमात्रः सन् तमो निवारयसि प्रवृद्धः सन् हितकारी भवसीत्यर्थः।
> त्वे त्वयि विश्वे सर्वॆऽपि देवा वर्तंते । त्वद्धत्तेन हविषा तेषां जीवनात् । ते
> देवा बिभ्यतोऽग्निं प्राविशन्निति हि श्रुतेः । हे सहसस्पुत्र बलेन मध्यमानत्वात् ।
> किंच त्वमिंद्रः स्वामी दाशुषे हविर्दात्रे मर्त्याय यजमानाय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, you are Varuṇa, the restrainer of darkness, the god presiding over night, when you are born. And you are Mitra, the god presiding over day, the protector from death, when you are kindled: when you have just arisen you ward off darkness, and when you are grown you do good. In you all the gods abide, since they live by the oblation given through you; for the śruti says that the gods, afraid, entered Agni. He is addressed as "son of strength" because he is produced by the force of churning. And you are Indra, the lord, to the mortal, the sacrificer who gives the oblation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- जायसे (*jāyase*)—you are born (then)
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—you are of the form of Varuṇa
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- समिद्धः (*samiddhaḥ*)—you blaze up (then)
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- मित्रः भवसि (*mitraḥ bhavasi*)—become of the form of Mitra
- त्वे (*tve*)—in you
- विश्वे (*viśve*)—all
- देवा (*devā*)—the gods (are contained)
- सहसस्पुत्र (*sahasasputra*)—O Agni, son of strength
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—who offers the oblation
- मर्त्याय (*martyāya*)—to the human
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—you are of the form of Indra (the lord)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, at the time you are born you are of the form of Varuṇa; then, when you blaze up, of the form of Mitra. In you all the gods are contained. O Agni, son of strength, you are of the form of Indra for the share of the man who offers the oblation.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
You, Agni, are born Varuna, you become Mitra when kindled : in
you, son of strength, are all the gods : you are Indra, son of strength, to
the mortal who presents (oblations).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Vasuśruta is the seer of this hymn and of the next three hymns (hymns 3, 4, 5, 6 of this maṇḍala). Beyond the fact that this Vasuśruta was born in the Ātreya line, nothing else is known about him.

In this ṛk and in some of the following ṛks Agni is praised as having the nature of other deities. Since all the gods receive the oblations offered in Agni through Agni's mouth, Agni is said to be of the nature of all the gods. To support this, the commentator quotes the Taittirīya Saṃhitā passage:

### Printed p. 771

देवासुराः संयत्ता आसन्ते देवा बिभ्यतोऽग्निं प्राविशन्तस्मादाहुरग्निः सर्वा देवता इति तेऽग्निमेव वरूथं कृत्वासुरानभ्यभवन् । (*devāsurāḥ saṃyattā āsante devā bibhyato 'gniṃ prāviśantasmādāhuragniḥ sarvā devatā iti te 'gnimeva varūthaṃ kṛtvāsurānabhyabhavan |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-2-6, 7).

That is: in former times the gods and the asuras were drawn up for battle. Seeing that the strength of the asuras was greater, fear arose in the gods. So the gods took refuge in Agni, that he must protect them; they entered into him and became one with him. Afterwards, by Agni's protection, the gods were able to conquer the asuras. For this and similar reasons it is well known that all the gods dwell in Agni and that Agni has the nature of all the gods.

Varuṇa, Mitra: the śruti sentence मैत्र्यं वा अहः । वारुणी रात्रिः (*maitryaṃ vā ahaḥ | vāruṇī rātriḥ*) declares that Mitra is the presiding deity of the day (ahas) and Varuṇa of the night. Because Agni's light shines chiefly at night, and because Agni with his light dispels darkness and makes light, Agni is praised as the gods Varuṇa and Mitra.

Sahasaḥ putra: Agni is addressed as the son of strength. In sacrifices and the like, when Agni is produced by churning in the araṇis (pieces of wood), much strength has to be used for the churning, so Agni is born of strength (force); hence it is customary to call Agni the son of strength.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विवाहे चतुर्थ्यामाज्याहुतौ त्वमर्यमेत्येषा । सूत्रितं च । त्वमर्यमा
> भवसि यत्कनीनामिति विवाहे चतुर्थीं । आ. गृ. १-४ । इति ॥
> हे अग्ने त्वमर्यमा भवसि । सर्वेषां नियमितासि । यद्यदा कनीनां
> कन्यकानां संबंध्यसि । किंच हे स्वधावन् हविर्लक्षणान्नवन् गुह्यं गोपनीयं
> नाम बिभर्षि वैश्वानर इति तन्नाम । सुधितं सुष्टु निहितं मित्रं न मित्रमिव गोभिः ।
> विकारे प्रकृतिशब्दः । गोविकार्यै क्षीरादिभिरंजंति । यद्यस्माद्दंपती ज्यायापती।
> समनसा समानमनस्कौ कृणोषि । करोषि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This ṛk is used at a wedding in the fourth ājya oblation; it is also set down in the sūtra: त्वमर्यमा भवसि यत्कनीनामिति विवाहे चतुर्थीं (*tvamaryamā bhavasi yatkanīnāmiti vivāhe caturthīṃ*) (Ā. Gṛ. 1-4)**NOTE**. O Agni, you are Aryaman, the regulator of all, when you are connected with maidens. And, O possessor of svadhā (food in the form of oblation), you bear a secret name, which is the name Vaiśvānara. "Like a friend well placed": the word for the source (prakṛti) stands for the product, that is, they anoint with milk and the like, made from the cow. Since you make husband and wife of one mind, (they anoint you).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे अग्नौ (*he agnau*)—O Agni
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- कनीनां (*kanīnāṃ*)—are connected with maidens (then)
- आर्यमा (*āryamā*)—of the form of Aryaman
- भवसि (*bhavasi*)—you become
- स्वधावन् (*svadhāvan*)—O Agni, who have food in the form of oblation
- गुह्यं (*guhyaṃ*)—secret
- नाम (*nāma*)—name
- बिभर्षि (*bibharṣi*)—you bear
- यत् (*yat*)—by what power
- दंपती (*daṃpatī*)—husband and wife
- समनसा (*samanasā*)—of one mind
- कृणोषि (*kṛṇoṣi*)—you make (therefore)
- सुधितं (*sudhitaṃ*)—excellently honoured
- मित्रं न (*mitraṃ na*)—like a friend
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—with milk and the like, products of the cow
- अंजंति (*aṃjaṃti*)—they adorn

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, when you are connected with maidens you become the god Aryaman**NOTE**. O Agni, who have food in the form of oblation, you bear a secret name. By the power by which you make husband and wife of one mind, for that very reason they adorn you with milk and the like, products of the cow, as one adorns a friend who is excellently honoured.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
You are Aryaman in relation to maidens ; you bear, enjoyer of
sacrificial food, a mysterious name : they anoint you, like a welcowe friend
with milk and butter, when you make husband and wife of one mind.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the principal homa of the wedding, when the ājya oblation is offered in Agni, this ṛk त्वमर्यमा (*tvamaryamā*) is to be used as the mantra of the fourth oblation, according to the Āśvalāyana Gṛhyasūtra

### Printed p. 773
The viniyoga is explained by the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya Sūtra rule (Ā. Gṛ. 1-4-7) that in the marriage rite the fourth oblation-mantra is the Ṛk *tvamaryamā bhavasi yatkanīnāṃ*.
**NOTE**

Yat tvaṃ kanīnām aryamā bhavasi: O Agni, when you enter into relation with maidens, you become Aryaman. That is, the relation with maidens here means that when the principal oblation is made in the marriage, the marriage fire is famed by the name Aryaman. On this point there is also a passage of another śruti: "The maiden worships the god Agni, famed by the name Aryaman, at the time of marriage." Therefore the marriage fire, connected with the maiden, is called Aryaman. That is what is stated here.

Svadhāvan guhyaṃ nāma bibharṣi: you bear the secret name Vaiśvānara, since you receive from the sacrificers the food in the form of oblation and carry it to the deities for whom it is intended. Vaiśvānara means one who is a friend to all. The intention, signified by the word Vaiśvānara-Agni, is that because you are needed by all men beginning with the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice, and by the gods who receive the oblation through you, you are a friend to all, that is, to gods, men and everyone.

Yat dampatī samanasā kṛṇoṣi sudhitaṃ mitraṃ na gobhiḥ añjanti: O Agni, because in the marriage rite you make bride and bridegroom of one mind, that is, mutually affectionate, people treat you with honour, as they behave toward a friend, honouring and worshipping you with milk and other substances. Here "gobhiḥ" means products of the cow, milk and the like; the word "go" itself is used to denote the milk obtained from the cow.

> पदं । यत् । विष्णोः । उपमं । निधायि । तेन । पासि । गुह्यं । नाम । गोनां॥

> *tava | śriye | marutaḥ | marjayaṃta | rudra | yat | te | janima | cāru | citraṃ |*  
> *padaṃ | yat | viṣṇoḥ | upamaṃ | nidhāyi | tena | pāsi | guhyaṃ | nāma | gonāṃ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनयाग्नेर्माध्यमिकी मूर्तिरुच्यते । हे अग्ने तव श्रिये श्रयणाय
> मरुतोऽपोऽंतरिक्ष्या मर्जयंत । मार्जयंति । हे रुद्र वृष्टा रुद्रवद्वर्धितरग्ने ते तव यज्जनिम।जन्म वैद्युतलक्षणं चारु चरणीयं चित्रं चायनीयं - च
> तत्कथमिति चेदुच्यते । विष्णोर्व्यापनशीलस्य देवस्कोपमं गुह्यमगम्यं यत्पदं
> निधायि! अनेनांतरिक्षमुक्तं । उपमेयमिव विष्णोर्मध्यमं पदं तस्मानांतरिक्षं
> पश्यंतीति ब्राह्मणं । तेन गोनामुदकानां गुह्यं नाम नामानि पासि । रक्षसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By this verse the middle (atmospheric) form of Agni is described. O Agni, for your श्रिये (*śriye*), your resort, the Maruts purify the atmospheric waters. O Rudra, Agni grown like Rudra by the rain: your birth, of the nature of lightning, is lovely (चारु (*cāru*), to be moved about in) and wonderful (चित्रं (*citraṃ*), to be gazed at). How so? He answers: the secret, inaccessible, highest-comparable step of Vishnu, the all-pervading god, has been placed. By this the atmosphere is meant. A Brāhmaṇa says: "As if it were the object of comparison, the middle step of Vishnu; therefore they see the atmosphere." By that you protect the secret names of the waters (गोनां (*gonāṃ*) = of the waters).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- तव (*tava*)—your
- श्रिये (*śriye*)—for the shining of glory
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Maruts
- मर्जयंत (*marjayaṃta*)—purify (the atmosphere)
- रुद्र (*rudra*)—O Agni, who are like Rudra
- ते (*te*)—your
- जनिम (*janima*)—birth in lightning form
- यत् (*yat*)—which is
- चारु (*cāru*)—charming
- चित्रं (*citraṃ*)—wonderful
- विष्णोः (*viṣṇoḥ*)—of Vishnu
- यत् (*yat*)—which
- उपमं पदं (*upamaṃ padaṃ*)—middle step
- निधायि (*nidhāyi*)—has been placed
- तेन (*tena*)—by that
- गोनां (*gonāṃ*)—of the waters
- गुह्यं नाम (*guhyaṃ nāma*)—secret names
- पासि (*pāsi*)—you protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, for the shining of your glory the Maruts purify the atmosphere. O Agni, who are like Rudra, your birth in the form of lightning is charming and wonderful. Because of the placing of Vishnu's middle step, you cherish the secret names of the waters.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
For your glory the Maruts sweep (the firmament), when your birth, Rudra, is beautiful and wounderful : the middle step of Vishnu has been placed, so you cherish the mysterious name of the waters.

### Printed p. 775

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The meaning of this Ṛk is somewhat difficult. Here the lightning-fire (Vaidyuta Agni), a deity of the middle region, is praised.

(हे अग्ने) तव श्रिये मरुतः मर्जयंत—तव श्रयणाय मरुतः अंतरिक्ष्याः मार्जयंति (*(he agne) tava śriye marutaḥ marjayaṃta—tava śrayaṇāya marutaḥ aṃtarikṣyāḥ mārjayaṃti*). O Agni, to make your glory shine, the Maruts purify the atmosphere. The appearance of lightning in the atmosphere happens only at the time of rain. At that time the wind (a swiftly blowing wind is called Marut) blows violently. Then, during the rain or just before it, the lightning-fire becomes visible. Since the wind blows strongly before the lightning-fire appears, it is described here in a different manner: the wind blows in the atmosphere and purifies it, in order to make the glory of the lightning-fire known to all. It is natural to clean the road when a king is about to arrive; that is, the road-cleaning takes place before the king comes. In the same way, before the appearance of the lightning-fire the wind blows swiftly and purifies the atmosphere, the path of Agni's movement; so it is described.

रुद्र ते जनिम यत् चारु चित्रं विष्णोः यत् पदं उपमं पदं निधायि (*rudra te janima yat cāru citraṃ viṣṇoḥ yat padaṃ upamaṃ padaṃ nidhāyi*)—here Agni is addressed by the word Rudra. Sāyaṇa's explanation is रुद्रवद्वर्धितः (*rudravadvardhitaḥ*), "grown like Rudra". It is said here that your appearance in the atmosphere, O Agni, is as astonishing as Vishnu's stride. Since it is well known that Vishnu's three strides are in the three places, earth, atmosphere and heaven, here Vishnu's second stride in the atmosphere is indicated. "Astonishing" means: the lightning or lightning-fire that appears suddenly in the atmosphere without warning is as astonishing as Vishnu's second stride in the atmosphere; thus the comparison with Vishnu's stride is made.

तेन गोनां गुह्यं नाम पासि-तेन उदकानां नामानि रक्षसि (*tena gonāṃ guhyaṃ nāma pāsi-tena udakānāṃ nāmāni rakṣasi*). O Agni, by this astonishing action of yours you protect the names of the waters (the rain-waters); that is, you make manifest the glory of the secret waters; this is the intention. The correct meaning of this last sentence is not clear.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तव॑ श्रि॒या सु॒दृशो॑ देव दे॒वाः पु॒रू दधा॑ना अ॒मृतं॑ सपंत  
> होता॑रम॒ग्निं मनु॑षो॒ नि षे॑दुर्दश॒स्यंत॑ उ॒तिजः॒ शंस॑मा॒योः ॥ ४ ॥

> *tava śriyā sudṛśo deva devāḥ purū dadhānā amṛtaṃ sapaṃta*  
> *hotāramagniṃ manuṣo ni ṣedurdaśasyaṃta utijaḥ śaṃsamāyoḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तव । श्रिया । सुदृशः । देव । देवाः । पुरु । दधानाः । अमृतं । सपंत ।  
> होतारं । अग्निं । मनुषः । नि । सेदुः । दशस्यंतः । उशिजः । शंसं । आयोः ॥ ४ ॥

> *tava | śriyā | sudṛśaḥ | deva | devāḥ | puru | dadhānāḥ | amṛtaṃ | sapaṃta |*  
> *hotāraṃ | agniṃ | manuṣaḥ | ni | seduḥ | daśasyaṃtaḥ | uśijaḥ | śaṃsaṃ | āyoḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देवाग्ने सुदृशस्तव श्रिया समृद्ध्या देवा इंद्रादयः पुर्वत्यधिकं
> दधानास्त्वयि प्रीतिं धारयंतोऽमृतं सपंत । स्पृशंति । होतारं होमनिष्पादकमग्निं मनुषो मनुष्या नि षेदुः । परिचरंत्यृत्विजः । किं कुर्वंतः ।
> दशस्यंतो हविर्वितरंतः शंसं फलमुशिजः कामयमानस्या योर्मनुष्यस्य
> यजमानस्यार्थ० ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O divine Agni, by your श्रिया (*śriyā*) (prosperity) the gods, Indra and the rest, of fair appearance, bearing (पुरु (*puru*), more abundantly) affection for you, touch (सपंत (*sapaṃta*)) the immortal drink. Men, the priests, sit around (नि षेदुः (*ni ṣeduḥ*), attend) Agni the Hotṛ, the accomplisher of the offering. What are they doing? Giving the oblation, for the sake of the man (आयोः (*āyoḥ*)), the sacrificer, who desires the reward (शंसं (*śaṃsaṃ*) = fruit).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देव (*deva*)—O shining Agni
- तव (*tava*)—your
- श्रिया (*śriyā*)—by the wealth of splendour
- सुदृशः (*sudṛśaḥ*)—having a lovely form
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods, Indra and others
- पुरु (*puru*)—abundantly
- दधानाः (*dadhānāḥ*)—bearing affection
- अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—the immortal drink
- सपंत (*sapaṃta*)—partake of
- शंसं (*śaṃsaṃ*)—the fruit of the sacrifice
- उशिजः (*uśijaḥ*)—desiring
- आयोः (*āyoḥ*)—for the sacrificer, a man
- दशस्यंतः (*daśasyaṃtaḥ*)—offering oblations
- मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*)—priests and others
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—the accomplisher of the offering
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- निषेदुः (*niṣeduḥ*)—attend and worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O shining Agni, the gods, Indra and others, who have obtained a lovely form through the wealth of your splendour, bearing great affection for you, partake of the immortal drink. For the sacrificer, a man who desires the fruit of the sacrifice, the priests, givers of oblations, attend and worship Agni, the accomplisher of the offering.

### Printed p. 777

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Divine (Agni), the gods (made) comely by your glory, and bearing (the) great (affection), sip the ambrosia : men adore Agni, the conveyer of the burnt-offering. presenting, oblations on behalf of the institutor of the rite, desirous of (its) reward.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Because Agni by his greatness carries the oblations and the like offered by the sacrificers to the gods, those gods, pleased with Agni and with the sacrificers, gladly partake of the immortal drink, in the form of Soma, offered in the sacrifice. And the priests, who offer the oblation on behalf of the sacrificer, attend and worship Agni, the accomplisher of the offering. This is the main intention.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न त्वद्धोता॒ पूर्वो॑ अग्ने॒ यजी॑या॒न्न काव्यैः॑ प॒रो अ॑स्ति  
> स्वधावः ।  
> वि॒शश्च॒ यस्या॒ अति॑थि॒र्भवा॑सि॒ स य॒ज्ञेन॑ वनवद्देव॒ मर्ता॑न् ॥५॥

> *na tvaddhotā pūrvo agne yajīyānna kāvyaiḥ paro asti*  
> *svadhāvaḥ |*  
> *viśaśca yasyā atithirbhavāsi sa yajñena vanavaddeva martān ‖5‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> न । त्वत् । होता । पूर्वः । अग्ने । यजीयान् । न । काव्यैः । परः । अस्ति ।  
> स्वधावः ।  
> विशः । च । यस्याः । अतिथिः । भवासि । सः । यज्ञेन । वनवत् । देव । मर्तान् ॥ ५ ॥

> *na | tvat | hotā | pūrvaḥ | agne | yajīyān | na | kāvyaiḥ | paraḥ | asti |*  
> *svadhāvaḥ |*  
> *viśaḥ | ca | yasyāḥ | atithiḥ | bhavāsi | saḥ | yajñena | vanavat | deva | martān ‖ 5 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वत्त्वत्तोऽन्यो नास्ति होता पूर्वः पूरकः पुराणो वा यजीयान्यष्टा वा । काव्यैः-स्तोत्रैः स्तुत्यः परः परस्तात्परस्मिन्नपि काले नास्ति । हे देव
> हे स्वधावोऽन्नवन् यस्या विशः प्रजाया ऋत्विग्रूपाया अतिथिर्भवासि । अतिथिवत्पूज्यो भवसि । स यज्ञेन मर्तानस्मद्वैष्टवान् वनवत् । वृश्चति । हिनस्ति । यद्वा।
> मर्तान्परिचारकान्वनवत् । संभजेत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, there is no other Hotṛ than you, whether earlier (पूर्वः (*pūrvaḥ*), or "fulfiller", or ancient) or more of a sacrificer (यजीयान् (*yajīyān*), यष्टा (*yaṣṭā*)). Nor is there, परः (*paraḥ*), anyone later, even in a later time, to be praised with hymns (काव्यैः (*kāvyaiḥ*)). O god, O स्वधावः (*svadhāvaḥ*) (possessor of food), the people (विशः (*viśaḥ*)), the priestly folk, of whom you become the guest, that is, are worshipful like a guest—that man वनवत् (*vanavat*) with the sacrifice cuts down, destroys, the mortals who are hostile to us. Or else: वनवत् (*vanavat*) means he would favour (संभजेत् (*saṃbhajet*)) the mortals, his attendants.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- त्वत् (*tvat*)—apart from you
- पूर्वः (*pūrvaḥ*)—earlier than you
- होता (*hotā*)—accomplisher of the offering
- न अस्ति (*na asti*)—there is none
- काव्यैः (*kāvyaiḥ*)—praised by hymns
- यजीयान् (*yajīyān*)—the performer of sacrifice
- परः (*paraḥ*)—anyone other than you
- न (*na*)—not
- देव (*deva*)—O Agni, of divine nature
- स्वधावः (*svadhāvaḥ*)—possessing food
- यस्या विशः (*yasyā viśaḥ*)—for which people, priests and others
- अतिथिः (*atithiḥ*)—as guest
- भवसि (*bhavasi*)—you become
- सः (*saḥ*)—such a man
- यज्ञेन (*yajñena*)—with the help of the sacrifice
- मर्तान् (*martān*)—his enemies in human form
- वनवत् (*vanavat*)—destroys

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, neither an excellent Hotṛ nor a sacrificer praised by hymns exists before you, apart from you. In future too there can be none who surpasses you. O Agni of divine nature, the man for whom you, possessing food, become a guest among priests and other people destroys, with the help of the sacrifice, his enemies in human form.
**NOTE**

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
There is no more venerable offerer of oblations, Agni, than you, nor (one) prior to you; neither, giver of food, is any one subsequent (to be more glorified by hymns): the man of whom you are the guest destroys hostile men by sacrifice.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

O Agni, among sacrificers who perform the sacrificial rite, or among priests, there is none better than you in knowledge of the respective rites and in their performance. You alone know everything. Moreover, being honoured like a guest by priests and others, you give them food and the like and destroy their enemies as a forest fire destroys a forest; or, in order to show favour to the priests and others who attend you, you go to them; this is the intention.

> हे अग्ने वयं यजमानास्वोतास्तया रक्षिताः संतो वनुयाम ।
> शत्रुन्पीडयाम संभजेमहि ना धनं ! कीदृशा वयं । वसूयवो वसुकामा
> हविषा त्वां बुध्यमाना बोधयंतो वयं समर्यॆ समरणे जयेम शत्रुनिति
> शेषः । विदथेषु यागेषु प्राप्नुयाम बलं । यद्वा । वनुयामेत्येतदनुषज्यते।
> अह्नां सर्वॆष्वहःसु । किंच वयं हे सहसस्पुत्र बलस्य पुत्र पालक वाग्ने राया
> धनेन सह मर्त्यान्पुत्रभृत्यादीन् लभेमहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Agni, we the sacrificers, protected by you (त्वोताः (*tvotāḥ*)), may we वनुयाम (*vanuyāma*), that is, may we crush our enemies and share in wealth. What kind are we? We are वसूयवः (*vasūyavaḥ*), desirous of wealth, and we awaken you with oblations. In समर्ये (*samarye*), in battle, may we conquer our enemies (the word "enemies" is to be supplied). In the विदथेषु (*vidatheṣu*), the sacrifices, may we obtain strength. Or else, the word वनुयाम (*vanuyāma*) is carried on (to the later part of the verse). अह्नां (*ahnāṃ*) means on all days. Further, O son of strength (सहसस्पुत्र (*sahasasputra*)), that is, O son or protector of strength, Agni, may we obtain together with wealth (राया (*rāyā*)) mortals, that is, sons, servants and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we, the sacrificers
- वसूयवः (*vasūyavaḥ*)—desiring wealth
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—with oblations
- बुध्यमानाः (*budhyamānāḥ*)—awakening (you)
- त्वोताः (*tvotāḥ*)—protected by you
- वनुयाम (*vanuyāma*)—may we obtain wealth
- अह्नां (*ahnāṃ*)—on all days
- विदथेषु (*vidatheṣu*)—in the sacrifices (obtaining strength)
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- समर्ये (*samarye*)—in battle (may we obtain victory)
- सहसस्पुत्र (*sahasasputra*)—O Agni, son of strength
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- राया (*rāyā*)—with wealth
- मर्तान् (*martān*)—sons, servants and the like (may we obtain)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, may we sacrificers, desirous of wealth, awakening you with oblations and protected by you, obtain wealth. May we obtain strength in the sacrifices on all days

### Printed p. 780
and may we obtain victory in battle. O Agni, son of strength, may we obtain sons, servants and the like together with wealth.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May we, desirous of wealth, Agni, and arousing you by oblations, secure in your protection, acquire (riches): may we (be victorious) in battle, (successful) in sacrifices every day ; and may we, son of strength, obtain with riches male (descendants).
